nodes.name: Nabopolassar (Founder of Neo-Babylonian Empire, 626–605 BCE)
nodes.notes: Founded the Chaldean Empire and allied with Media to conquer Nineveh (612 BCE); father of Nebuchadnezzar II.

nodes.name: Amel-Marduk / Evil-Merodach (Son of Nebuchadnezzar II, 562–560 BCE; 2 Kgs 25:27)
nodes.notes: Son of Nebuchadnezzar II; released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison in Babylon.

nodes.name: Neriglissar / Nergal-sharezer (Son-in-Law of Nebuchadnezzar II, 560–556 BCE)
nodes.notes: Married Nebuchadnezzar II's daughter Kashshaya; seized the throne from Amel-Marduk.

nodes.name: Labashi-Marduk (Son of Neriglissar, 556 BCE)
nodes.notes: Young son of Neriglissar deposed after nine months by the Nabonidus conspiracy.

nodes.name: King Nabonidus (Son of Nabu-balatsu-iqbi & Adad-guppi, 556–539 BCE)
nodes.notes: Resided 10 years at Tayma in Arabia while entrusting Babylon to his eldest son Belshazzar.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Belshazzar (Son & Coregent of Nabonidus, Daniel 5)
nodes.role: Babylonian Crown Prince at the Fall of Babylon
nodes.notes: Coregent of Babylon under Nabonidus until the city fell to Cyrus the Great in 539 BCE.

nodes.name: Manetho's Divine & Shemsu-Hor Horizon (Pre-Menes Era)
nodes.era: Predynastic Mythic Era (Manetho Fr. 1-4, Loeb pp. 3-19)
nodes.notes: Manetho's opening divine & demigod kingship sequence preceding Menes: Ptah -> Re -> Shu -> Geb -> Osiris -> Seth -> Horus -> 9 Demigods -> Shemsu-Hor ('Spirits of the Dead').

nodes.name: King Scorpion I/II & Palermo Stone Lower Egypt Kings (Dynasty 0)
nodes.role: Earliest Historically Inscribed Rulers of the Nile Before Narmer
nodes.notes: Pre-Unification Red Crown kings preserved on Row 1 of the Palermo Stone (Seka, Khayu, Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazner, Mekh) alongside Upper Egyptian Dynasty 0 rulers Iry-Hor, Ka & King Scorpion.

nodes.name: Dynasty I Horizon (Thinite, 8 Kings, c. 2982–2803 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 179 historical years (Manetho: 253 yrs); Africanus makes every king son of his predecessor.

nodes.name: Dynasty II Horizon (9 Kings, c. 2803–2657 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Under Nynetjer (Binothris) it was decreed women could hold royal dignity.

nodes.name: Dynasty III Horizon (Memphite Step Pyramid Era, c. 2657–2589 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Djoser & Imhotep built the Saqqara Step Pyramid; Huni inaugurated the royal cartouche.

nodes.name: Dynasty IV Horizon (Giza Great Pyramid Builders, c. 2589–2454 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sneferu, Khufu, Djedefre, Khafre, Baka, Menkaure, Shepseskaf & Queen Khentkawes.

nodes.name: Dynasty V Horizon (Solar Kings & Pyramid Texts, c. 2454–2297 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Palermo Stone Annals compiled under Userkaf; oldest Pyramid Texts inscribed under Unas.

nodes.name: Dynasty VI Horizon (Memphite Old Kingdom Finale, c. 2297–2168 BCE)
nodes.role: Era of Pepi II & Queen Nitocris
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Concludes the Old Kingdom with 94-year reign of Pepi II and Queen Nitocris.

nodes.name: First Intermediate Period (Dynasties VII–X, Khety/Achthoes & Merikare)
nodes.era: c. 2168-2040 BCE (Manetho Fr. 23-30; Breasted Vol. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Khety / Achthoes of Heracleopolis (Teaching for King Merikare).

nodes.name: Dynasty XI Horizon (Theban Middle Kingdom Unifiers, c. 2160–2000 BCE)
nodes.era: c. 2160-2000 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §63; Manetho Fr. 31-32)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Intef I–III and Mentuhotep II–IV reunified Upper & Lower Egypt.

nodes.name: Dynasty XII Horizon (Middle Kingdom Golden Age, 2000–1788 BCE)
nodes.role: Classical Peak of Egyptian Literature & Labyrinth
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves direct parent-child succession through Queen Sobekneferu (Scemiophris).

nodes.name: Dynasties XIII–XIV Horizon (Second Intermediate Period)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sobekhotep IV (Chenephres in Artapanus) and Dedumose (Tutimaeus).

nodes.name: Dynasties XV–XVII Horizon (Great Hyksos & Theban Liberation)
nodes.era: c. 1650-1550 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42-49 via Josephus Against Apion)
nodes.role: Hyksos Rulers of Avaris & Theban Liberators
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Josephus (quoting Manetho verbatim) preserved the 6 Great Hyksos rulers until Seqenenre & Kamose launched liberation.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Horizon (Thutmoside Empire, 1550–1391 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ahmose I through Hatshepsut, Thutmose III & Thutmose IV.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Late Horizon (Amarna & Harmais/Danaus Transition)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho Fr. 50/53 identifies Horemheb ('Harmais') = Danaus & Ramesses/Seti = Aegyptus.

nodes.name: Dynasty XIX Horizon (Ramesside & Trojan War Synchronism)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Queen Twosret ('Thuoris') Troy was taken.

nodes.name: Dynasty XX Horizon (Ramesside II & Sea Peoples Defense)
nodes.era: 1189-1077 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 1-20; Manetho Fr. 57)
nodes.role: Ten Sons of Ramesses III to High Priest Herihor
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Concludes the New Kingdom down to Ramesses XI.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXI Horizon (Tanite Pharaohs & Theban Priest-Kings)
nodes.era: 1077-943 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 20-34; Manetho Fr. 58-59)
nodes.role: Divided Egypt (Biblical Era of David & Solomon)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Siamun & Psusennes II in Tanis alongside High Priests Herihor to Pinudjem II at Thebes.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXII Horizon (Libyan Bubastite — Stele of Pasenhor)
nodes.era: 943-716 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 35-60; Manetho Fr. 60-61)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor traces Shoshenq I back 6 generations to Buyuwawa and forward to Shoshenq V.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXIII–XXIV Horizon (Delta Coalitions & Bocchoris)
nodes.era: 818-715 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 60-69; Manetho Fr. 62-65)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Pedubast I, Osorkon III, Tefnakht I & lawgiver Bakenranef (Bocchoris).

nodes.name: Dynasty XXV Horizon (Kushite Pharaohs & God's Wives Amenirdis/Shepenupet)
nodes.era: 744-656 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 70-78, 195-199; Manetho Fr. 66-67)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Unifies Kushite royal family with 26th Dynasty Saite succession.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXVI Horizon (Saite Renaissance, 664–525 BCE)
nodes.era: 664-525 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 78-90; Manetho Fr. 68-69; Jer 44:30)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Psamtik I, Necho II, Psamtik II, Apries (Hophra), Amasis II & Psamtik III.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXVII–XXXI Horizon (Persian Conquests & Last Native Pharaohs)
nodes.era: 525-332 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 91-106; Manetho Fr. 70-75)
nodes.role: Native Resistance Through Nectanebo II to Alexander (332 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Amyrtaeus, Nepherites I, Hakor, Nectanebo I, Teos & Nectanebo II.

nodes.name: Ptolemaic Dynasty Horizon (Alexandria, 305–30 BCE)
nodes.role: Macedonian-Greek Pharaohs of Alexandria (Septuagint & Rosetta Stone)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: All 15 Ptolemies & 7 Cleopatras down to Cleopatra VII & Ptolemy XV Caesarion.

nodes.name: Napatan Kingdom of Kush Horizon (c. 653–315 BCE)
nodes.role: Post-25th Dynasty Nubian Pyramid Builders of Nuri
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 199-205)
nodes.notes: Napatan succession at Nuri & Jebel Barkal from Atlanersa through Nastasen.

nodes.name: Meroitic Kingdom Horizon (c. 270 BCE – 50 CE)
nodes.era: c. 270 BCE – 50 CE (Budge Vol. II pp. 205-214; Diodorus III.6; Acts 8:27)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 205-214)
nodes.notes: Meroitic monarchs from Arqamani (Ergamenes) to Natakamani & Kandake Amanitore.

nodes.name: Djer / Kenkenes (Dyn. I, 47 yrs)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Hor-Aha; tomb at Abydos.

nodes.name: Djet / Uenephes (Dyn. I, 13 yrs)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Djer; wed Queen Merneith.

nodes.name: Queen Merneith (Regent of Dyn. I; Mother of Den)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Consort of Djet and mother-regent for young King Den; buried with royal honors at Abydos.

nodes.name: Adjib / Miebis (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Den.

nodes.name: Semerkhet / Semempses (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 7th king of the Thinite First Dynasty.

nodes.name: Qa'a / Bieneches (Dyn. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Last king buried in the Abydos Umm el-Qa'ab royal necropolis.

nodes.name: Hotepsekhemwy / Boethos (Dyn. II Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Moved royal tombs to Saqqara.

nodes.name: Nebre / Kaiechos (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First pharaoh to incorporate Ra into his royal name.

nodes.name: Nynetjer / Binothris (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho records that in his reign women were declared eligible to hold royal dignity.

nodes.name: Weneg / Tlas (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Mid-2nd Dynasty Memphite ruler.

nodes.name: Sened / Sethenes (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Revered in Memphite funerary cults.

nodes.name: Seth-Peribsen (Dyn. II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Took a Seth-name above his Abydos serekh before Khasekhemwy reconciled Horus and Seth.

nodes.name: Sanakht / Necherophes (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Elder brother/predecessor of Djoser; buried at Beit Khallaf.

nodes.name: Sekhemkhet / Tyris (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Builder of the Buried Pyramid at Saqqara.

nodes.name: Khaba (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Builder of the Layer Pyramid at Zawyet el-Aryan.

nodes.name: Huni / Kerpheres (Dyn. III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Hetepheres I and builder of Meidum.

nodes.name: Djedefre / Ratoises (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Khufu; built pyramid at Abu Rawash and first took 'Son of Ra' title.

nodes.name: Baka / Bicheris (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho's Bicheris placed amid Khufu's sons.

nodes.name: Shepseskaf (Dyn. IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built Mastabat el-Fir'aun at South Saqqara.

nodes.name: Queen Khentkawes I (Dyn. IV/V Bridge; 'Mother of Two Kings')
nodes.role: Daughter of Menkaure & Mother of Dyn. V
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Monument at Giza calls her 'King of Upper and Lower Egypt' and mother of Userkaf/Sahure.

nodes.name: Userkaf / Usercheres (Dyn. V Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built the first solar temple at Abusir; Palermo Stone annals era.

nodes.name: Sahure / Sephres (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Dispatched first attested Egyptian maritime expedition to Punt.

nodes.name: Neferirkare Kakai (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Honored in the Abusir Papyri.

nodes.name: Shepseskare (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief Abusir ruler.

nodes.name: Neferefre (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Elder son of Neferirkare.

nodes.name: Nyuserre Ini (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built solar temple at Abu Gorab.

nodes.name: Menkauhor (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Seventh king of Dynasty V.

nodes.name: Djedkare Isesi (Dyn. V)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Era of Vizier Ptahhotep's Maxims.

nodes.name: Unas / Onnus (Last of Dyn. V — Pyramid Texts!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First ruler to carve the sacred Pyramid Texts inside his Saqqara tomb.

nodes.name: Teti / Othoes (Dyn. VI Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Princess Iput daughter of Unas.

nodes.name: Userkare (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief ruler between Teti and Pepi I.

nodes.name: Pepi I / Phius (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded trade to Byblos & Nubia; father of Merenre I & Pepi II.

nodes.name: Merenre I (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Received Nubian chiefs' homage at Elephantine.

nodes.name: Pepi II / Phiops (Dyn. VI — 94-Year Reign!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ascended at age 6 and ruled into his 90s (Manetho: 94 yrs).

nodes.name: Merenre II Nemtyemsaf (Dyn. VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brief successor of aged Pepi II.

nodes.name: Queen Nitocris / Neith-iqerty (Close of Old Kingdom, Dyn. VI)
nodes.role: Last Sovereign of the Old Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Described by Manetho as 'the noblest and loveliest of the women of her time' who built the third pyramid tradition.

nodes.name: Intef I (Theban Dyn. XI Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: First Theban ruler to take a Horus name Sehertawy.

nodes.name: Intef II Wahankh (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Pushed Theban power north to Abydos over 49-year reign.

nodes.name: Intef III (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of unifier Mentuhotep II.

nodes.name: Mentuhotep III Sankhkare (Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sent Hannu on Red Sea expedition to Punt.

nodes.name: Mentuhotep IV Nebtawyre (Last of Dyn. XI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Vizier Amenemhat (future Amenemhat I) led his Wadi Hammamat quarry expedition.

nodes.name: Amenemhat I (Dyn. XII Founder)
nodes.era: c. 1985–1955 BCE (Manetho Fr. 34; Breasted Vol. I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Founded Itjtawy; father of Senusret I.

nodes.name: Senusret I / Sesonchosis (Dyn. XII)
nodes.era: c. 1955–1911 BCE (Manetho Fr. 35; Story of Sinuhe)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built White Chapel at Karnak; era of Story of Sinuhe.

nodes.name: Amenemhat II (Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded Near Eastern & Nubian trade.

nodes.name: Senusret II (Dyn. XII; Beni Hasan Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Faiyum irrigation pioneer; Beni Hasan tomb painting of Semitic caravan of Abishai.

nodes.name: Amenemhat IV (Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Reigned 9 years before sister Sobekneferu.

nodes.name: Queen Sobekneferu / Scemiophris (First Attested Female Pharaoh, Dyn. XII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sister of Amenemhat IV; Manetho explicitly notes Scemiophris 'reigned for 4 years' closing the 12th Dynasty.

nodes.name: Sobekhotep IV / Chenephres (Dyn. XIII; Artapanus's Moses Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Identified in Waddell's Manetho notes with Artapanus's Pharaoh Chenephres.

nodes.name: Dedumose / Tutimaeus (Late Dyn. XIII; Manetho Hyksos Entry)
nodes.era: c. 1660 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42 via Josephus Ag. Ap. I.14)
nodes.role: Pharaoh Under Whom Hyksos Entered Egypt
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Named by Josephus quoting Manetho as Tutimaeus, when easterners seized Memphis without battle.

nodes.name: Salitis (1st Great Hyksos King of Avaris, Dyn. XV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Avaris in the Eastern Delta.

nodes.name: Khyan / Iannas (Great Hyksos King, Dyn. XV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Inscribed artifacts found from Knossos to Hattusa and Baghdad.

nodes.name: Apophis / Apepi (Hyksos King, Dyn. XV; Traditional Pharaoh of Joseph)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Synchronized by George Syncellus as Pharaoh of Joseph; clashed with Seqenenre Tao.

nodes.name: Kamose (Last King of Dyn. XVII; Liberator Before Ahmose I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Drove Hyksos back to Avaris; succeeded by younger brother Ahmose I.

nodes.name: Amenhotep I (Son of Ahmose I; Deir el-Medina Founder, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Consolidated Nubia and founded the royal artisans' village.

nodes.name: Thutmose II (Son of Thutmose I; Husband of Hatshepsut, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Thutmose III.

nodes.name: Queen Hatshepsut / Amessis (Regnant Female Pharaoh, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Built Deir el-Bahari and dispatched fleet to Punt; co-regent with stepson Thutmose III.

nodes.name: Amenhotep II (Son of Thutmose III; Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Renowned archer-king who campaigned in Canaan.

nodes.name: Thutmose IV (Dream Stele Pharaoh; Father of Amenhotep III, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Mitanni princess and restored Great Sphinx.

nodes.name: Queen Tiye (Wife of Amenhotep III; Mother of Akhenaten)
nodes.role: Great Royal Wife of Amenhotep III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yuya & Tjuyu; mother of Akhenaten.

nodes.name: Queen Nefertiti (Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten)
nodes.role: Queen of Amarna & Mother-in-Law of Tutankhamun
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Bore six princesses incl. Ankhesenamun (wife of Tutankhamun).

nodes.name: Smenkhkare / Neferneferuaten (Amarna Co-Regent, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Married Meritaten.

nodes.name: Pharaoh Ay (Successor of Tutankhamun, Dyn. XVIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Former vizier & God's Father who buried Tutankhamun.

nodes.name: Horemheb / Harmais = Danaus (Manetho Fr. 50/53; Dyn. XVIII)
nodes.role: Final King of Dyn. XVIII Synchronized With Danaus
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho explicitly equates Horemheb ('Harmais') fleeing Egypt to Argos with Greek King Danaus!

nodes.name: Ramesses I (Dyn. XIX Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Vizier Paramesse designated heir by Horemheb.

nodes.name: Seti I / Sethos (Father of Ramesses II; Manetho's Aegyptus!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho equates Sethos with Aegyptus, brother of Harmais/Danaus; carved the Abydos King List.

nodes.name: Amenmesse (Dyn. XIX Rival)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Reigned in Upper Egypt during Seti II's early years.

nodes.name: Seti II (Son of Merneptah; Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Husband of Queen Twosret.

nodes.name: Siptah (Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled six years under stepmother Queen Twosret's regency.

nodes.name: Queen Twosret / Thuoris (Manetho's Trojan War Synchronism, Dyn. XIX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho states Troy was taken during the reign of Thuoris (identified with Homer's Polybus/Alcandra).

nodes.name: Setnakhte (Dyn. XX Founder; Father of Ramesses III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Restored order and fathered Ramesses III.

nodes.name: Ramesses IV (Son of Ramesses III; Papyrus Harris I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Commissioned Great Harris Papyrus.

nodes.name: Ramesses V (Son of Ramesses IV)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Turin Papyrus era.

nodes.name: Ramesses VI (Son of Ramesses III)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Brother of Ramesses IV.

nodes.name: Ramesses VII (Son of Ramesses VI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Short Valley of the Kings reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses VIII (Son of Ramesses III)
nodes.role: Last Surviving Son of Ramesses III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: One-year reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses IX (Dyn. XX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 18-year reign.

nodes.name: Ramesses X (Dyn. XX)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Predecessor of Ramesses XI.

nodes.name: Ramesses XI (Final Ramesside Pharaoh, Dyn. XX)
nodes.role: Last Pharaoh of Dynasty XX & New Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Saw Rise of High Priest Herihor at Thebes & Smendes at Tanis (Report of Wenamun).

nodes.name: Herihor (High Priest of Amun & Ruler at Thebes)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Assumed royal titles in Upper Egypt alongside Smendes in the Delta.

nodes.name: Piankh (High Priest of Amun)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Pinudjem I.

nodes.name: Pinudjem I (Theban Priest-King)
nodes.role: High Priest & Father of Psusennes I
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Wed Duathathor-Henuttawy (daughter of Ramesses XI!); father of Psusennes I & Menkheperre.

nodes.name: Menkheperre (High Priest of Amun)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Upper Egypt; father of Pinudjem II.

nodes.name: Pinudjem II (High Priest of Amun; Royal Cache Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fathered Psusennes II and preserved the New Kingdom royal mummies in DB320.

nodes.name: Smendes I (Dyn. XXI Founder at Tanis)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled Lower Egypt during Wenamun's mission to Byblos.

nodes.name: Psusennes I (Silver Pharaoh of Tanis, Dyn. XXI)
nodes.role: Son of Pinudjem I; King of Tanis
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Intact silver-coffin royal tomb excavated at Tanis.

nodes.name: Amenemope (Dyn. XXI; Contemporary of David)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ruled Tanis during David's monarchy.

nodes.name: Siamun (Dyn. XXI — Era of King Solomon & Gezer)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Synchronized with early reign of King Solomon (cf. 1 Kgs 3:1, 9:16).

nodes.name: Psusennes II (Last of Dyn. XXI; Father-in-Law of Osorkon I)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Pinudjem II; daughter Maatkare married Osorkon I of Dyn. XXII.

nodes.name: Buyuwawa the Libyan (6-Gen Ancestor, Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Founder of the Meshwesh lineage recorded on the Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor.

nodes.name: Osorkon I (Son of Shoshenq I & Karamat; Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Shoshenq I; wed Maatkare (daughter of Psusennes II).

nodes.name: Takelot I (Son of Osorkon I, Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Osorkon II.

nodes.name: Osorkon II (Son of Takelot I, Dyn. XXII)
nodes.role: Ally of Ahab & Levant Coalition (853 BCE Battle of Qarqar Era)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Sent Egyptian contingent noted with Ahab in Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith.

nodes.name: Shoshenq II (Silver Falcon Coffin, Tanis, Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Co-regent buried at Tanis.

nodes.name: Takelot II (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Chronicle of Prince Osorkon.

nodes.name: Shoshenq III (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: 39-year reign at Tanis.

nodes.name: Pami (Dyn. XXII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Shoshenq V.

nodes.name: Shoshenq V (Dyn. XXII; Pasenhor Stele Erected in Year 37!)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Priestly Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor dated to his 37th regnal year.

nodes.name: Pedubast I (Dyn. XXIII Founder)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Rival Theban-Leontopolitan king during Shoshenq III.

nodes.name: Osorkon III (Dyn. XXIII)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Takelot III & Shepenupet I.

nodes.name: Tefnakht I of Sais (Dyn. XXIV Founder vs. Piye)
nodes.era: 732–725 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.68; Victory Stele)
nodes.role: Chief of Sais & Dynasty XXIV Founder
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fought Kushite King Piye (Piankhi Stele); father of Bocchoris.

nodes.name: Bakenranef / Bocchoris (Dyn. XXIV Lawgiver)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Defeated by Kushite Shabaka when uniting Egypt under Dynasty XXV.

nodes.name: Shabaka / Sabacon (Dyn. XXV Pharaoh)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Kashta; defeated Bocchoris and unified all Egypt.

nodes.name: Shabataka / Sebichos (Dyn. XXV Pharaoh)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Dispatched young Prince Taharqa northward to relieve Hezekiah.

nodes.name: Psamtik I (Dyn. XXVI Reunifier, 54-Year Reign!)
nodes.era: 664–610 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.79; Herodotus II)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Son of Necho I of Sais; unified Egypt & expelled Assyrians; father of Necho II.

nodes.name: Psamtik II (Son of Necho II, Dyn. XXVI)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led 593 BCE Napatan expedition.

nodes.name: Apries / Biblical Pharaoh Hophra (Dyn. XXVI, Jer 44:30)
nodes.role: Son of Psamtik II; Sheltered Prophet Jeremiah
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Marched against Nebuchadnezzar II during 588 BCE siege of Jerusalem (Jer 37:5).

nodes.name: Amasis II / Ahmose II (Dyn. XXVI, 44-Year Reign!)
nodes.era: 570–526 BCE (Herodotus II.162; Budge Vol. II p.86)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Promoted Greek Naucratis trade & allied with Croesus of Lydia.

nodes.name: Psamtik III (Last Native Saite King, 525 BCE)
nodes.role: Defeated at Pelusium by Cambyses II
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fell to Persian conquest in 525 BCE.

nodes.name: Amyrtaeus of Sais (Sole King of Dyn. XXVIII, 404–399 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led native Egyptian revolt freeing Egypt from Darius II.

nodes.name: Nepherites I (Founder of Mendes Dyn. XXIX, 399–393 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Allied with King Agesilaus II of Sparta against Persia.

nodes.name: Hakor / Achoris (Dyn. XXIX, 393–380 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Repelled Persian invasion with Greek mercenaries.

nodes.name: Nectanebo I / Nakhtnebef (Founder of Dyn. XXX, 380–362 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Fortified Delta & built Philae/Karnak pylons.

nodes.name: Teos / Tachos (Dyn. XXX, 362–360 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Led joint Greco-Egyptian campaign into Phoenicia.

nodes.name: Nectanebo II / Nakhthorheb (LAST Native Pharaoh of Egypt, 360–343 BCE)
nodes.era: 360–343 BCE (Manetho Fr. 74; Budge Vol. II p.104)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Nephew of Teos; deposed by Artaxerxes III in 343 BCE (Alexander Romance calls him Alexander's secret father!).

nodes.name: Ptolemy I Soter (+ Berenice I, 305–282 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: General of Alexander; built Alexandria & Library; father of Ptolemy II.

nodes.name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus (+ Arsinoe II; Sponsored Septuagint, 282–246 BCE)
nodes.era: 282–246 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.114; Letter of Aristeas)
nodes.role: Patron of Manetho & Septuagint Torah Translation
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Expanded Library of Alexandria and commissioned High Priest Eleazar's 72 translators.

nodes.name: Ptolemy III Euergetes (+ Berenice II, 246–222 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Canopus Decree.

nodes.name: Ptolemy IV Philopator (+ Arsinoe III, 222–204 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Victor of Raphia (217 BCE) over Antiochus III.

nodes.name: Ptolemy V Epiphanes (+ Cleopatra I Syra; Rosetta Stone, 204–180 BCE)
nodes.era: 204–180 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.126; Memphis Decree)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Issued the trilingual Rosetta Stone (196 BCE) and wed Seleucid Princess Cleopatra I Syra.

nodes.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor (+ Cleopatra II; Patron of Onias IV, 180–145 BCE)
nodes.era: 180–145 BCE (Budge Vol. II p.129; Josephus Ant. XIII.3)
nodes.role: Elder Son of Ptolemy V & Cleopatra I Syra
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Granted Leontopolis to Jewish High Priest Onias IV.

nodes.name: Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II Physcon (+ Cleopatra III, 170–116 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Cleopatra VII.

nodes.name: Ptolemy IX Soter II Lathyros (116–81 BCE)
nodes.role: Son of Ptolemy VIII & Cleopatra III
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Ptolemy XII Auletes.

nodes.name: Ptolemy X Alexander I (+ Berenice III, 107–88 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Co-regent & uncle of Ptolemy XII.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XII Auletes (Father of Cleopatra VII, 80–51 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Father of Cleopatra VII, Berenice IV, Arsinoe IV, Ptolemy XIII & Ptolemy XIV.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XV Caesarion (Son of Cleopatra VII & Julius Caesar, d. 30 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of Kings Vol. II
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Cleopatra VII by Julius Caesar; slain after Actium.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XIII Theos Philopator (Son of Ptolemy XII, d. 47 BCE)
nodes.notes: Drowned in the Nile during the Alexandrian War.

nodes.name: Ptolemy XIV (Younger Brother of Cleopatra VII, d. 44 BCE)
nodes.notes: Nominal co-ruler alongside Cleopatra VII.

nodes.name: Atlanersa of Napata (Son of Taharqa / Tantamani Era)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Buried at Nuri.

nodes.name: Senkamanisken of Napata
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Father of Anlamani & Aspelta.

nodes.name: Anlamani of Napata
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Crowned at Kawa; elder brother of Aspelta.

nodes.name: Aspelta (Moved Kushite Capital South to Meroe, c. 593 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Resisted Psamtik II's 593 BCE expedition and transferred center to Meroe.

nodes.name: Harsiotef of Kush
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Stele of 35 regnal years.

nodes.name: Nastasen of Kush (Last Great Napatan Tomb at Nuri)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Defended Nubia against Khababash era forces.

nodes.name: Arqamani / King Ergamenes of Meroe (Friend of Ptolemy II & IV)
nodes.era: c. 270–220 BCE (Diodorus III.6; Budge Vol. II)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Greek-educated Meroitic king mentioned by Diodorus Siculus.

nodes.name: King Natakamani of Meroe (Husband of Kandake Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Co-ruler with Kandake Queen Amanitore during Meroe's architectural zenith.

nodes.name: Queen Amanitore (Kandake / Biblical 'Candace' Era)
nodes.era: c. 1–20 CE (Budge Vol. II p.214; Acts 8:27)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Built Lion Temple at Naqa & restored Amun temple at Meroe; maternal figure of Acts 8:27 'Candace' dynasty.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Arikhankharer (Son of Natakamani & Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Depicted with Natakamani & Amanitore at Naqa.

nodes.name: King Shorkaror (Son of Natakamani & Amanitore)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp.195–214)
nodes.notes: Inscribed victory relief at Jebel Qeili.

nodes.name: Targamos / Togarmah (Patriarch of All Caucasian Nations, Kartlis Tskhovreba)
nodes.era: Caucasian Table of Nations (Kartlis Tskhovreba pp. 13-18)
nodes.role: Patriarchal Origin of All Peoples of the Caucasus
nodes.notes: Targamos (Togarmah, lived 600 yrs between Mt. Ararat & Masis) divided the Caucasus among 8 sons (Haos, Kartlos, Bardos, Movak'an, Lek', Heros, K'avk'as, Egros) + Uobos.

nodes.name: Kartlos's Proto-Georgian Branch Anchor (Mtskhetos to Uplos)
nodes.role: Founders of Mtskheta, Kakheti, Gardabani, Uplistsikhe & Javakheti Anchor
nodes.notes: Bridge from Kartlos's sons Mtskhetos and Uplos down to King Parnavaz I of Kartli.

nodes.name: Kings of Iberia / Kartli Anchor (Pharnavazids, Nebrotids & Arshak'ids)
nodes.role: First Royal Dynasties of Georgia & Creator of Georgian Script Anchor
nodes.notes: Anchor linking Parnavaz I through Mirvan I (Nebrotid), Arshak' I, Parsman, and Aspagur to Abeshuru.

nodes.name: Chosroid (Mihranid-Sasanian) Dynasty Anchor (Mirian III to Vakht'ang Gorgasali)
nodes.role: Christianizers of Georgia & Founder of Tbilisi Anchor
nodes.notes: Mirian III (Mikhran, Sasanian prince + Abeshuru + St. Nino) -> Bakar -> Archil -> Vakht'ang I Gorgasali -> Dachi.

nodes.name: Bagrat'ioni Royal House Anchor (Sumbat Davitisdze Davidic Claim)
nodes.role: Longest-Reigning Christian Royal House (Davidic Claim Anchor)
nodes.notes: Unrolled person-by-person below from Bagrat' and Guaram I through Ashot' I, Bagrat' III, David IV, and Queen Tamar.

nodes.name: Parthian / Ashkanian Empire Anchor (Al-Biruni -> Kayanian Siyavush)
nodes.era: 247 BCE - 224 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 116-120; Betham Tab. CV)
nodes.role: 470-Year Iranian Superpower Bridged to Kayanian Siyavush
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 116) traces Ashk ben Ashkan (Arsaces I) directly back to Kayanian Prince Siyavush; unrolled individually in Wave 4.

nodes.name: Sasanian Empire Anchor (Al-Biruni Pedigree from Kay Bahman & Esfandiyar)
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 122) traces Ardashir I -> Babak -> Sasan -> Bahman -> Isfandiyar; unrolled person-by-person below.

nodes.name: Afrighid Shahs of Khwarazm Anchor (22 Generations in Al-Biruni)
nodes.role: Al-Biruni's Homeland Dynasty — 22 Unbroken Generations Anchor
nodes.notes: 22 unbroken father-to-son Khwarazmshahs from Afrigh (305 CE) to Abu 'Abdallah Muhammad (d. 995 CE), chained individually below.

nodes.name: Pre-Islamic Arab Kingdoms Anchor (Himyarite Tubbas, Lakhmids & Ghassanids)
nodes.era: c. 110 BCE - 636 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 40-50, 311, 384; Kebra Nagast Ch. 117)
nodes.role: Qahtanite / South Arabian & Syro-Mesopotamian Arab Monarchies Anchor
nodes.notes: Himyarite Tubbas, Lakhmid kings of Al-Hirah, and Christian Ghassanid kings of Syria.

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast Royal Court & Pre-Makeda Kings Anchor
nodes.era: c. 960 BCE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 22-48, Intro p. xxxv)
nodes.role: Bearers of the Ark of Zion from Jerusalem to Aksum Anchor
sources: Kebra Nagast (Budge 1922 Intro p. xxxv, Ch. 22-48, p. 62)
nodes.notes: 5 pre-Makeda kings, Merchant Tamrin, and High Priest 'Azaryas (son of Zadok) + 21 Israelite firstborn nobles.

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast World-Kingdoms Bridge ('Adrami, Fares & 'Akamhel)
nodes.role: Ethiopic Universal Bridge of Rome, Persia & Philistia to Israel
nodes.notes: Solomon's youngest son 'Adrami marries 'Adlonya to rule Rome; Perez (Fares) -> Persia; Samson + Delilah -> 'Akamhel.

nodes.name: Aksumite & Solomonic Restoration Anchor (King Kaleb -> Gabra Maskal -> Yekuno 'Amlak)
nodes.era: c. 520-1285 CE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 117 & Colophon, Budge pp. 225-229)
nodes.notes: King Kaleb defeated Himyarite Dhu-Nuwas in Yemen (525 CE); restored under Yekuno 'Amlak in 1270 CE.

nodes.name: Haos / Hayk (Eldest Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Armenians)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Haos / Hayk (Eldest Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Armenians).

nodes.name: Kartlos (2nd Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Georgians)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Kartlos (2nd Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Georgians).

nodes.name: Bardos (Son of Targamos; Founder of Barda)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Bardos (Son of Targamos; Founder of Barda).

nodes.name: Movak'an (Son of Targamos; Founder of Movak'neti / Albania)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Movak'an (Son of Targamos; Founder of Movak'neti / Albania).

nodes.name: Lek' (Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Lezgins / Dagestan)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Lek' (Son of Targamos; Progenitor of Lezgins / Dagestan).

nodes.name: Heros (Son of Targamos; Founder of Hereti)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Heros (Son of Targamos; Founder of Hereti).

nodes.name: K'avk'as (Son of Targamos; Progenitor of North Caucasians)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: K'avk'as (Son of Targamos; Progenitor of North Caucasians).

nodes.name: Durdzuk' (Renowned Son of K'avk'as; Eponym of Vainakhs)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Durdzuk' (Renowned Son of K'avk'as; Eponym of Vainakhs).

nodes.name: Egros (Son of Targamos; Founder of Egrisi / Colchis)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Egros (Son of Targamos; Founder of Egrisi / Colchis).

nodes.name: Uobos (Khazar-Targamosid Ancestor of Ossetians)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Uobos (Khazar-Targamosid Ancestor of Ossetians).

nodes.name: Mtskhetos (Eldest Son of Kartlos; Founder of Mtskheta)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Mtskhetos (Eldest Son of Kartlos; Founder of Mtskheta).

nodes.name: Uplos (Eldest Son of Mtskhetos; Builder of Uplistsikhe)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Uplos (Eldest Son of Mtskhetos; Builder of Uplistsikhe).

nodes.name: Odzrkhos (Son of Mtskhetos; Eponym of Odzrkhe)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Odzrkhos (Son of Mtskhetos; Eponym of Odzrkhe).

nodes.name: Javakhos (Son of Mtskhetos; Eponym of Javakheti)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Javakhos (Son of Mtskhetos; Eponym of Javakheti).

nodes.name: Gardabos (Son of Kartlos; Eponym of Gardabani)
nodes.notes: Caucasian chronicle ancestor: Gardabos (Son of Kartlos; Eponym of Gardabani).

nodes.name: Pontus, Phorcys, Ceto & Nereus (Greek Sea Cosmogony)
nodes.notes: Pontus + Gaia -> Phorcys & Ceto (-> Graiae & Gorgon Medusa) and Nereus + Doris -> 50 Nereids (including Thetis, mother of Achilles).

nodes.name: Hyperion, Coeus, Crius & Titan House (Hesiod / Apollodorus I.ii)
nodes.notes: Unites Hyperion/Theia (-> Helios, Selene, Eos), Coeus/Phoebe (-> Leto, Asteria), and Crius (-> Perses -> Hecate).

nodes.name: Calliope & the Nine Muses (Zeus + Mnemosyne, Hesiod Theog. 53–920)
nodes.notes: Calliope (+ Oeagrus/Apollo) -> Orpheus & Linus; Zeus + Themis -> Horae & Fates.

nodes.name: Calyce (Daughter of Aeolus; Ancestress of Aetolia, Apollodorus I.vii.5)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Aeolus who bore Endymion -> Aetolus -> Oeneus -> Meleager, Deianira & Tydeus -> Diomedes.

nodes.name: Enipeus / Tyro Pylos-Iolcus Lineage Anchor (Apollodorus I.ix.8)
nodes.notes: Salmoneus's daughter Tyro bore Pelias of Iolcus and Neleus of Pylos (-> wise King Nestor).

nodes.name: Cretheid House of Iolcus & Argonauts Anchor (Apollodorus I.ix.11–28)
nodes.notes: Cretheus's sons Aeson (-> Jason), Pheres (-> Admetus), and Amythaon (-> Melampus & Bias -> Adrastus).

nodes.name: Glaucus of Corinth (Son of Sisyphus; Father of Bellerophon, Apollodorus I.ix.3)
nodes.notes: Son of Sisyphus & Merope; father of Bellerophon.

nodes.name: Danaid Survival Line Anchor (Hypermnestra & Lynceus, Apollodorus II.i.5)
nodes.notes: Hypermnestra spared Lynceus, continuing the Argive royal stem to Abas -> Acrisius & Proetus.

nodes.name: Perseid Royal Line Anchor (Mycenae & Tiryns, Apollodorus II.iv.5)
nodes.notes: Connects Perseus & Andromeda to Alcaeus, Sthenelus, and Electryon (-> Alcmene -> Heracles).

nodes.name: Heraclid Cleodaeus → Aristomachus (Return of the Heraclidae Anchor, c. 1104 BCE)
nodes.role: Dorian Conquest & Return of the Heraclidae
nodes.notes: Hyllus's son Cleodaeus -> Aristomachus, whose sons Temenus (Argos), Cresphontes (Messene) & Aristodemus (Sparta) led the Dorian return.

nodes.name: Cretan House of Minos Anchor (Catreus & Deucalion, Apollodorus III.i–iii)
nodes.role: Cretan Royal Bridge to Atreids & Athens
nodes.notes: Minos + Pasiphae -> Catreus (-> Aerope), Deucalion (-> Idomeneus), Ariadne, and Phaedra.

nodes.name: Cadmean Labdacid House of Thebes Anchor (Apollodorus III.iv–vii)
nodes.notes: Cadmus & Harmonia -> Semele (-> Dionysus), Illyrius, and Polydorus -> Labdacus -> Laius -> Oedipus -> Eteocles, Polynices, Antigone.

nodes.name: Aleus & Auge of Arcadia (Ancestors of Telephus of Mysia, Apollodorus III.ix)
nodes.role: Arcadian Pelasgid Bridge to Heracles & Mysia
nodes.notes: Arcas -> Aleus -> Princess Auge (+ Heracles -> King Telephus of Mysia).

nodes.name: Pleiades Maia & Taygete (Ancestresses of Hermes & Sparta, Apollodorus III.x)
nodes.notes: Daughters of Atlas & Pleione: Maia -> Hermes; Taygete -> Lacedaemon -> Tyndareus & Icarius.

nodes.name: Asopus & Aegina (Aeacid Ancestors of Achilles, Ajax & Alexander, Apollodorus III.xii)
nodes.notes: River god Asopus -> Aegina -> King Aeacus -> Telamon (Ajax & Teucer) and Peleus (Achilles -> Neoptolemus -> Olympias -> Alexander!).

nodes.name: Erichthonius & Pandion I (Early Kings of Athens Anchor, Apollodorus III.xiv)
nodes.notes: Cecrops -> Erichthonius -> Pandion I -> Erechtheus -> Pandion II -> Aegeus -> Theseus.

nodes.name: House of Atreus Anchor (Pelopids of Mycenae, Apollodorus Epit. II–VI)
nodes.notes: Tantalus -> Pelops -> Atreus/Thyestes/Pittheus -> Agamemnon/Menelaus -> Orestes.

nodes.name: Orpheus (Thracian Singer & Argonaut, Son of Calliope)
nodes.notes: Orpheus (Thracian Singer & Argonaut, Son of Calliope).

nodes.name: Helios (Sun Titan; Son of Hyperion & Theia; Father of Aeetes)
nodes.notes: Helios (Sun Titan; Son of Hyperion & Theia; Father of Aeetes).

nodes.name: Selene (Moon Titaness; Daughter of Hyperion & Theia)
nodes.notes: Selene (Moon Titaness; Daughter of Hyperion & Theia).

nodes.name: Eos (Dawn Titaness; Mother of Memnon, Hyperion & Theia)
nodes.notes: Eos (Dawn Titaness; Mother of Memnon, Hyperion & Theia).

nodes.name: Hecate (Daughter of Perses & Asteria, Hesiod Theog. 411)
nodes.notes: Hecate (Daughter of Perses & Asteria, Hesiod Theog. 411).

nodes.name: Chiron the Wise Centaur (Son of Cronus & Philyra; Tutor of Achilles)
nodes.notes: Chiron the Wise Centaur (Son of Cronus & Philyra; Tutor of Achilles).

nodes.name: Medusa (Mortal Gorgon; Daughter of Phorcys & Ceto)
nodes.notes: Medusa (Mortal Gorgon; Daughter of Phorcys & Ceto).

nodes.name: Pegasus (Winged Steed Sprung From Medusa & Poseidon)
nodes.notes: Pegasus (Winged Steed Sprung From Medusa & Poseidon).

nodes.name: King Endymion of Elis (Son of Aethlius & Calyce)
nodes.notes: Son of Calyce (dau. of Aeolus) & Aethlius; father of Aetolus.

nodes.name: King Aetolus (Son of Endymion; Eponym of Aetolia)
nodes.notes: Son of Endymion; father of Pleuron & Calydon (-> Oeneus).

nodes.name: King Oeneus of Calydon (Father of Meleager, Deianira & Tydeus)
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Aetolus; father of Meleager, Deianira (wife of Heracles), and Tydeus.

nodes.name: Meleager (Hero of Calydonian Boar Hunt, Son of Oeneus & Althaea)
nodes.notes: Slew the Calydonian Boar alongside Atalanta.

nodes.name: Deianira (Daughter of Oeneus; Last Mortal Wife of Heracles)
nodes.role: Princess of Calydon & Mother of Hyllus
nodes.notes: Married Heracles and bore Hyllus, ancestor of the Dorian Heraclidae & Spartan kings.

nodes.name: Tydeus (Son of Oeneus; Hero of Seven Against Thebes)
nodes.notes: Wed Deipyle (daughter of Adrastus of Argos) and fathered Diomedes.

nodes.name: King Diomedes of Argos (Son of Tydeus; Iliad & Epigoni Hero)
nodes.notes: Led 80 Argive ships to Troy; succeeded maternal grandfather Adrastus.

nodes.name: Phrixus (Son of Athamas; Carrier of the Golden Fleece to Colchis)
nodes.role: Aeolid Prince Carried by the Golden Ram
nodes.notes: Fled to King Aeetes in Colchis, marrying Chalciope and bequeathing the Golden Fleece.

nodes.name: Helle (Daughter of Athamas; Eponym of the Hellespont)
nodes.notes: Twin sister of Phrixus who fell into the strait named Hellespont.

nodes.name: Bellerophon (Son of Glaucus; Slayer of the Chimera)
nodes.notes: Son of Glaucus of Corinth; slew the Chimera in Lycia; grandfather of Glaucus & Sarpedon.

nodes.name: Tyro (Daughter of Salmoneus; Mother of Pelias, Neleus & Aeson)
nodes.notes: Bore twins Pelias & Neleus by Poseidon, and Aeson, Pheres & Amythaon by Cretheus.

nodes.name: King Pelias of Iolcus (Half-Brother of Aeson; Opponent of Jason)
nodes.notes: Sent nephew Jason for the Golden Fleece; father of Alcestis & Acastus.

nodes.name: King Neleus of Pylos (+ Chloris; Father of Nestor)
nodes.role: Founder of Neleid Dynasty of Pylos
nodes.notes: Father of 12 sons, of whom youngest Nestor survived to rule Pylos.

nodes.name: King Nestor of Pylos (Wise Counselor of the Iliad, Son of Neleus)
nodes.role: Aged Counselor of Greeks at Troy
nodes.notes: Wise elder king of Pylos; father of Antilochus & Pisistratus.

nodes.name: Aeson (Eldest Son of Cretheus & Tyro; Father of Jason)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Cretheus; entrusted infant Jason to Centaur Chiron.

nodes.name: Jason (Leader of the Argonauts, Son of Aeson)
nodes.role: Captain of the Argo & Winner of the Golden Fleece
nodes.notes: Led the 50 Argonauts to Colchis and married Princess Medea.

nodes.name: Medea of Colchis (Daughter of King Aeetes; Granddaughter of Helios)
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Aeetes of Colchis; bore Medus/Medeus (mythic Greek eponym of the Medes).

nodes.name: Melampus the Seer (Son of Amythaon; King of Argos, Apollodorus I.ix.11)
nodes.notes: Cured Proetus's daughters and received a third of Argos; ancestor of Amphiaraus.

nodes.name: Amphiaraus the Seer (Argonaut & Seven Against Thebes; Descendant of Melampus)
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Melampus; married Eriphyle (sister of Adrastus) and fathered Epigoni leader Alcmaeon.

nodes.name: King Adrastus of Argos (Son of Talaus; Leader of Seven Against Thebes)
nodes.role: Argive Leader of the Seven Against Thebes
nodes.notes: Grandson of Bias (brother of Melampus); survived the expedition on winged horse Arion.

nodes.name: King Admetus of Pherae (Son of Pheres; Husband of Alcestis)
nodes.role: Aeolid King of Pherae in Thessaly
nodes.notes: Served by Apollo for a year; wed Princess Alcestis.

nodes.name: Queen Alcestis (Daughter of Pelias; Wife of Admetus)
nodes.role: Devoted Queen Rescued From Hades by Heracles
nodes.notes: Gave her life for husband Admetus before Heracles restored her from the underworld.

nodes.name: King Phoroneus of Argos (Son of Inachus; First Man of Greece)
nodes.notes: Son of Inachus; father of Niobe (mother of Argus & Pelasgus).

nodes.name: Argus Panoptes (All-Seeing Descendant of Niobe & Phoroneus)
nodes.notes: All-seeing Argive hero slain by Hermes.

nodes.name: Hypermnestra (Eldest Danaid Who Spared Her Husband)
nodes.notes: Sole Danaid to spare Lynceus; mother of Abas.

nodes.name: King Lynceus of Argos (Son of Aegyptus; Husband of Hypermnestra)
nodes.notes: Son of Aegyptus; wed Hypermnestra and founded the later Argive dynasty.

nodes.name: King Abas of Argos (Son of Lynceus & Hypermnestra)
nodes.role: Father of Twin Kings Acrisius & Proetus
nodes.notes: Father of Acrisius of Argos and Proetus of Tiryns.

nodes.name: King Acrisius of Argos (Father of Danaë)
nodes.role: Twin Son of Abas & King of Argos
nodes.notes: Father of Danaë; accidentally slain at Larissa by grandson Perseus.

nodes.name: King Proetus of Tiryns (Twin Brother of Acrisius)
nodes.role: King of Tiryns & Builder of Cyclopean Walls
nodes.notes: Twin brother of Acrisius; shared Argos with Melampus & Bias.

nodes.name: Princess Danaë of Argos (Daughter of Acrisius; Mother of Perseus)
nodes.notes: Placed in a wooden chest with infant Perseus and washed ashore at Seriphos.

nodes.name: Princess Alcmene of Mycenae (Daughter of Electryon; Mother of Heracles)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Electryon (son of Perseus); bore Heracles by Zeus and twin Iphicles by Amphitryon.

nodes.name: Prince Amphitryon (Son of Alcaeus; Stepfather of Heracles)
nodes.notes: Son of Alcaeus (son of Perseus); husband of Alcmene and biological father of Iphicles.

nodes.name: Iphicles (Twin Brother of Heracles; Father of Iolaus)
nodes.notes: Son of Amphitryon & Alcmene; father of Heracles's charioteer Iolaus.

nodes.name: King Eurystheus of Mycenae (Son of Sthenelus; Imposer of 12 Labors)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Perseus via Sthenelus & Nicippe; ordered Heracles's Twelve Labors.

nodes.name: Hyllus (Eldest Son of Heracles & Deianira; Forefather of Spartan Kings)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Heracles & Deianira; wed Iole; ancestor of Cleodaeus -> Aristomachus -> Temenus & Aristodemus.

nodes.name: King Telephus of Mysia (Son of Heracles & Auge)
nodes.notes: Son of Heracles & Arcadian princess Auge; healed by Achilles's spear rust before Troy.

nodes.name: King Temenus of Argos (Great-Great-Grandson of Heracles; Ancestor of Macedon!)
nodes.role: Heraclid Conqueror of Argos & Founder of Argead Line
nodes.notes: Dorian Heraclid king of Argos from whom Alexander the Great's Argead house traced descent.

nodes.name: King Cresphontes of Messene (Brother of Temenus & Aristodemus)
nodes.notes: Drew Messene by lot alongside brothers Temenus and Aristodemus.

nodes.name: Aristodemus (Heraclid Father of Spartan Twin Kings)
nodes.role: Father of Eurysthenes & Procles of Sparta
nodes.notes: Married Argia and sired twins Eurysthenes & Procles, founding Sparta's dual kingship.

nodes.name: King Eurysthenes (Founder of Agiad Dynasty of Sparta — Line of Leonidas!)
nodes.notes: Elder twin son of Aristodemus; forefather of Agis I, Leonidas I & Areus I.

nodes.name: King Procles (Founder of Eurypontid Dynasty of Sparta — Line of Agesilaus II!)
nodes.notes: Younger twin son of Aristodemus; forefather of Lycurgan-era Charilaus & Agesilaus II.

nodes.name: Queen Pasiphaë of Crete (Daughter of Helios; Wife of Minos)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sun Titan Helios; wife of King Minos.

nodes.name: Asterion / The Minotaur (Born to Pasiphaë, Apollodorus III.i.4)
nodes.notes: Housed in Daedalus's Knossos Labyrinth until slain by Theseus.

nodes.name: Princess Ariadne of Crete (Daughter of Minos & Pasiphaë; Wife of Dionysus)
nodes.notes: Gave Theseus the thread to escape the Labyrinth; wed Dionysus at Naxos.

nodes.name: Queen Phaedra of Athens (Daughter of Minos & Pasiphaë; Wife of Theseus)
nodes.notes: Younger sister of Ariadne; wed Theseus and bore Acamas & Demophon.

nodes.name: King Idomeneus of Crete (Son of Deucalion; Trojan War Commander)
nodes.role: Cretan Leader of 80 Ships at Troy
nodes.notes: Grandson of Minos via Deucalion.

nodes.name: Princess Semele of Thebes (Daughter of Cadmus; Mother of Dionysus)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Cadmus & Harmonia; bore Dionysus by Zeus.

nodes.name: Dionysus (God of Wine & Ecstasy, Son of Zeus & Semele)
nodes.notes: Became an Olympian god and husband of Cretan princess Ariadne.

nodes.name: King Polydorus of Thebes (Son of Cadmus & Harmonia)
nodes.notes: Son of Cadmus; father of Labdacus.

nodes.name: King Labdacus of Thebes (Son of Polydorus)
nodes.notes: Father of King Laius.

nodes.name: King Laius of Thebes (Son of Labdacus; Husband of Jocasta)
nodes.notes: Wed Jocasta (Epicaste), daughter of Menoeceus.

nodes.name: King Oedipus of Thebes (Son of Laius & Jocasta; Solver of the Sphinx)
nodes.notes: Solved the Sphinx's riddle and fathered Eteocles, Polynices, Antigone & Ismene.

nodes.name: King Eteocles of Thebes (Elder Son of Oedipus)
nodes.role: Defender of Thebes Against the Seven
nodes.notes: Fell in single combat against brother Polynices at the Seventh Gate.

nodes.name: Polynices of Thebes (Younger Son of Oedipus; Initiator of Seven Against Thebes)
nodes.notes: Wed Argeia (daughter of Adrastus) and marched with the Seven.

nodes.name: Antigone (Daughter of Oedipus Who Buried Polynices)
nodes.notes: Defied King Creon's decree to bury brother Polynices.

nodes.name: Ismene (Younger Daughter of Oedipus)
nodes.notes: Younger sister of Antigone.

nodes.name: Illyrius (Youngest Son of Cadmus; Eponym of Illyria)
nodes.notes: Born in Encheleia / Illyria in Cadmus's old age.

nodes.name: Alcmaeon (Son of Amphiaraus; Leader of the Epigoni)
nodes.role: Conqueror of Thebes With the Epigoni
nodes.notes: Led the sons of the Seven to capture Thebes a decade later.

nodes.name: King Pelasgus of Arcadia (Autochthonous Progenitor / Son of Niobe)
nodes.notes: Father of Lycaon in Arcadia.

nodes.name: King Lycaon of Arcadia (Father of 50 Sons & Callisto)
nodes.notes: Struck down before Deucalion's Flood; father of Callisto.

nodes.name: Callisto (Daughter of Lycaon; Constellation Ursa Major)
nodes.notes: Bore Arcas to Zeus.

nodes.name: King Arcas of Arcadia (Son of Callisto; Eponym of Arcadia)
nodes.notes: Father of Elatus, Aphidas (-> Aleus) & Azan.

nodes.name: Atalanta of Arcadia (Daughter of Iasus; Huntress & Argonaut)
nodes.role: Virgin Huntress of the Calydonian Boar
nodes.notes: Descendant of Arcas via Clymene; mother of Parthenopaeus.

nodes.name: King Lacedaemon (Son of Zeus & Taygete; Eponym of Sparta)
nodes.notes: Married Sparta (daughter of Eurotas) and named the kingdom after himself & his queen.

nodes.name: Queen Sparta (Daughter of River Eurotas; Eponym of City of Sparta)
nodes.notes: Wife of Lacedaemon; mother of Amyclas & Eurydice (wife of Acrisius!).

nodes.name: King Tyndareus of Sparta (Descendant of Lacedaemon; Husband of Leda)
nodes.role: Spartan King & Stepfather of Helen & Dioscuri
nodes.notes: Brother of Icarius; wed Aetolian princess Leda.

nodes.name: Queen Leda of Sparta (Daughter of Thestius; Mother of Helen, Clytemnestra, Castor & Pollux)
nodes.notes: Mother of Castor, Pollux, Helen & Clytemnestra.

nodes.name: Helen of Sparta / Troy (Daughter of Zeus & Leda; Consort of Menelaus & Paris)
nodes.role: Queen of Sparta Whose Abduction Sparked the Trojan War
nodes.notes: Sister of Clytemnestra, Castor & Pollux; married Menelaus.

nodes.name: Queen Clytemnestra of Mycenae (Daughter of Tyndareus & Leda; Wife of Agamemnon)
nodes.notes: Mother of Orestes, Electra & Iphigenia.

nodes.name: Castor (Dioscuri Twin, Son of Tyndareus & Leda)
nodes.notes: Twin brother of Pollux, celebrated among the Argonauts.

nodes.name: Pollux / Polydeuces (Dioscuri Immortal Boxer, Son of Zeus & Leda)
nodes.notes: Boxer-twin of Castor who shared immortality between Olympus and Hades.

nodes.name: Queen Penelope of Ithaca (Daughter of Icarius of Sparta; Wife of Odysseus)
nodes.role: Faithful Queen of Ithaca & Cousin of Helen
nodes.notes: Daughter of Spartan prince Icarius; bore Telemachus to Odysseus.

nodes.name: Asclepius (God of Medicine, Son of Apollo & Arsinoe/Coronis)
nodes.notes: Taught medicine by Chiron; father of physicians Machaon & Podalirius at Troy.

nodes.name: King Aeacus of Aegina (Son of Zeus & Aegina; Father of Telamon & Peleus)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Achilles, Ajax & Alexander the Great.

nodes.name: King Telamon of Salamis (Son of Aeacus; Argonaut & Father of Ajax)
nodes.role: King of Salamis & Companion of Heracles
nodes.notes: Fathered Ajax the Great (by Periboea) and Teucer (by Trojan princess Hesione!).

nodes.name: Ajax the Great (Telamonian Bulwark of the Achaeans at Troy)
nodes.notes: Son of Telamon & Periboea; cousin of Achilles.

nodes.name: Teucer (Son of Telamon & Trojan Princess Hesione; Founder of Salamis in Cyprus)
nodes.role: Master Archer & Founder of Cypriot Salamis
nodes.notes: Half-brother of Ajax and nephew of King Priam of Troy through mother Hesione.

nodes.name: King Peleus of Phthia (Son of Aeacus; Father of Achilles)
nodes.notes: Wed Nereid Thetis in the presence of all the Olympians.

nodes.name: Nereid Thetis (Daughter of Nereus & Doris; Mother of Achilles)
nodes.notes: Dipped infant Achilles in the Styx and commissioned Hephaestus's armor.

nodes.name: King Neoptolemus / Pyrrhus of Epirus (Son of Achilles; Ancestor of Olympias!)
nodes.era: Apollodorus Epit. V.10, VI.12; Plutarch Pyrrhus 1
nodes.role: Founder of Molossian Royal Line of Epirus
nodes.notes: Son of Achilles & Deidamia; founded the Aeacid Molossian dynasty of Epirus leading to Olympias & King Pyrrhus.

nodes.name: Queen Olympias of Epirus (Daughter of Neoptolemus I of Epirus; Mother of Alexander!)
nodes.role: Molossian Princess & Mother of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Claimed direct descent from Achilles's son Neoptolemus; wed King Philip II of Macedon and bore Alexander the Great.

nodes.name: King Cecrops I of Athens (1st King of Attica; Eusebius 1556 BCE Trad.)
nodes.notes: Judged the contest between Athena & Poseidon for Attica.

nodes.name: King Erechtheus of Athens (Father of Creusa & Orithyia)
nodes.notes: Son of Pandion I; father of Creusa (mother of Ion!) and Cecrops II.

nodes.name: King Aegeus of Athens (Father of Theseus, Apollodorus III.xv.5)
nodes.notes: Wed Aethra (daughter of King Pittheus of Troezen) and fathered Theseus.

nodes.name: King Theseus of Athens (Slayer of the Minotaur; Son of Aegeus & Aethra)
nodes.notes: Slew the Cretan Minotaur, united Attica, wed Ariadne & Phaedra, and fathered Hippolytus, Acamas & Demophon.

nodes.name: King Tantalus of Lydia / Sipylus (Father of Pelops & Niobe)
nodes.role: Anatolian Founder of the Pelopid House
nodes.notes: Father of Pelops (Peloponnese) and Niobe.

nodes.name: Queen Niobe of Thebes (Daughter of Tantalus; Wife of Amphion)
nodes.role: Queen of Thebes Weeping on Mt. Sipylus
nodes.notes: Boasted over Leto, bringing grief upon Thebes.

nodes.name: Thyestes (Son of Pelops; Rival Brother of Atreus)
nodes.notes: Father of Aegisthus.

nodes.name: Aegisthus (Son of Thyestes; Slain by Orestes)
nodes.notes: Slain by Orestes after plotting Agamemnon's death.

nodes.name: King Orestes of Mycenae & Sparta (Son of Agamemnon; Father of Tisamenus)
nodes.role: Heir of Atreids Who United Mycenae & Sparta
nodes.notes: Married cousin Hermione (daughter of Menelaus & Helen) and fathered Tisamenus.

nodes.name: Princess Electra (Daughter of Agamemnon & Clytemnestra)
nodes.notes: Protected young Orestes; later wed Pylades.

nodes.name: Iphigenia (Eldest Daughter of Agamemnon; Priestess at Tauris)
nodes.notes: Carried by Artemis to Tauris before reuniting with Orestes.

nodes.name: Paris / Alexander of Troy (Son of Priam & Hecuba)
nodes.notes: Son of King Priam & Hecuba; awarded the golden apple to Aphrodite.

nodes.name: Prince Hector of Troy (Champion of Troy; Husband of Andromache)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Priam & Hecuba; slain outside Troy's gates by Achilles.

nodes.name: Princess Cassandra of Troy (Prophetess Daughter of Priam & Hecuba)
nodes.notes: Gifted true prophecy never believed.

nodes.name: Prince Helenus of Troy (Prophet Twin of Cassandra; King in Epirus)
nodes.role: Trojan Seer Who Wed Andromache in Epirus
nodes.notes: Welcomed Aeneas at Buthrotum in Epirus.

nodes.name: Princess Creusa of Troy (Daughter of Priam; 1st Wife of Aeneas & Mother of Ascanius)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Priam & Hecuba; mother of Ascanius/Iulus by Aeneas.

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine Anchor (Gens 2–30: Ikshvaku to Trayyaruna)
nodes.era: Satya Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 2-30, p. 145)
nodes.role: First 30 Generations of Solar Ayodhya Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 90-92, 145
nodes.notes: Anchor for the first 30 generations of Aikshvaku kings (Mandhatri, Purukutsa, Trasadasyu), unrolled father-to-son below.

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine Anchor (Gens 31–64: Trishanku to Dasharatha)
nodes.era: Treta Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 31-64, pp. 145, 147)
nodes.role: Golden Era of Solar Dynasty Leading to Lord Rama Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 92-94, 145-147
nodes.notes: Anchor for Gens 31-64 (Harishchandra, Sagara, Bhagiratha, Raghu, Dasharatha), chained individually below.

nodes.name: Ayodhya Post-Rama Spine Anchor (Gens 66–95: Kusha to Brihatkshaya)
nodes.era: Dvapara Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 66-95, p. 149)
nodes.role: 30 Generations from Rama's Son Kusha to Mahabharata Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 94-95, 149
nodes.notes: Anchor for post-Rama Solar kings down to Brihadbala (Kurukshetra) & Brihatkshaya, chained below.

nodes.name: Videha / Mithila Solar Dynasty (All 54 Kings: Nimi → Mithi Janaka → Siradhvaja → Janaka-Ugrasena)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 95-96, 145-149
nodes.notes: Founded by Ikshvaku's son Nimi -> Mithi Janaka -> Siradhvaja Janaka (father of Goddess Sita).

nodes.name: Manu's Other Solar Kingdoms: Vaisali (Nabhanedishtha → Marutta → Trinabindu), Sharyatas & Nabhagas
nodes.role: Ancient Dynasties of North Bihar (Vaisali) & Gujarat (Anarta)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 97-98, 145-147
nodes.notes: Nabhanedishtha's line produced Marutta & Trinabindu; Sharyati's line produced Raivata Kakudmin.

nodes.name: Kanyakubja Dynasty Anchor (Amavasu → Jahnu → Gadhi → Vishvamitra)
nodes.role: Aila Kingdom of Kanauj & Origin of Vishvamitra Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 99-101, 234-237
nodes.notes: Pururavas's son Amavasu -> Jahnu -> Gadhi -> Brahmarshi Vishvamitra (Rigveda Mandala III).

nodes.name: Kasi (Varanasi) Dynasty Anchor (Kshatravriddha → Dhanvantari → Divodasa II → Alarka)
nodes.era: Gens 5-94 (Pargiter Ch. IX p. 101; Ch. XIII pp. 153-155)
nodes.role: Ancient Sacred Kingdom of Varanasi & Origin of Ayurveda Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 101, 145-155
nodes.notes: Kshatravriddha -> Dhanvantari -> Divodasa II -> Pratardana -> Alarka.

nodes.name: Haihaya Dynasty Anchor (Yadu → Sahasrajit → Kartavirya Arjuna → Talajanghas)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102, 144-146, 153-156
nodes.notes: Kartavirya Arjuna (Gen 31) of Mahishmati; crushed by Parashurama & Sagara.

nodes.name: Yadava Main Line Anchor (Kroshtu → Shashabindu → Vidarbha → Satvata → Vrishni)
nodes.role: Complete Yadava Pedigree Anchor (Yadu to Krishna & Vajra)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102-107, 144-148, 284
nodes.notes: Kroshtu -> Shashabindu -> Jyamagha -> Vidarbha -> Satvata -> Andhaka & Vrishni.

nodes.name: Druhyus (Gandhara → Pracetas) & Turvasus (Pandya, Kerala & Chola Anchor)
nodes.role: Northwest (Gandhara/Central Asia) & South Indian Aila Bridges
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108, 144, 146
nodes.notes: Druhyu -> Gandhara -> Pracetas; Turvasu -> Marutta -> Pandya, Kerala, and Chola.

nodes.name: Anavas Anchor (Ushinara → Shibi & Titikshu → Bali → Anga/Vanga/Kalinga → Karna)
nodes.role: Progenitors of Panjab (Shibi) & Eastern India (Bengal/Odisha/Anga) Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108-109, 145-149
nodes.notes: Ushinara -> King Shibi; Titikshu -> King Bali -> Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Pundra & Suhma -> Karna.

nodes.name: North & South Panchalas Anchor (Mudgala → Sudas → Drupada & Draupadi)
nodes.role: Rigvedic Battle of Ten Kings Hero Sudas & Panchala Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 115-117, 146-148
nodes.notes: Ajamidha -> Nila -> Mudgala -> Divodasa -> Sudas -> Drupada -> Draupadi & Dhrishtadyumna.

nodes.name: Cedi & Magadha Barhadratha Anchor (Vasu Uparichara → Brihadratha → Jarasandha)
nodes.role: First Historical Dynasty of Magadha & Cedi Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 118-119, 149
nodes.notes: Vasu Uparichara -> Brihadratha -> Emperor Jarasandha & Damaghosha -> Shishupala (Cedi).

nodes.name: Post-Mahabharata Kurus Anchor (Janamejaya III → Adhisimakrishna → Nicakshu → Udayana)
nodes.era: c. 950-500 BCE (Pargiter Ch. XXIV p. 285; Ch. XXVII p. 330)
nodes.role: Continuation of Pandava/Kuru Royal Line After Hastinapura Flood
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 285, 330
nodes.notes: Nicakshu moved Kuru capital to Kaushambi in Vatsa down to King Udayana.

nodes.name: Great Rishi Clans Anchor: Bhargavas & Angirasas / Kanvas
nodes.role: Complete Genealogies of Bhargava, Angirasa & Kanva Seers Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 191-202, 218-227
nodes.notes: Synchronizes Bhrigu/Cyavana/Jamadagni/Parashurama/Valmiki & Atharvan/Brihaspati/Bharadvaja/Drona across the 95-gen master table.

nodes.name: Great Rishi Clans Anchor: Vasishthas (Vyasa), Atreyas, Kashyapas & Agastyas
nodes.era: Gens 1-94 (Pargiter Ch. XVIII, XX, XXII, pp. 203-242)
nodes.role: Complete Pedigrees of Vyasa, Durvasas, Rishyashringa & Agastya Anchor
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 203-242
nodes.notes: Synchronizes Vasishtha -> Shakti -> Parashara -> Vyasa -> Shuka alongside Datta/Durvasas, Kanva, Rishyashringa & Agastya.

nodes.name: Historical Magadha Anchor (22 Barhadrathas → Pradyotas → Shishunaga/Bimbisara → 9 Nandas)

sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 179-182, 286-287

nodes.name: Mermnad Dynasty of Lydia: Gyges → Ardys → Sadyattes → Alyattes → King Croesus
nodes.era: 680-546 BCE (Herodotus I; Eusebius; Betham Tab. LXVI)
nodes.role: Inventors of Coinage & Anatolian Empire Defeated by Cyrus
nodes.notes: Overthrew Heraclid king Candaules (son of Myrsus). Alyattes's daughter Aryenis married Median King Astyages (grandfather of Cyrus the Great!), making Croesus the great-uncle/brother-in-law of the Median court he fought to avenge against Cyrus in 546 BCE.

nodes.name: Kings of Tyre: Abibaal → Hiram I → Baal-ezer → Ethbaal I (Ithobaal) → Mattan I → Pygmalion & Dido
nodes.era: c. 990-774 BCE (Josephus Against Apion I.18; Betham Tab. XCII)
nodes.role: Phoenician Maritime Dynasty Linking Solomon, Ahab & Carthage
nodes.notes: Menander of Ephesus (quoted by Josephus!) preserves the complete Tyrian royal archive: Hiram I (ally of David & Solomon) -> ... -> Ethbaal I (Priest of Astarte, father of Queen Jezebel who married King Ahab of Israel!) -> Baal-ezer II -> Mattan I -> Pygmalion & Princess Elissa/Dido (founder of Carthage, 814 BCE)!

nodes.name: Barcid Dynasty of Carthage: Hamilcar Barca → Hannibal Barca, Hasdrubal & Mago
nodes.notes: Hamilcar Barca (hero of 1st Punic War) fathered Hannibal the Great (crossed the Alps in 218 BCE, victor at Cannae), Hasdrubal Barca, Mago Barca, and daughters married to Hasdrubal the Fair & Numidian prince Naravas. Allied with Hasdrubal Gisco (father of Sophonisba).

nodes.name: Kings of Numidia & Mauretania: Gaia → Masinissa → Micipsa → Jugurtha; Juba I → Juba II (+ Cleopatra Selene II)
nodes.role: Amazigh (Berber) Royal Dynasties of North Africa
nodes.notes: Masinissa unified Numidia (ally of Scipio Africanus against Hannibal); his grandson Jugurtha resisted Rome. Later King Juba II of Mauretania married Cleopatra Selene II (daughter of Mark Antony & Cleopatra VII of Egypt!), fathering King Ptolemy of Mauretania — uniting Berber, Ptolemaic Egyptian, and Roman bloodlines!

nodes.name: Seleucid Empire: Seleucus I Nicator (+ Apama of Sogdia) → Antiochus I → Antiochus III the Great → Antiochus IV Epiphanes
nodes.era: 312-63 BCE (Eusebius Chronicle; Betham Tab. CIII; 1 Maccabees)
nodes.role: Hellenistic Kings of Syria, Mesopotamia & Persia
nodes.notes: Founded by Alexander's general Seleucus I Nicator & Iranian princess Apama (daughter of Spitamenes of Sogdia). Antiochus III the Great's daughter Cleopatra I Syra married Ptolemy V (starting the 'Cleopatra' name in Egypt!). Antiochus IV Epiphanes sparked the Maccabean Revolt (167 BCE).

nodes.name: Antigonid Macedon (Antigonus I, Demetrius, Philip V, Perseus) & Pyrrhus of Epirus
nodes.role: Final Macedonian Kings & Aeacid Kings of Epirus
nodes.notes: Antigonus Monophthalmus -> Demetrius Poliorcetes -> Antigonus II Gonatas -> Philip V -> Perseus (defeated by Rome at Pydna, 168 BCE). King Pyrrhus of Epirus (cousin of Alexander via Olympias & claiming descent from Achilles's son Neoptolemus!) fought Rome ('Pyrrhic victory').

nodes.name: Kingdom of Pontus: Mithridates I Ktistes → Pharnaces I → Mithridates VI Eupator ('The Poison King')
nodes.role: Persian-Greek Royal Dynasty of the Black Sea
nodes.notes: Claimed descent from both Darius the Great (Achaemenids) and Alexander/Seleucids! Mithridates VI Eupator waged three Mithridatic Wars against Rome; his daughter Cleopatra married King Tigranes the Great of Armenia, and his son Pharnaces II ruled the Bosporan Kingdom ('Veni, vidi, vici').

nodes.name: Artaxiad Armenia: Artaxias I → Tigranes II the Great (+ Cleopatra of Pontus) → Artavasdes II & Herodian Tigranes V/VI
nodes.era: 189 BCE – 63 CE (Betham Tab. LXXXIII; Josephus Ant. XVIII)
nodes.role: Imperial Kingdom of Armenia Linking Pontus, Parthia & Judea
nodes.notes: Artaxias I founded Artaxata; Tigranes the Great built a vast empire from the Caspian to the Mediterranean. Remarkable dynastic link: Herod the Great's grandson Tigranes V & great-grandson Tigranes VI (via Alexander + Glaphyra of Cappadocia) were placed on the throne of Armenia by Rome!

nodes.name: Greco-Bactrian & Indo-Greek Kings: Diodotus I → Euthydemus → Demetrius I → Menander I (King Milinda)
nodes.role: Hellenistic Kings of Afghanistan & Northwest India
nodes.notes: Diodotus broke away from the Seleucids in Bactria; Demetrius I invaded India (Gandhara/Punjab); Menander I Soter (Pali: Milinda) converted to Buddhism in the famous dialogue Milinda Panha with sage Nagasena — bridging Greek, Iranian, and Indian civilizations!

nodes.name: Royal Houses of Adiabene (Monobazus I & Queen Helena → Izates II) & Osroene/Edessa (King Abgar V)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XX.2; Betham Tab. LXX-LXXI)
nodes.role: Upper Mesopotamian Client Kingdoms Famous in Jewish & Syriac History
nodes.notes: Queen Helena of Adiabene & her son King Izates II converted to Judaism (~30 CE), funded famine relief in Jerusalem, and built the monumental Tomb of the Kings in Jerusalem. King Abgar V Ukkama of Edessa (Osroene) features in Syriac chronicles as the first Christian monarch.

nodes.name: Kings of Alba Longa: Ascanius (Iulus) → Silvius → Capys → Tiberinus → Aventinus → Procas → Numitor & Amulius
nodes.era: c. 1177-753 BCE (Livy I; Eusebius Chronicle; Betham Tab. CIX-CXI)
nodes.role: 14 Trojan-Latin Kings Bridging Aeneas to Romulus & Remus
nodes.notes: Complete Latin succession from Aeneas (+ Lavinia daughter of King Latinus): Ascanius/Iulus (claimed ancestor of the Julii Caesars!), Silvius Posthumus, Aeneas Silvius, Latinus Silvius, Alba, Atys, Capys, Capetus, Tiberinus (eponym of the Tiber River), Agrippa, Romulus Silvius, Aventinus, Procas -> Numitor (father of Rhea Silvia) & usurper Amulius.

nodes.name: 7 Kings of Rome: Romulus, Numa Pompilius, Tullus Hostilius, Ancus Marcius, Tarquinius Priscus, Servius Tullius & Tarquinius Superbus
nodes.era: 753-509 BCE (Livy I; Eusebius; Betham Tab. CXII)
nodes.role: Complete Roman Monarchy to Republic Founder L. Junius Brutus
nodes.notes: Sabine co-ruler Titus Tatius -> Numa Pompilius -> Tullus Hostilius -> Ancus Marcius -> Etruscan Tarquinius Priscus (+ Tanaquil) -> Servius Tullius -> Tarquinius Superbus (expelled in 509 BCE by Lucius Junius Brutus & Tarquinius Collatinus, founding the Roman Republic!).

nodes.name: Julio-Claudian Emperors: Augustus (+ Livia) → Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius & Nero
nodes.era: 27 BCE – 68 CE (Suetonius; Tacitus; Betham Tab. CXXI; Anderson)
nodes.role: First Imperial Dynasty of Rome (New Testament Era)
nodes.notes: Augustus (census at Jesus's birth, Luke 2:1) -> Tiberius (Jesus's ministry & crucifixion, Luke 3:1) -> Caligula (descended from Mark Antony & Agrippa) -> Claudius (Acts 18:2) -> Nero (martyrdom of Peter & Paul, Great Fire of 64 CE).

nodes.name: Flavian (Vespasian, Titus, Domitian), Five Good Emperors (Trajan, Hadrian, Marcus Aurelius) & Severan Dynasties
nodes.role: High Imperial Roman Dynasties (Including Syro-Punic Severans)
nodes.notes: Vespasian & Titus (destruction of Jerusalem Temple, 70 CE — patrons of Josephus!) -> Domitian (interviewed grandsons of Jude, brother of Jesus!). Nerva -> Trajan -> Hadrian -> Antoninus Pius -> Marcus Aurelius -> Commodus. Septimius Severus (Punic/Libyan from Leptis Magna!) + Julia Domna (Priest-King house of Emesa!) -> Caracalla.

nodes.name: Constantine the Great → Theodosius I → Justinian I → Heraclius → Basil I → Alexios Komnenos → Constantine XI
nodes.role: Christian Roman & Eastern Byzantine Imperial Lineages
nodes.notes: Constantine I (+ St. Helena) founded Constantinople (330 CE) -> Theodosius I (split East/West 395 CE) -> Justinian I (+ Empress Theodora, Hagia Sophia) -> Heraclius (defeated Sasanian Khosrow II) -> Macedonian Dynasty (Basil I, Basil II) -> Komnenoi -> Palaiologoi (until 1453).

nodes.name: Merovingians (Merovech → Clovis I) & Carolingians (Charles Martel → Pepin → Charlemagne)
nodes.role: Frankish Kings & Founder of the Holy Roman Empire (Ancestral Hub of Europe)
nodes.notes: Clovis I unified the Franks (481-511). Carolingian Mayor of the Palace Charles Martel (Battle of Tours, 732) -> Pepin the Short -> Charlemagne (crowned Emperor 800 CE) -> Louis the Pious -> Treaty of Verdun (Lothair, Louis the German, Charles the Bald). Chroniclers (Fredegar/Anderson) linked early Franks back to Trojan exiles (Francus)!

nodes.name: House of Wessex (Cerdic → Egbert → Alfred the Great → Æthelstan) & Normans (Rollo → William the Conqueror)
nodes.role: Founders of England (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle Bridges Woden → Sceaf of Noah's Ark!)
nodes.notes: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (under King Æthelwulf, father of Alfred the Great) famously traces Wessex back through Cerdic -> Woden (Odin) -> Geat -> Sceaf ('born in Noah's Ark'!) -> Noah -> Adam! Rollo the Viking founded Normandy -> William the Conqueror (1066) -> Henry II & Eleanor of Aquitaine (Plantagenets).

nodes.name: Rurik (+ Sineus & Truvor, 862 CE) → Oleg & Igor' (+ St. Olga of Kiev)
nodes.role: Varangian-Japhethic Founders of the Rurikid Dynasty
nodes.notes: Varangian prince Rurik (expressly placed under the race of Japheth in the Primary Chronicle p. 52) settled Novgorod with brothers Sineus & Truvor (862 CE); regent Oleg united Novgorod & Kiev for Rurik's son Igor' and St. Olga of Pskov.

nodes.name: Svyatoslav I of Kiev (Son of Igor' & Olga)
nodes.notes: Son of Igor' and St. Olga; campaigned across the Volga, Khazaria, and the Danube; father of Vladimir the Great.

nodes.name: St. Vladimir the Great of Kiev (Baptized Kievan Rus', 988 CE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Rurik and St. Olga; married Byzantine Princess Anna Porphyrogenita and established Christianity across Rus' in 988 CE.

nodes.name: Yaroslav the Wise (1019–1054 CE) → Royal Houses of Rus', France, Norway & Hungary
nodes.role: Grand Prince of Kiev & Pan-European Ancestor
nodes.notes: Son of St. Vladimir; linked the Rurikid line into Western & Northern European monarchies through his daughters Anne of Kiev (Queen of France), Anastasia (Hungary) & Elisiv (Norway).

nodes.name: Hayk Nahapet (Patriarch of Armenia, Slayer of Bel/Nimrod)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.5-11
nodes.notes: Movses Khorenatsi traces Hayk from Noah -> Japheth -> Gomer -> Tiras -> Togarmah (Torgom), describing his refusal to serve the tyrant Bel (Nimrod) at Babel and his victory over Bel near Lake Van.

nodes.name: Aramaneak → Aramayis → Amasia → Gegham → Harma → Aram (Eponym of Armenia) → Ara the Handsome
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Direct Haykid generational succession in Movses Khorenatsi leading through Aram (from whom neighbors named Armenia) to Ara the Handsome, contemporary of Assyrian queen Semiramis.

nodes.name: Shambat (Jewish Noble Exiled by Nebuchadnezzar) → Armenian Bagratuni Dynasty

nodes.role: Judeo-Armenian Ancestor of the Bagratuni & Bagrationi Houses
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.22, II.3
nodes.notes: Khorenatsi records that Armenian king Hracheay brought a prominent Jewish captive named Shambat (Smbat) from Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian exile — establishing the Armenian Bagratuni & Georgian Bagrationi royal claim.

nodes.name: Goths / Scythians (Berig → Filimer) — Race of Magog
nodes.role: Japhethic Origin of the Gothic & Scythian Peoples
nodes.notes: Jordanes (following Josephus) connects the Scythian & Gothic peoples to Magog son of Japheth and recounts King Berig leading three ships of Goths from Scandza across the Baltic to Gothiscandza, followed by Filimer to Oium.

nodes.name: Gapt (Gaut) → Amal (Amali) → Hermanaric → Theoderic the Great (Ostrogoths) & Alaric I (Visigoths)
nodes.role: Royal Ostrogothic Amali & Visigothic Balthi Lines
nodes.notes: Complete royal genealogy of the Gothic Amali from Gapt (Gaut) -> Hulmul -> Augis -> Amal -> Ostrogotha -> Achiulf -> Hermanaric & Vandalarius -> Thiudimer -> Theoderic the Great, alongside Alaric I of the Visigoths.

nodes.name: Baath (King of Scythia) → Fenius Farsa (Inventor of Letters at Shinar/Babel)
nodes.era: Post-Babel Scythia (Annals of the Four Masters; O'Hart pp. 31-34)
nodes.role: Magogian Patriarch of Gaelic & Scythian Learning
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 31-35
nodes.notes: O'Hart traces the stem of the Irish nation directly from Adam -> Seth -> ... -> Noah -> Japheth -> Magog -> Baath (King of Scythia) -> Fenius Farsa, who established a school of the 72 languages on the plain of Shinar after Babel.

nodes.name: Niul (+ Scota, Dau. of Pharaoh; Friend of Moses!) → Gaodhal Glas (Gael) → Asruth → Sruth → Heber Scot
nodes.role: Egyptian-Milesian Bridge & Eponym of the Gaels
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 6, 34-35
nodes.notes: Fenius Farsa's younger son Niul was invited to Egypt by Pharaoh, married Princess Scota, befriended Moses & the Israelites at the Red Sea, and begat Gaodhal Glas (Gael), father of the Goidelic language and line through Asruth, Sruth & Heber Scot.

nodes.name: Breoghan (Brigus of Spain) → Bile → Milesius of Spain (Galamh)
nodes.role: Progenitor of the Milesian High Kings of Ireland
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 29-35
nodes.notes: O'Hart generations #34-36 from Adam: Breoghan (Brigus, builder of Brigantia in Spain) -> Bile -> Galamh / Milesius of Spain, who married a second Pharaoh's daughter Scota.

nodes.name: Heber, Heremon, Ir & Uncle Ith (Milesian Monarchs of Ireland)
nodes.role: Joint Progenitors of the Major Irish & Scottish Houses
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 49-84
nodes.notes: Milesius's sons Heber (Munster lines), Heremon (Connacht, Leinster, High Kings & Dal Riada Scots), and Ir (Ulster), alongside uncle Ith, established the Milesian roll of Irish monarchs.

nodes.name: Conn of the Hundred Battles → Niall of the Nine Hostages (Uí Néill) & Brian Boru (Munster)
nodes.role: Historic High Kings of Ireland from Heremon & Heber
nodes.notes: Traces Heremon's line to Conn of the Hundred Battles -> Niall of the Nine Hostages (Uí Néill) and Heber's line to Brian Boru (d. 1014 CE) & MacCarthy/O'Brien families.

nodes.name: Cruithne (Founder of the Picts) → 7 Sons Dividing Alba (Fib, Fidach, Floclaid, Fortrenn, Got, Ce, Circinn)
nodes.role: Eponymous Ancestor of the Picts of Alba (Scotland)
sources: Skene Chronicles of the Picts & Scots pp. 209-252
nodes.notes: The Pictish Chronicle derives both Scots and Picts from Scythia/Albani (Noah -> Japheth -> Magog/Gomer), recording Cruithne and his seven sons giving their names to the seven provinces of Pictish Scotland.

nodes.name: Fergus Mor mac Erc (King of Dal Riada, 498 CE) → Kenneth MacAlpin (1st King of Scots & Picts, 843 CE)
nodes.role: Unifier of the Picts & Scots into the Scottish Crown
sources: Skene Chronicles of the Picts & Scots pp. cx, 44
nodes.notes: Fergus Mor mac Erc crossed from Irish Dal Riada (Heremon's Milesian line) to Argyll in 498 CE; his descendant Cináed mac Ailpín (Kenneth MacAlpin) united the Scottish and Pictish kingdoms in 843 CE.

nodes.name: Cunedda → Cadwaladr → Rhodri Mawr → Hywel Dda → Llywelyn the Great (Princes of Wales)

nodes.role: Welsh Royal Succession Descended from Brutus of Troy & Camber
