nodes.notes: Follows the Welsh chronicle tradition from Cunedda Wledig and Cadwaladr the Blessed through Rhodri Mawr (the Great), lawgiver Hywel Dda, Gruffudd ap Rhys & Llywelyn the Great, tracing Welsh sovereignty back to Brutus of Troy & Camber.

nodes.notes: Anderson Table p. 464 identifies Japheth's grandson Ashkenaz (Askanez) with Tacitus & Aventinus's Tuisco/Tuisto, pioneer ruler near the Tanais and Germany.

nodes.notes: Josephus Antiquities I.6.1 identifies Tubal son of Japheth with the Iberi ('Thobelites'), later joined in royal chronologies to the ancient kingdoms of Spain.

nodes.name: Gomer / Samothes (Progenitor of Gauls / Celts / Cimbri)

nodes.role: Japhethic Patriarch of the Cimmerians, Cimbri, Celts & Gauls
nodes.notes: Josephus states 'Gomer founded those whom the Greeks now call Galatians [Gauls], but were then called Gomerites'; Anderson links Gomer (Cimbri) and his son Samothes/Meshech to the Celts.

nodes.name: Noah = Janus / Ogyges → Sabatius Saga → Italus (Ancient Kings of Italy / Tuscany)
nodes.era: Annius / Anderson Chronography (1732 Table CCCCXXIV p. 702)
nodes.role: Renaissance-Baroque Noahic Synchronization of Pre-Roman Italy
sources: James Anderson Royal Genealogies (1732 Table CCCCXXIV p. 702)
nodes.notes: Anderson Table CCCCXXIV places Noah (identified as Janus / Ogyges) planting colonies in Italy with Gomer & Kittim, succeeded by Sabatius Saga and the ancient Kings of Tuscany & Italy.

nodes.name: Yam / Kan'an (Unbelieving Son of Noah Who Perished in the Flood)
nodes.era: Deluge Narrative (Al-Tabari Vol. 1 p. 360; Al-Mas'udi p. 75)
nodes.role: Fourth Pre-Flood Son in Islamic Exegesis
nodes.notes: Recorded alongside Shem, Ham, and Japheth by Al-Tabari and Al-Mas'udi (citing Quran 11:42-44): Noah's son Yam (or Kan'an) refused to board the Ark and perished in the waters.

nodes.name: Book of Jubilees Post-Flood Matriarchs (Rasu'eja, Melka dau. of Madai, Mu'ak, Azura dau. of Nimrod, Lomna, Ora, Milkah, Iyaska & Edna)
nodes.role: Named Post-Flood Matriarchs Connecting Shem, Japheth & Ham Lines
sources: Book of Jubilees (R.H. Charles Ch. 8-11 pp. 66-89)
nodes.notes: Jubilees 8-11 preserves every matriarch from Arphaxad to Abraham: Arphaxad + Rasu'eja (dau. of Elam); Cainan + Melka (dau. of Madai of Japheth!); Shelah + Mu'ak (dau. of Kesed); Eber + Azura (dau. of Nimrod/Nebrod!); Peleg + Lomna (Shinar); Reu + Ora (dau. of Ur); Serug + Milkah; Nahor + Iyaska; Terah + Edna!

nodes.name: Shabokah (Daughter of Japheth & Arbasisah)
nodes.role: Named Daughter of Japheth in Al-Tabari
sources: Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 11 (citing Wahb b. Munabbih)
nodes.notes: Al-Tabari records Japheth's wife Arbasisah (daughter of Marazil b. Darmasil of the Cainite line) bearing seven sons and daughter Shabokah.

nodes.name: 'Ad (Prophet Hud) & Thamud (Prophet Salih) — Ancient Arabian Tribes
nodes.era: Early Arabian Peninsula (Al-Tabari Vol. 2 pp. 14-16; Al-Mas'udi p. 76)
nodes.role: Shem -> Aram -> Uz -> Ancient Arab Nations ('Arab al-'Ariba)
nodes.notes: Arabian chroniclers derive the extinct 'original Arabs' ('Ad of al-Ahqaf under Prophet Hud, and Thamud of al-Hijr under Prophet Salih) directly from 'Us (Uz) b. Aram b. Shem b. Noah.

nodes.name: Tasm, Judays, Umaym & 'Imliq (Arabian Amalekites)
nodes.era: Post-Babel Dispersion (Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 16; Al-Mas'udi pp. 76-77)
nodes.role: Sons of Lud b. Shem Across Yamamah, Hijaz, Oman & Faris
nodes.notes: Tabari & Mas'udi preserve the Arabian Ludite tribes: Tasm & Judays (Yamamah/Bahrain), Jasim (Oman), 'Imliq (Hijaz/Syria/Amalekite Pharaohs), and Umaym (whose descendants settled Persia/Wabar).

nodes.name: Ya'rub (1st Arabic King), Jurhum (Mecca) & Saba → Himyar & Kahlan (Lakhmids & Ghassanids)
nodes.era: South & North Arabia (Al-Tabari Vol. 2 & 5; Al-Mas'udi p. 78)
nodes.role: Qahtanite / Yemenite Sovereign Stem & Mecca Marriage to Ishmael
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan p. 131
nodes.notes: Qahtan (Joktan) -> Ya'rub (said by Mas'udi to be the first king to articulate classical Arabic) & cousin Jurhum (who settled Mecca and married their daughter to Ishmael!) -> Abd Shams Saba -> Himyar (Yemen) & Kahlan (Banu Lakhm of al-Hirah & Ghassanids of Syria).

nodes.name: Al-Rum / Banu al-Asfar (Byzantines/Romans via Esau) & Prophet Job (Ayyub) + Liyya (dau. of Jacob)
nodes.role: Islamic/Arabian Identification of Esau with Rome & Job with Esau's Line
nodes.notes: Al-Tabari transmits the classical Arabic historical tradition identifying al-Rum / Banu al-Asfar (Romans/Byzantines) as descendants of Esau b. Isaac, and tracing Prophet Job (Ayyub b. Maws b. Razih/Raghwil b. Esau) marrying Jacob's daughter Liyya.

nodes.name: Prophet Shu'ayb (Jethro / Reuel of Midian)
nodes.role: Prophet of Midian Descended from Abraham & Keturah
nodes.notes: Mas'udi records the genealogy of Shu'ayb (identified with Jethro/Reuel, father-in-law of Moses): Shu'ayb b. Thoriel b. Da'wayel b. Marik b. 'Anka b. Madyan (Midian) b. Abraham.

nodes.name: Complete 21-Gen Quraysh Lineage (Tabari Vol. 6): Adnan → Ma'add → Nizar → Mudar → Ilyas → Mudrikah → Khuzaymah → Kinanah → al-Nadr → Malik → Fihr (Quraysh) → Ghalib → Lu'ayy → Ka'b → Murrah → Kilab → Qusayy → 'Abd Manaf → Hashim → 'Abd al-Muttalib → 'Abdallah
nodes.role: Unbroken 21-Generation Pedigree from Adnan to the Father of Prophet Muhammad
nodes.notes: Complete 21-generation genealogy preserved in Tabari Vol. 6 (and tabulated by Lane-Poole & Zambaur), linking Adnan (Ishmaelite) down to 'Abdallah b. 'Abd al-Muttalib, father of Muhammad.

nodes.name: Major Islamic Caliphal Houses (Lane-Poole & Zambaur): Umayyads ('Abd Shams), Abbasids (al-'Abbas), Fatimids (Isma'il), Idrisids (Morocco) & Sharifs of Mecca
nodes.role: Caliphal & Royal Houses Descending from Quraysh & Abraham via Ishmael
sources: E. de Zambaur Manuel de Généalogie (1927)
nodes.notes: Complete comparative dynasties from Lane-Poole & Zambaur: 'Abd Manaf -> 'Abd Shams (Umayyad Caliphs of Damascus & Cordoba); Hashim -> al-'Abbas (Abbasid Caliphs of Baghdad); Ali & Fatimah -> Fatimids of Cairo, Idrisids of Morocco & Qatadid Sharifs of Mecca.

nodes.name: Sanchuniathon & Bar Hebraeus Synchronisms: Chrysor/Vulcan (= Tubal-Cain), Misor (= Mizraim), Chna (= Canaan) & 10 Chaldean Kings (Aloros → Ksisothros = Noah)
nodes.era: Antediluvian Comparative Chronology (Jackson 1752 p. 207; Bar Hebraeus p. 6)
nodes.role: Phoenician & Syriac Synchronizations Anchored to Adam & Noah
nodes.notes: John Jackson (1752) aligns Sanchuniathon's Phoenician line (Chrysor/Vulcan = Tubal-Cain in the exact 7th descent from Adam; Misor = Mizraim; Chna = Canaan), while Bar Hebraeus p. 6 preserves the 10 Chaldean kings from Aloros to Ksisothros (= Noah).

nodes.name: Berr → Bernes (Branes: Sanhaja, Masmuda, Kutama, Auréba) & Madghis al-Abtar (Botr: Zenata, Luwata, Hawwara)
nodes.era: Maghreb Tribal Origins (Ibn Khaldun Vol. 3 pp. 189-191)
nodes.role: Two Great Amazigh Branches Descended from Canaan b. Ham / Mazigh
sources: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berbères Vol. 1, 3 & 4
nodes.notes: Ibn Khaldun transmits the Berber genealogies dividing the Imazighen into the Branes (Sanhaja, Masmuda, Kutama, Auréba) and Botr / Madghis al-Abtar (Zenata, Luwata, Hawwara, Nefzaoua), explicitly preserving Ibn Hazm's chain tracing Madghis through Ber -> Herik -> Bedian -> Canaan -> Ham -> Noah.

nodes.name: Koceila (Auréba) & Queen al-Kahina / Dihya (Jerawa Zenata, 7th c. CE)
nodes.role: Sovereign Amazigh Leaders Descended from Branes & Botr
sources: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berbères Vol. 3 p. 193
nodes.notes: Koceila (leader of the Branes Auréba) and Queen al-Kahina / Dihya (queen of the Botr Jerawa Zenata confederation) led the Amazigh resistance across North Africa.

nodes.name: Nubians (Nuba) & Beja (Blemmyes) — Christian Kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria & Alodia
nodes.era: Ancient to Medieval Sudan (MacMichael Vol. 1 pp. 12-51; Arkell)
nodes.role: Cushitic/Nubian Lineages of the Middle Nile
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan pp. 12-51
nodes.notes: Documents the pre-Islamic Cushite/Nubian and Beja populations (Blemmyes) of Northern Sudan who formed the Christian kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria (Dongola) & Alodia (Soba).

nodes.name: Ja'aliyyin Confederation of Sudan (Descent from al-'Abbas b. 'Abd al-Muttalib → Ishmael)
nodes.role: Sudanese 'Abbasid Nisba Lineages Blended with Nubia
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan Vol. 1 pp. xi, 131-195
nodes.notes: MacMichael catalogs dozens of Sudanese Arab nisba manuscripts uniting the Ja'aliyyin, Danagla, Shayqiya, Batahin & Rubatab via Ibrahim Ja'al back to al-'Abbas, uncle of Prophet Muhammad (Quraysh/Ishmael), while intermarrying with Nubian princesses.

nodes.name: Juhayna (Guhayna), Baqqara, Kababish & Shukriya of Sudan & Kordofan (Qahtan / Joktan Line)
nodes.role: Yemenite Qahtanite Migrations via Egypt & Red Sea into Sudan
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan pp. 131, 271-319
nodes.notes: Sudanese chronicles trace the Juhayna/Guhayna confederation (Baqqara, Kababish, Shukriya, Hamar, Rizayqat) back to southern Arabian Himyar & Qahtan (Joktan), migrating through Egypt and the Red Sea into Kordofan & Darfur.

nodes.name: Funj Sultanate of Sennar (1504–1821 CE — Umayyad / Nubian Pedigree)
nodes.role: Black Sultanate of Sudan Linking Umayyad & Nubian Royal Traditions
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan
nodes.notes: Amara Dunqas founded the Funj Sultanate at Sennar in 1504 CE; Funj royal genealogies claimed descent from Umayyad refugees passing through Abyssinia and Nubia.

nodes.name: 'Abur (Amur) b. Japheth → Yarej → Na'ur → Lotsatis (1st King of China at Anku)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Eastern Dispersion (Al-Mas'udi Vol. I pp. 312-313)
nodes.role: Classical Arabic Japhethic Ancestry of the Early Sovereigns of China
sources: Al-Mas'udi Meadows of Gold Vol. I pp. 312-313
nodes.notes: Al-Mas'udi explicitly derives the Chinese sovereigns from Japheth b. Noah: 'The majority of the children of Abur followed the course of the river to the extremity of China... Their first king in this new settlement was Lotsatis ben Na'ur ben Yarej ben Abur ben Yafeth ben Nuh' at Anku.

nodes.name: 'Arun → 'Abirun → 'Athinan → Jaraban (Early Noahic Chinese Monarchs of Mas'udi)
nodes.role: Early Chinese Dynasty in Al-Mas'udi's Universal Chronicle
sources: Al-Mas'udi Meadows of Gold Vol. I pp. 313-317
nodes.notes: Al-Mas'udi continues Lotsatis's lineage through 'Arun, 'Abirun, 'Athinan (bordering the Turks, descendants of his uncle), Jaraban (who sent ships to India & Babylon) & his temple-building lawgiver successor.

nodes.name: Hind & Sind (Progenitors of India & Sindh in Tabari & Mas'udi)
nodes.era: Post-Flood South Asia (Al-Tabari Vol. 2 pp. 15-17; Al-Mas'udi)
nodes.role: Noahic Anchors of India & Sindh via Ham (Cush) and Shem (Joktan)
nodes.notes: Al-Tabari records both major traditions linking India to Noah: (1) Indians & Sindis descending from Ham -> Cush/Canaan (p. 15), and (2) Ibn 'Abbas & Hisham al-Kalbi's line Shem -> Arphaxad -> Shelah -> Eber -> Qahtan (Joktan) -> Buqayin, father of Hind & Sind (p. 17).

nodes.name: King Mahāsammata (= Manu) → Okkaka (= Ikshvaku) → Śākya Royal Stem
nodes.era: Pali & Buddhist Royal Stem (Mahavamsa Ch. II p. 80)
nodes.role: Solar-Buddhist Dynastic Bridge Linking India, Sri Lanka, Burma & Tibet
nodes.notes: The Pali Mahavamsa opens its royal pedigree with first elected king Mahāsammata (cognate of Manu) -> Roja -> Mandhatar -> Okkaka (Pali form of Solar Dynasty founder Ikshvaku!) -> the Śākya clan of Kapilavastu.

nodes.name: Kashmir Kings (Kalhana's Rajatarangini): Gonanda I (Kurukshetra) → Ashoka of Kashmir
nodes.era: Kurukshetra to 3rd c. BCE (Kalhana's Rajatarangini Book I)
nodes.role: Historical Kashmiri Dynasty Synchronized with Pandavas & Emperor Ashoka
nodes.notes: Kalhana's Rajatarangini begins Kashmir's royal chronology at the Kurukshetra War under Gonanda I (contemporary of the Pandavas) and directly includes Emperor Ashoka (who exchanged envoys with Ptolemy II of Egypt!).

nodes.name: Sri Lanka (Mahavamsa): Prince Vijaya (1st King of Lanka, 543 BCE) & Thera Mahinda (Son of Ashoka)
nodes.role: Founding Sinhalese Dynasty & Mauryan Buddhist Mission to Lanka
nodes.notes: The Mahavamsa connects Sri Lanka's first monarch Vijaya (landing on the exact day of Buddha's Parinirvana) -> Devanampiya Tissa with Emperor Ashoka's own son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta.

nodes.name: Burma (Glass Palace Chronicle): King Abhiraza (Śākya Prince of Kapilavastu → Founder of Tagaung)
nodes.role: Burmese Royal Origin Descended from Mahāsammata & Okkaka / Śākya
sources: Glass Palace Chronicle of the Kings of Burma (Pe Maung Tin & Luce)
nodes.notes: The Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle) traces the founding kings of Burma to Śākya prince Abhiraza, descendant of Mahāsammata and Okkaka (Ikshvaku), who marched from northern India to build Tagaung.

nodes.name: Tibet (The Blue Annals): Nyatri Tsenpo (1st Yarlung King, Śākya/Licchavi Stem) → Songtsen Gampo
nodes.era: Ancient Yarlung to 7th c. CE (Roerich The Blue Annals Book I)
nodes.role: Tibetan Royal Lineage Derived from India's Śākya / Licchavi House
sources: The Blue Annals (Deb-ther sngon-po, George Roerich tr., Book I)
nodes.notes: 'Gos Lo-tsā-ba's Blue Annals Book I opens the Royal Chronicle of Tibet with the Indian Śākya/Licchavi origin of Tibet's first king Nyatri Tsenpo (gNya'-khri btsan-po) descending to Buddhist unifier Songtsen Gampo.

nodes.name: Abulghazi's 8 Sons of Japheth: Turk, Chars (Khazars), Sacklap (Slavs), Russ (Russians), Maninach, Zwin (China), Camari (Gomer) & Tarich (Tiras)
nodes.role: Japhethic Progenitors of Turks, Khazars, Slavs, Russians, China & Steppe Nations
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks p. 62
nodes.notes: Abulghazi explicitly names eight sons of Japheth (Japhis) sent northward across Eurasia after Noah's Flood: 1. Turk (Japhis-Oglany), 2. Chars (Khazars), 3. Sacklap (Slavs), 4. Russ (Russians), 5. Maninach, 6. Zwin (Chin / Chinese), 7. Camari (Gomer / Cimmerians), and 8. Tarich (Tiras).

nodes.name: Turk (Japhis-Oglany) → Taunak → Ilchi → Dib Bakuy → Kayuk → Alanja Khan
nodes.role: Patrilineal Descent from Japheth's Eldest Son Turk to Alanja Khan
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks pp. 62-66
nodes.notes: Turk (Japhis-Oglany, founder of laws and tents near Issyk-Kul) fathered four sons — Taunak, Zakale, Bersazar, and Amlak — continuing from Taunak through Ilchi Khan, Dib Bakuy Khan, and Kayuk Khan to Alanja Khan.

nodes.name: Twin Sons of Alanja: Tatar Khan (7 Gens → Siuntz) & Mogul (Mung'l) Khan → Kara Khan
nodes.role: Twin Progenitors of the Tatar and Mongol Branches
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks pp. 66-69
nodes.notes: Alanja Khan divided his dominions between his twin sons: Tatar Khan (whose seven-generation line ran Bucha -> Jalanza -> Ettela -> Attaisir -> Orda -> Baydu -> Siuntz) and Mogul (Mung'l) Khan (father of Cara/Kara, Auwas, Cauwas, and Cavar).

nodes.name: Oghuz Khan's Monotheistic Restoration & Steppe Nations (Uighurs, Kanglis, Kipchaks, Karluks & 24 Oghuz Tribes)
nodes.role: Unifier of the Steppe, Conqueror of Kitay & Khorasan, Ancestor of the 24 Oghuz Tribes
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks pp. 69-82
nodes.notes: Oghuz Khan restored the worship of one God against his father Kara Khan and his Tatar kinsmen, conquering Tangut, Kitay (China), and Khorasan (Iran) following the death of Gayomart. His six sons (Buzuk Golden Bow: Kun, Ay, Yildiz; Uch-Ok Three Arrows: Kuk, Tag, Tengiz) sired the 24 Oghuz tribes alongside the Uighurs, Kanglis, Kipchaks, and Karluks.

nodes.name: Il Khan → Qiyan & Nukuz (Ergenekon / Irgana-kon) → Bertezena (Börte Čino) → Alan Qo'a → Dutumin → Kaidu → Tumana → Kabul → Bortan → Yesugei
nodes.era: Ergenekon Refuge to 12th c. CE (Abulghazi pp. 82-120)
nodes.role: Restoration from the Ergenekon Valley to the Borjigin Forefathers of Genghis Khan
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks pp. 82-120
nodes.notes: After the defeat of Il Khan, survivors Qiyan and Nukuz took refuge in the enclosed valley of Ergenekon (Irgana-kon) for generations until Bertezena (Börte Čino) led the Mongols back out onto the steppe, continuing through Alan Qo'a, Dutumin, Kaidu, Tumana, Kabul, Bortan, and Yesugei.

nodes.name: Seljuk Empire: Seljuk → Mikail → Tughril Beg (Tangrolipix, 1030) → Alp Arslan → Malik Shah → Kilij Arslan
nodes.era: 11th–12th c. CE (Knolles Vol. 1 pp. 2-15; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 2)
nodes.role: Oghuz-Seljuk Sultans of Persia, Baghdad & Anatolia
sources: Knolles & Rycaut The Turkish History Vol. 1 pp. 2-15
nodes.notes: Knolles traces the Turks from Scythia (Tanais/Caucasus, Magog horizon) into Turcomania and Armenia, rising under Seljuk and Mikail to Tughril Beg (Tangrolipix, crowned in Persia c. 1030), Alp Arslan, Malik Shah, and the Seljuks of Rum under Kilij Arslan.

nodes.name: Ottoman Founders: Süleyman Shah → Ertuğrul → Sultan Osman I (1299) → Orhan → Murad I → Bayezid I
nodes.role: Kayi-Oghuz Founders of the Ottoman Dynasty
sources: Knolles & Rycaut The Turkish History Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Ascending from the Oghuz Kayi branch in the wake of the Seljuk disintegration, Süleyman Shah and Ertuğrul settled in Bithynia, where Osman I proclaimed sovereign rule in 1299 CE and was succeeded by Orhan, Murad I, and Bayezid I.

nodes.name: Imperial Ottomans: Mehmed II the Conqueror (1453) → Bayezid II → Selim I → Suleiman the Magnificent (1520–1566)
nodes.role: Ottoman Sultans from the Conquest of Constantinople to Imperial Zenith
sources: Knolles & Rycaut The Turkish History Vols. 1-3
nodes.notes: Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 (ending the Byzantine Palaiologos line), followed by Bayezid II, Selim I (adding Egypt and the Hejaz), and Suleiman the Magnificent.

nodes.name: Jochi (Zuzi Chan) → Batu Sagin Chan (Golden Horde) & Berke (Burga) Khan
nodes.role: Ulus of Jochi & Rulers of the Kipchak Steppe / Golden Horde
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks Part V
nodes.notes: Abulghazi details the lineage of Genghis Khan's eldest son Jochi (Zuzi Chan) into the Golden Horde under Batu Sagin Chan and Berke (Burga) Khan across the Kipchak Steppe and Volga.

nodes.name: Shaybanid Uzbeks of Bukhara & Khwarazm: Shaybani Khan → Muhammad Shaybani (Shah Bakht) → Ilbars → Abulghazi Bahadur Khan (1603–1663)
nodes.role: Genghisid Shaybanid Khans of Bukhara & Khwarazm (Author's Own Royal Pedigree)
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks Parts VII-IX
nodes.notes: Through Jochi's fifth son Shaybani Khan, Abulghazi traces the Uzbek khans — including Muhammad Shaybani (Shah Bakht) and Ilbars Khan of Khwarazm — directly down to himself, Khan of Khiva and chronicler of the Shajara-i Turk (1603-1663).

nodes.name: Togai Timur → Crimean Khans (Caffa & Crim) & Kazakh Khans (Janibek Khan → Kasim Khan)
nodes.role: Tuka-Timurid Lines of Jochi Ruling Crimea & the Kazakh Steppe
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks pp. 252-259
nodes.notes: Abulghazi chronicles Jochi's son Togai Timur as progenitor both of the Crimean Khans (Caffa and Crim) and of the Kazakh Khans led by Janibek Khan and Kasim Khan.

nodes.name: Chagatai Khanate & Timurids: Buga Timur → Tarmashirin; Amir Timur (Tamerlane, 1370) → Shah Rukh → Ulugh Beg
nodes.era: 13th–15th c. CE (Abulghazi p. 12; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 3)
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks p. 12
nodes.notes: Traces the house of Chagatai (Zagatai Chan) in Transoxiana and Kashgar through Buga Timur and Tarmashirin, alongside Barlas conqueror Amir Timur (Tamerlane, son-in-law/Guregen of the Chagatayids) -> Shah Rukh -> astronomer-king Ulugh Beg at Samarkand.

nodes.name: Mughal Empire of Hindustan: Zahir-ud-din Babur (1526, Timurid-Genghisid Line) → Emperor Humayun
nodes.era: 1526–1556 CE (Abulghazi p. 296; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 3)
nodes.role: Founders of the Mughal Empire in Northern India
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks p. 296
nodes.notes: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur — descended paternally from Timur and maternally from Genghis Khan via Chagatai — established the Mughal Empire in India in 1526 and was succeeded by Emperor Humayun.

nodes.name: Great Mughals of Delhi & Agra: Akbar the Great → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 3 (History of Hindustan)
nodes.notes: Continuous Mughal imperial succession in Modern Universal History Vol. 3 from Akbar the Great through Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb.

nodes.name: Ilkhanate of Persia: Tolui → Hulagu (Halaku) Khan (1256) → Abaqa → Ghazan Khan
nodes.era: 1256–1304 CE (Abulghazi p. 240; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 2)
sources: Abulghazi Bahadur Khan General History of the Turks p. 240
nodes.notes: Tolui's son Hulagu (Halaku) Khan founded the Ilkhanate across Persia and Iraq in 1256, continuing through Abaqa Khan and Islamizing reformer Ghazan Khan.

nodes.name: Manchu / Qing Tartar Unification of China, Tartary, Korea & Tibet: Nurhaci (Tianming) → Hong Taiji (Tsong-te) → Shunzhi (1644) → Kangxi Emperor
nodes.era: 1616–1722 CE (Du Halde 1738 Vol. 1 Preface & p. 239; Compleat Universal History)
nodes.role: Qing Dynasty Uniting China Proper, Great Tartary, Korea & Tibet
sources: Jean-Baptiste Du Halde Description of China and Chinese-Tartary (1738 Vol. 1 Preface & p. 239)
nodes.notes: Du Halde (1738 Vol. 1 Preface & p. 239) and A Compleat Universal History document the Ming-to-Qing transition under Jurchen/Manchu Tartar founders Nurhaci (Tianming) and Hong Taiji (Tsong-te) -> Shunzhi (Shun-chi, 1644) -> Kangxi (Kang-hi), uniting China, Inner/Outer Tartary, Korea, and Tibet.

nodes.name: Ancient Germanic Nations (Mascou 1737 & Tacitus): Cimbri & Teutones, Suevi, Alemanni, Saxons, Franks, Vandals (Gaiseric) & Lombards (Alboin)
nodes.era: 3rd c. BCE – 6th c. CE (J.J. Mascou 1737; Tacitus Germania)
nodes.role: Early Germanic Tribal Confederations Rooted in Tuisto / Mannus / Ashkenaz
sources: John Jacob Mascou History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Mascou traces the major Germanic confederations from Tacitus's Tuisto and Mannus (linked in universal chronologies to Ashkenaz/Gomer) through the Cimbri & Teutones, Suevi, Alemanni, Saxons, Franks, Vandals (Gaiseric), and Lombards (Alboin).

nodes.name: Kingdom of Burgundy: King Gonderic → King Gundobad (Burgundian Law) → King Sigismund
nodes.era: 5th–6th c. CE (Mascou 1737; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14)
nodes.role: Burgundian Royal House of the Rhone & Geneva
sources: John Jacob Mascou History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
nodes.notes: Mascou and Modern Universal History Vol. 14 trace the Burgundian kings from Gonderic and Gundobad (codifier of Lex Burgundionum) to St. Sigismund before Frankish absorption and the later Kingdom of Burgundy/Arles.

nodes.name: House of Savoy & Sardinia: Duke Witichind of Saxony (Contemp. of Charlemagne) → Bertold → Hubert of the White Hands → Amadeo → King Victor Amadeus I & II
nodes.era: 8th–18th c. CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14 pp. 125-140)
nodes.role: Ducal House of Savoy & Royal House of Sardinia
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14 p. 125 derives the House of Savoy from Saxony's Duke Witichind (contemporary of Charlemagne) via Bertold (who received Savoy from Rodolf of Burgundy) and Hubert with the White Hands (d. c. 1050) to Amadeo and King Victor Amadeus II.

nodes.name: Capetian Kings of France: Hugh Capet (987 CE) → Henry I (+ Anne of Kiev!) → Philip II Augustus → St. Louis IX
nodes.role: Direct Capetian Dynasty Bridging Kievan Rus' & Western Europe
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 9 (History of France)
nodes.notes: Hugh Capet (crowned 987 CE) founded the Capetian line; King Henry I married Yaroslav the Wise's daughter Anne of Kiev, uniting Rurikid Rus' and France through Philip II Augustus and St. Louis IX.

nodes.name: Valois & Bourbon Kings of France: Philip VI → Francis I → Henry IV of Navarre (Bourbon, 1589) → Louis XIII → Louis XIV
nodes.role: Cadet Capetian Royal Houses of Valois & Bourbon
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 9 (History of France)
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 9 traces the Capetian cadet successions from Philip VI of Valois and Francis I to Henry IV of Navarre (first Bourbon King of France, 1589), Louis XIII, and Louis XIV.

nodes.name: Roman, British & Danish Rulers in Britain (Howell 1685): Julius Caesar → Claudius → King Lucius → King Canute (Cnut)
nodes.role: Roman Imperial Governors, British Kings & Danish Crown in England
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Howell (1685) opens the English monarchy with Julius Caesar and Claudius, Christian British king Lucius, the Saxon Heptarchy unified under Egbert and Alfred the Great, and the Danish conquest under Canute (Cnut).

nodes.name: House of Plantagenet (England): Henry II → Richard I Lionheart → King John → Edward I → Edward III → Henry V
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Ascending from the Anglo-Norman & Wessex heritage via Empress Matilda, Henry II inaugurated the Plantagenet line leading through Richard I, King John, Edward I, Edward III, and Henry V.

nodes.name: House of Tudor (Welsh-English Royal Union): Owen Tudor → Henry VII (1485) → Henry VIII → Edward VI → Queen Elizabeth I
nodes.role: Tudor Sovereigns Linking Welsh Princes & English Crown
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Owen Tudor's grandson Henry VII (uniting Lancaster and York at Bosworth Field, 1485) brought Welsh royal pedigree onto the English throne through Henry VIII, Edward VI, and Elizabeth I.

nodes.name: House of Stuart (Union of Scotland & England): King James VI & I (1603) → Charles I → Charles II → James II
nodes.era: 1603–1688 CE (William Howell 1685; Raleigh 1736 Preface p. ix)
nodes.role: Unified Crown of Great Britain (Scottish Milesian & English Tudor Union)
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Preface p. ix)
nodes.notes: Descended both from Scottish Dal Riada (Fergus Mor & Kenneth MacAlpin) and from Henry VII's daughter Margaret Tudor, King James VI of Scotland became James I of Great Britain in 1603 (celebrated in Raleigh's 1736 Preface p. ix), continuing through Charles I, Charles II, and James II.

nodes.name: Foundation of Portugal: Alfonso VI of Castile + Teresa & Count Henry of Burgundy → King Afonso I Henriques (1139, Battle of Ourique)
nodes.role: Burgundian-Capetian Founder of the Kingdom of Portugal
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
nodes.notes: Connecting Iberian monarchy (Tubal/Spain -> Castile) with the Capetian House of Burgundy: Count Henry of Burgundy married Alfonso VI's daughter Teresa, and their son Afonso I Henriques won independence at the Battle of Ourique (1139).

nodes.name: House of Aviz & Portuguese Asia: King John I → Prince Henry the Navigator → King Manuel I (Vasco da Gama to India, 1498)
nodes.era: 1385–1580 CE (History of Portugal 1661/1726; The Portuguese Asia)
nodes.role: Aviz Dynasty & Oceanic Sea Route to East Africa & India
sources: Faria y Sousa The Portuguese Asia
nodes.notes: King John I of Aviz (son-in-law of John of Gaunt / Plantagenet) and Prince Henry the Navigator launched the Atlantic voyages culminating under King Manuel I in Vasco da Gama's 1498 voyage to India.

nodes.name: House of Braganza (Portuguese Restoration): King John IV (1640) → King Afonso VI (1656) → Peter II
sources: A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
nodes.notes: John, Duke of Braganza (descending from Afonso, son of King John I of Aviz), restored Portuguese independence as King John IV in 1640, succeeded by Afonso VI and Peter II.

nodes.name: Grand Princes & Tsars of Muscovy: St. Alexander Nevsky → Ivan III the Great (1480) → Tsar Ivan IV the Terrible
nodes.era: 1221–1584 CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13: History of Russia)
nodes.role: Rurikid Grand Princes of Vladimir-Moscow & First Tsar of All Russia
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 13 (History of Russia)
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13 continues the Rurikid lineage from Yaroslav the Wise via St. Alexander Nevsky and Ivan III the Great (who ended Golden Horde tribute at the Ugra in 1480) to Tsar Ivan IV the Terrible.

nodes.name: House of Romanov (Russian Empire): Tsar Michael I Romanov (1613) → Alexis I → Emperor Peter the Great (1682–1725)
nodes.era: 1613–1725 CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13: History of Russia)
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 13 (History of Russia)
nodes.notes: Connected to the Rurikids through Tsar Ivan IV's marriage to Anastasia Romanovna, the House of Romanov ascended in 1613 under Michael I, continuing via Alexis I to Emperor Peter the Great.

nodes.name: Raleigh & Methodius's 3 Post-Flood Leaders: Nimrod (Ham), Joktan (Shem) & Suphene (Japheth)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Dispersion (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69; Petavius 1659)
nodes.role: Tripartite Dispersion Commanders of Ham, Shem & Japheth
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69)
nodes.notes: Sir Walter Raleigh (citing Methodius of Tyre) records the three post-Flood commanders who led the peoples after Babel: Nimrod over Ham's line, Joktan over Shem's line, and Suphene over Japheth's line — framed within Petavius's universal chronology from Creation.

nodes.name: Raleigh's Shemite Plantation of the East Indies: Joktan, Havilah & Ophir
nodes.era: Eastward Dispersion (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
nodes.role: Biblical Shemite Pioneers of India & the East Indies
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Engraved Noahic Map)
nodes.notes: Raleigh argues at length in Book I Ch. VIII (and marks on his engraved dispersion map) that Joktan's descendants Havilah and Ophir planted the regions stretching across Persia and India / the East Indies.

nodes.name: Raleigh's Cushite Arabia the Happy: Seba, Sabtah & Raamah (Sabe Regia & Aden)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Arabia (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
nodes.notes: Raleigh maps Cush's sons Seba, Sabtah, and Raamah (Rhegma) directly along the coasts and cities of Arabia the Happy (Arabia Felix), including Sabe Regia and Aden.

nodes.name: Cato's Scythia Saga (Raleigh p. 69): Post-Flood Scythians → Galli (Gauls) & Italian Umbri
nodes.role: Classical Witness to mankind's Post-Flood Restoration via Scythia & Italy
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69, citing Cato)
nodes.notes: Raleigh quotes Cato (Fragments) that after mankind was restored following the Deluge, populations spread from Scythia Saga into the Galli (Gauls) and ancient Umbri of Italy.

nodes.name: Gautruche's Poetical History Cognates: Golden Age (Saturn/Janus = Noah), Silver Age (Jupiter = Ham), Brazen Age (Nimrod), Vulcan (= Tubal-Cain) & Apollo (= Jubal)
nodes.role: Systematic Identification of Greco-Roman Mythic Figures with Genesis Patriarchs
nodes.notes: Gautruche translates Greco-Roman mythology back into Biblical history: the Golden Age under Saturn/Janus corresponds to Noah (threefold division of the world), the Silver Age to Jupiter (Ham/Cham), the Brazen Age to Nimrod, Vulcan to metal-worker Tubal-Cain, and Apollo to musician Jubal.

nodes.name: The Parian Chronicle (264 BCE Marble) & Lucian: Epoch 1 Cecrops (1582 BCE) & Epoch 2 Deucalion's Flood (1529 BCE)
nodes.era: 264 BCE Greek Inscription (The Parian Chronicle 1788 pp. 1-5; Lucian De Dea Syria)
nodes.role: Epigraphic Greek Chronicle & Syrian Flood Witness
sources: The Parian Chronicle or Chronicle of the Arundelian Marbles (1788 pp. 1-5)
nodes.notes: Inscribed in marble on Paros in 264 BCE, the Parian Chronicle anchors Greek chronology at Epoch 1 (Cecrops, first king of Athens, 1582 BCE) and Epoch 2 (Deucalion escaping the Great Flood to Athens from Parnassus, 1529 BCE), paired with Lucian's De Dea Syria preserving the Near Eastern Deluge tradition under Deucalion's name.

nodes.name: Classical Persian-Greek Bridge (Xenophon, Curtius Rufus & Plutarch): Artaxerxes II Mnemon, Cyrus the Younger (401 BCE) & Darius III
nodes.role: Late Achaemenid Emperors Leading to Alexander the Great
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus History of Alexander
nodes.notes: Documented across Xenophon's Anabasis (Cyrus the Younger vs. his brother Artaxerxes II at Cunaxa, 401 BCE), Plutarch, and Curtius Rufus down to Darius III and Alexander the Great.

nodes.name: Classical Roman Imperial Spine (Livy, Tacitus, Echard 5 Vols., Ammianus & Mexía): Vespasian & Titus (70 CE) → Trajan → Marcus Aurelius → Diocletian → Romulus Augustulus (476 CE)
nodes.era: 69–476 CE (Echard Vols. 2-4; Tacitus; Ammianus Marcellinus; Mexía)
nodes.role: Flavians, Five Good Emperors, Tetrarchy & Western Roman Finale
nodes.notes: Synthesizes the Roman imperial succession across Echard's 5-volume Roman History, Tacitus, Ammianus Marcellinus, Florus, Aurelius Victor, and Mexía from Vespasian & Titus through Trajan, Marcus Aurelius, Diocletian, and Romulus Augustulus (476 CE) to Charlemagne (Echard Vol. 5).

nodes.name: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (Vincent 1800): King Zoscales of Aksum, Saba/Sheba, Ophir & Red Sea–India Corridor
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (William Vincent Periplus of the Erythrean Sea, 1800)
nodes.role: Classical Greco-Egyptian Maritime Bridge Linking Aksum, Sheba, Arabia & India
sources: William Vincent The Periplus of the Erythrean Sea (1800)
nodes.notes: Vincent's scholarly commentary identifies King Zoscales of Aksum (Adulis, 1st c. CE), maps classical Saba/Mariaba to Biblical Sheba, examines the Ophir trade corridor, and documents direct monsoon voyages linking Ethiopia and Arabia to western India.

nodes.name: Za-Al-Ayaman ('Came from Yemen' → Kukya on the Niger) → 14 Pre-Islamic Za Kings → Za-Kosoi (1st Muslim King of Songhai, 1009 CE)
nodes.era: Early Niger Bend → 1010 CE (Tarikh es-Soudan Ch. 1 pp. 35-38)
nodes.role: Yemeni-Originated Founder of the Songhai Za Dynasty on the Niger
sources: Abderrahman es-Sa'di Tarikh es-Soudan (tr. Houdas 1900) Ch. 1 pp. 35-38
nodes.notes: Tarikh es-Soudan derives the royal Za (Dia) dynasty of Kukya/Songhai from two brothers who traveled from Yemen ('dja men el-Yemen' -> Za-Al-Ayaman), slaying the pagan river-idol and ruling through 14 pre-Islamic kings until Za-Kosoi (Moslem-dam) embraced Islam in AH 400 (1009-1010 CE).

nodes.name: Songhai Empire & Timbuktu: Sonni Ali-Kolon → Sonni Ali (1464) → Askia El-Hadj Mohammed (Askia the Great, 1493)
nodes.role: Imperial Sultans of Gao & Timbuktu Following Mali Supremacy
sources: Abderrahman es-Sa'di Tarikh es-Soudan (tr. Houdas 1900) Ch. 2-3 pp. 39-44
nodes.notes: Brothers Ali-Kolon and Selman-Nar (sons of Za-Yasiboy) freed Songhai from Mansa Musa's Mali suzerainty, inaugurating the Sonni line culminating in Sonni Ali before Askia El-Hadj Mohammed (the Great, 1493) elevated Timbuktu and Songhai.

nodes.name: Futuh Misr (Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam): 'Amr ibn al-'As (Egypt), Uqba ibn Nafi (Maghreb) & Tariq ibn Ziyad (Al-Andalus, 711 CE)
nodes.era: 7th–8th c. CE (Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam Futuh Misr, Torrey ed.)
nodes.role: Earliest Arabic Chronicle of Egypt, Berbers of North Africa & Al-Andalus
sources: Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam Futuh Misr (ed. C.C. Torrey, Yale Oriental Series III)
nodes.notes: Earliest extant Arabic historical narrative covering 'Amr ibn al-'As's Coptic treaty in Egypt (Misr), Uqba ibn Nafi's campaigns across the Amazigh/Berber Maghreb, and Tariq ibn Ziyad & Musa ibn Nusayr's 711 CE crossing into Visigothic Spain.

nodes.name: Ancient Arabian Ariba (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1): Cushites of Arabia, 'Ad (Loqman) & Amaliqa / Samayda of Ayla
nodes.era: Pre-Islamic Antiquity (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1 pp. 21-39)
nodes.role: Extinct Ancient Arabian Tribes Bridged to Cush, Uz/Aram & Ham
sources: Caussin de Perceval Essai sur l'Histoire des Arabes Vol. 1 (1847) pp. 21-39
nodes.notes: Caussin de Perceval synthesizes Jewish and classical Arab genealogies (Ibn Sa'id, Ibn Habib, Tabari) tracing the primitive Arab al-'Ariba — Cushites along the Arabian peninsula, 'Ad (Uz b. Aram / Amalek b. Ham, including Loqman of the Seven Vultures), and the Samayda Amaliqa of Ayla.

nodes.name: Pre-Islamic Arabian Tribal Tree (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1): Qahtan (Himyar, Kahlan, Azd, Kindah) & Adnan (Ma'add → Nizar → Mudar & Rabi'a)
nodes.era: Bronze Age → 6th c. CE (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1 pp. 23-39+)
nodes.role: Complete Bifurcation of Southern Qahtanite & Northern Adnanite Arab Confederations
sources: Caussin de Perceval Essai sur l'Histoire des Arabes Vol. 1 (1847) pp. 23-39+
nodes.notes: Maps the dual trunk of Arabian ethnogenesis: Southern Al-'Ariba / Mutariba descending from Qahtan (Joktan b. Eber -> Ya'rub -> Himyar, Kahlan, Azd, Ghassan, Lakhm & Kindah) and Northern Musta'riba descending from Ishmael via Adnan -> Ma'add -> Nizar -> Mudar & Rabi'a.

nodes.name: Ludolf's Ethiopian-Himyarite War (1684): King Kaleb (Elesbaan) vs. Dhu Nuwas, Abreha & Saif ibn Dhi Yazan (+ Khosrow I Anushirvan)
sources: Hiob Ludolf A New History of Ethiopia (1684) pp. 166-167
nodes.notes: Ludolf chronicles King Kaleb (Caleb / Elesbaan) of Aksum avenging the Christian martyrs of Najran against Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas, placing Abreha in Yemen until Himyarite prince Saif ibn Dhi Yazan regained Yemen with Sasanian Emperor Khosrow I Anushirvan's aid.

nodes.name: Gondar Solomonic Emperors (Ludolf 1684): Lebna Dengel → Galawdewos → Emperor Susenyos → Emperor Fasilides (Founder of Gondar, 1632)
nodes.role: Renaissance & Early Modern Ethiopian Solomonic Sovereign Succession
sources: Hiob Ludolf A New History of Ethiopia (1684)
nodes.notes: Continues the Ethiopian Solomonic line documented in Ludolf's 1684 chronicle from Lebna Dengel (Dawit II) and Galawdewos (Claudius) through Emperor Susenyos I and his son Emperor Fasilides, who established the royal capital at Gondar in 1632.

nodes.name: Palmyra / Tadmor (Seller 1696): Founded by King Solomon → Nabataean King Aretas (Al-Harith of Ghassan / Petra)
nodes.role: Solomonic Foundation of Tadmor & Arab-Nabataean Princes of Syria
sources: Abednego Seller The Antiquities of Palmyra (1696) Preface
nodes.notes: Seller (1696) links ancient Palmyra directly to Biblical Tadmor fortified by King Solomon in the Syrian desert, tracing subsequent Arabian mastery from Nabataean king Aretas (equated by Seller with the Al-Harith rulers of Petra and Ghassan, contemporary of Pompey c. 63 BCE).

nodes.name: Palmyrene Empire (Seller 1696): King Odenathus → Queen Zenobia (Claiming Descent from Cleopatra VII & Dido) & Vaballathus
nodes.role: Palmyrene Imperial House Claiming Ptolemaic & Phoenician Royal Bloodlines
sources: Abednego Seller The Antiquities of Palmyra (1696)
nodes.notes: Seller details the rise of Palmyra under Septimius Odaenathus ('King of Kings') and his learned queen Zenobia Bat-Zabbai — who claimed royal ancestry from Egypt's Cleopatra VII and Carthaginian Dido while ruling Syria, Egypt & Anatolia before Aurelian's triumph.

nodes.name: Mariana's General History of Spain (1699 Book I Ch. I): Tubal (5th Son of Japheth, 131 yrs after Flood) → Ancient Kings of Spain
nodes.era: Post-Flood Dispersion (Mariana 1699 Book I Ch. I p. 1)
nodes.role: Spaniards Traced Directly from Tubal, 5th Son of Japheth
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (tr. Stevens 1699) Book I Ch. I p. 1
nodes.notes: Mariana opens his monumental history of Spain (p. 1): 'Tubal, the son of Japheth, was the first man that peopled Spain after the Flood... the 5th son of Japheth, was sent to the farthest regions westward, that is, to Spain, where he founded the Spanish monarchy.'

nodes.name: Visigothic Kingdom of Spain (Mariana 1699): Ataulf → Leovigild → King Reccared I (589 CE) → King Roderick (711 CE)
nodes.role: Gothic Sovereigns of Hispania Bridged to Islamic Al-Andalus
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Traces Visigothic Hispania from Alaric's successor Ataulf and Toledo unifier Leovigild to King Reccared I (589 CE) and last Visigothic king Roderick (711 CE).

nodes.name: Reconquista Spain (Mariana 1699): Don Pelayo of Asturias (718) → Alfonso VI of Castile & Leon → Ferdinand III & James I of Aragon
nodes.role: Asturian, Castilian, Leonese & Aragonese Christian Crowns
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Follows the Christian continuity from Don Pelayo at Covadonga (718 CE) through Alfonso VI of Castile and Leon (father-in-law of Count Henry of Burgundy/Portugal), St. Ferdinand III, and James I the Conqueror of Aragon.

nodes.name: Unified Catholic & Habsburg Spain (Mariana 1699): Ferdinand of Aragon & Isabella of Castile (1492) → Emperor Charles V → King Philip II
nodes.role: Unifiers of Aragon & Castile and Spanish Habsburg Dynasty
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Unites Castile and Aragon under Ferdinand II and Isabella I (1492), continuing through Joanna the Mad and Philip the Handsome to Emperor Charles V (Charles I of Spain) and King Philip II.

nodes.name: Aylett Sammes's Phoenician Britain (1676): Tyre & Sidon Tin Trade ('Bratanac') + Cimmerian / Gomerite Britons
nodes.role: Phoenician & Cimmerian-Gomerite Origin of Ancient Britain
sources: Aylett Sammes Antiquities of Ancient Britain (1676) p. 2
nodes.notes: Sammes rejects later fables in favor of classical Phoenician sources, arguing that Phoenician navigators from Sidon and Tyre ('Barat-anac' / land of tin) discovered and settled Britain alongside Gomerite Cimmerian peoples.

nodes.name: Ancient British Kings vs. Rome (Strutt 1779 & Caesar Commentaries): Cassivellaunus (54 BCE) → Cunobelinus → Caractacus & Queen Boadicea
sources: Joseph Strutt Chronicle of England (1779) p. 3
nodes.notes: Combines Caesar's eyewitness Commentaries (55-54 BCE) and Strutt's Chronicle of England: Cassivellaunus (commander against Julius Caesar) -> Tasciovanus -> Cunobelinus ('Cymbeline') -> Caractacus, alongside Iceni Queen Boadicea.

nodes.name: Venerable Bede's Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy (731 CE): Hengist & Horsa (from Woden) → King Ethelbert of Kent, Edwin & St. Oswald of Northumbria & Offa of Mercia
nodes.role: Germanic-Wodenic Kingdoms of the Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy
sources: Venerable Bede Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723 ed.)
nodes.notes: Bede explicitly traces Kentish brothers Hengist & Horsa (and fellow Heptarchy dynasties of Kent, Northumbria, Mercia, East Anglia & Wessex) to Woden -> Ethelbert of Kent (baptized 597), St. Edwin & St. Oswald of Northumbria, and Offa of Mercia.

nodes.name: Mézeray's First Race of France (1683): King Pharamond → Clodion → Meroveus (King III, Defeated Attila 451 CE) → Childeric I → Clovis I
nodes.role: Salian Frankish Founders of the First Race (Merovingians)
sources: François Eudes de Mézeray General Chronological History of France (1683) p. 10
nodes.notes: Mézeray (1683) documents the First Race of French monarchs from Pharamond and Clodion through Meroveus (King III, p. 10, who allied with Aëtius and Theodoric against Attila at the Catalaunian Plains, 451 CE), Childeric I, and Clovis I.

nodes.name: Sandford's Genealogical Proof of Portugal (1662): Robert Duke of Burgundy (Capetian Male Line) → Count Henry of Burgundy → Kings of Portugal
nodes.role: Strict Agnate Capetian Pedigree Refuting Alternative Legends for Count Henry
sources: Francis Sandford Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal (1662) pp. 2-3
nodes.notes: Quoting Théodore Godefroy and ancient Fleury manuscripts (pp. 2-3), Sandford demonstrates Count Henry of Burgundy descended in direct male line from Robert the Pious & Robert I, Duke of Burgundy (House of France), marrying Alfonso VI's daughter Teresa in 1089/1090 to found Portugal's crown.

nodes.name: Assyrian Eponym Canon Synchronisms (George Smith 1875): Shalmaneser III (↔ Ahab & Jehu), Tiglath-Pileser III (↔ Uzziah/Menahem/Ahaz) & Sargon II (722 BCE Samaria)
nodes.role: Cuneiform Year-by-Year Lock Linking Biblical Kings of Israel & Judah with Assyria
sources: George Smith The Assyrian Eponym Canon (1875) pp. 10-77
nodes.notes: British Museum Assyriologist George Smith edits the limmu eponym canon from Shalmaneser III through Sennacherib and Esarhaddon, locking Biblical reigns (Ahab, Jehu, Uzziah, Menahem, Pekah, Ahaz, Hezekiah & Tirhakah) to astronomical & eponym dates.

nodes.name: Records of the Past Vols. 9 & 11 (Cuneiform & Phoenician): Rimmon-Nirari I, Khorsabad Palace, Sennacherib Nebbi Yunus (46 Cities of Hezekiah), Ashurbanipal & King Eshmunazar of Sidon
nodes.era: 1320–5th c. BCE (Records of the Past Vols. 9 & 11)
nodes.role: Primary Translated Assyrian, Babylonian & Phoenician Royal Inscriptions
sources: Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Oppert, Pinches, George Smith)
Records of the Past Vol. 11 (Sayce, Budge)
nodes.notes: Primary translations of Adad-nirari I (son of Pudil, grandson of Bel-nirari, great-grandson of Assur-uballit I), Sargon's Khorsabad Annals, Sennacherib's Bavian & Nebbi Yunus inscriptions (46 cities of Hezekiah & Luli/Tubali of Sidon), Ashurbanipal's Cylinder B, and Sidon King Eshmunazar's sarcophagus.

nodes.name: The Turin King-List / Royal Canon of Turin (Kim Ryholt): Gods → Spirit Kings (Ax.w / Shemsu-Hor) → Historical Human Pharaohs
nodes.role: Only Native Pre-Ptolemaic True Royal Canon of Ancient Egypt
sources: Kim Ryholt The Turin King-List (Papyrus Turin inv. 1874 verso)
nodes.notes: Ryholt analyzes the 19th-Dynasty Turin King-List structuring Egyptian kingship into three tiers: mythological gods (Cols. I-II, ending in Seth & Horus), spirit/demigod kings (Ax.w / Shemsu-Hor), and exact human pharaohs through the Second Intermediate Period.

nodes.name: Sir Isaac Newton's Chronology Amended (1728): Sesostris = Shishak (1 Kings 14), Canaanites Fleeing Joshua, Danaus & Nabonassar (747 BCE)
nodes.era: Newtonian Synchronism Model (Sir Isaac Newton 1728 pp. 9-93)
nodes.role: Sir Isaac Newton's Compression of Pagan Chronologies to Biblical Anchors
sources: Sir Isaac Newton The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended (1728) pp. 9-93
nodes.notes: Newton synchronizes Mediterranean antiquity to Scripture by identifying Egyptian conqueror Sesostris with Biblical Shishak (1 Kings 14), tracing the Canaanite flight from Joshua into Egypt and Greece (Danaus), and anchoring Babylon & Assyria at Pul (747 BCE) and Nabonassar.

nodes.name: Archbishop Ussher's Annals of the World (1658), Blair (1753), Guthrie (1764) & Betham Tables (1795): Universal Biblical-Classical Chronology (4004 BCE – 70 CE)
nodes.era: Universal Chronography (Ussher 1658 p. 7; Blair 1753; Guthrie 1764; Betham 1795)
nodes.role: Grand Comparative Synchronism Unifying Creation, Patriarchs, Egypt & Greece
sources: Archbishop James Ussher Annals of the World (1658) p. 7
nodes.notes: Ussher's Annals (with Blair's Tables, Guthrie & Gray's 13-volume Universal History, the Universal History of the Holy Bible & British Family Bible) align Creation (4004 BCE), the Flood, Abraham, Jacob, Sicyon/Argos (Aegialeus/Inachus), and Manetho's Hyksos Pharaohs into one continuous timeline.

nodes.name: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XXXVI (Pagan Roman Testimony): Damascus → Abraham → Israhel (Jacob) → Judah, Joseph in Egypt & Moses
nodes.era: 1st c. BCE / 2nd c. CE (Justin Epitome of Pompeius Trogus XXXVI.2)
nodes.role: Independent Greco-Roman Ethnographic Summary of Israelite Origins
sources: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XXXVI (Watson 1853 p. 245)
nodes.notes: Trogus & Justin independently attest Hebrew patriarchs as historical kings/rulers in Syria ('Damascus -> Azelus -> Adores -> Abraham -> Israhel' with ten/twelve sons, Judas, Joseph in Egyptian dreamcraft & magic, and Moses leading the Exodus).

nodes.name: Justin Book XLI (Scythian Origin of Parthia): Exiled Scythians ('Parthi') → King Arsaces I → Mithridates I → Phraates
nodes.era: 247 BCE – 20 CE (Justin Epitome Book XLI pp. 272-297)
nodes.role: Classical Testimony Tracing the Arsacid Parthian Empire to Scythia
sources: Justin / Pompeius Trogus Book XLI (Watson 1853 pp. 272-297)
nodes.notes: Justin Book XLI explains that the Parthians — rivals who divided the world with Rome — originated as 'Parthi' (exiles) from Scythia before rising under Arsaces I, Mithridates I, and Phraates.

nodes.name: Suetonius (Twelve Caesars), Pliny & Herodian: Commodus → Pertinax → Septimius Severus → Caracalla → Elagabalus → Severus Alexander
nodes.era: 49 BCE – 238 CE (Suetonius; Pliny; Herodian; Basil Kennett)
nodes.role: Julio-Claudian / Flavian Documentation & Severan Roman Emperors
sources: Suetonius Lives of the Twelve Caesars
Herodian History of the Roman Emperors (1689 / 1749)
nodes.notes: Combines Suetonius's biographies of the Twelve Caesars, Pliny's Panegyrick on Trajan, Kennett's Roman Antiquities, and Herodian's eyewitness narrative from Marcus Aurelius & Commodus through Pertinax, Septimius Severus (campaigns in Britain), Caracalla, Elagabalus, and Severus Alexander.

nodes.name: Herodotus (Egypt, Persia & Greece) & Polybius (Punic Wars / Scipio & Hannibal): Classical Mediterranean Synchronisms
nodes.era: 5th–2nd c. BCE (Herodotus Vols. 1-2; Polybius Books I-V)
nodes.role: Father of History (Egypt/Cyrus/Xerxes) & Carthage–Rome Constitutional Bridge
sources: Polybius General History in Five Books
nodes.notes: Anchors Achaemenid, Saitic Egyptian, and Ionian/Athenian lineages (Herodotus Vols. 1-2) alongside Polybius's analytical account of the Punic Wars uniting Barcid Carthage, Numidia, Hellenistic Macedon/Seleucids, and Republican Rome.

nodes.name: Cradock's Apostolical History (1672): Global Missions of the Apostles — Paul's 5 Journeys to Rome, Peter, James, John, Thomas & the Early Churches
nodes.role: Complete Narrative Chronotaxis of the Apostolic Era & Epistles
sources: Samuel Cradock The Apostolical History (1672) Preface
nodes.notes: Cradock maps all five missionary journeys of Apostle Paul (Syria, Cyprus, Galatia, Macedonia, Greece, Ephesus & Rome), alongside the churches founded by Peter, James, John, and the Twelve Apostles.

nodes.name: Acamapichtli (1st Tlatoani of Tenochtitlan, 1376–1395)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Codex Mendoza, Modern Universal History Vol. 14.

nodes.name: Huitzilihuitl (2nd Tlatoani)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Codex Mendoza, Modern Universal History Vol. 14.
