nodes.role: Mother of Samson Named in Pseudo-Philo
nodes.notes: Named wife of Manoah of Zorah in Pseudo-Philo.

nodes.name: King Abibaal of Tyre (Father of Hiram I, Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.notes: Father of Solomon's ally King Hiram I.

nodes.name: King Hiram I of Tyre (980–947 BCE; Ally of David & Solomon, 1 Kgs 5)
nodes.era: 980–947 BCE (1 Kgs 5; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.role: King of Tyre & Lebanon Cedar Ally
nodes.notes: Son of Abibaal; supplied cedar and craftsman Huram-Abi for Solomon's Temple.

nodes.name: King Baal-ezer I of Tyre (Son of Hiram I, 946–930 BCE)
nodes.notes: Succeeded Hiram I through Abdastartus.

nodes.name: King Baal-ezer II of Tyre (Son of Ethbaal I; Brother of Jezebel, 846–841 BCE)
nodes.era: 846–841 BCE (Kurkh Monolith; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.role: Son of Ethbaal & Brother of Queen Jezebel
nodes.notes: Paid tribute to Shalmaneser III in 841 BCE.

nodes.name: King Mattan I of Tyre (Father of Pygmalion & Queen Dido, 840–832 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Baal-ezer II; father of Pygmalion and Elissa/Dido.

nodes.name: King Pygmalion / Pumayyaton of Tyre (Brother of Dido, 831–785 BCE)
nodes.era: 831–785 BCE (Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18; Nora Stone)
nodes.notes: Reigned 47 years; sister Elissa/Dido founded Carthage in his 7th year (814 BCE).

nodes.name: General Hamilcar Barca (First Punic War & Iberia, d. 228 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Hannibal, Hasdrubal, and Mago Barca.

nodes.name: Hannibal Barca of Carthage (247–183 BCE; Crossed Alps 218 BCE)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Hamilcar Barca; victor of Trebia, Trasimene & Cannae.

nodes.name: Hasdrubal Barca (Brother of Hannibal; Commander in Hispania, d. 207 BCE)
nodes.notes: Fell at the Battle of the Metaurus.

nodes.name: Mago Barca (Youngest Son of Hamilcar Barca, d. 203 BCE)
nodes.notes: Founded Port Mahon and fought in Italy.

nodes.name: General Hasdrubal Gisco (Father of Sophonisba, d. 202 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Sophonisba.

nodes.name: Queen Sophonisba (Daughter of Hasdrubal Gisco; Wife of Syphax & Masinissa)
nodes.notes: Married Numidian kings Syphax and Masinissa during the 2nd Punic War.

nodes.name: King Gaia of the Massylii (Father of Masinissa, d. 206 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of unifier King Masinissa.

nodes.name: King Masinissa of Numidia (202–148 BCE; Ally of Rome at Zama)
nodes.notes: Allied with Scipio Africanus at Zama; father of Micipsa, Mastanabal & Gulussa.

nodes.name: King Micipsa of Numidia (148–118 BCE; Adoptive Father of Jugurtha)
nodes.notes: Father of Adherbal & Hiempsal I; adopted nephew Jugurtha.

nodes.name: King Jugurtha of Numidia (Nephew of Micipsa, 118–104 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mastanabal; resisted Rome in the Jugurthine War.

nodes.name: King Juba I of Numidia (Father of Juba II, d. 46 BCE)
nodes.notes: Allied with Cato & Scipio at Thapsus; father of scholar-king Juba II.

nodes.name: King Ptolemy of Mauretania (Son of Juba II & Cleopatra Selene II, 23–40 CE)
nodes.era: c. 10 BCE – 40 CE (Tacitus Annals IV.23; Suetonius Caligula 35)
nodes.notes: Son of King Juba II and Queen Cleopatra Selene II; grandson of Mark Antony & Cleopatra VII!

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra Selene II (Daughter of Cleopatra VII & Mark Antony; Wife of Juba II)
nodes.notes: Twin daughter of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony; raised by Octavia Minor in Rome, wed King Juba II of Mauretania, and bore King Ptolemy of Mauretania.

nodes.name: King Gyges of Lydia (Mermnad Founder, 680–644 BCE)
nodes.notes: Overthrew Heraclid Candaules; allied with Assyria under Ashurbanipal.

nodes.name: King Ardys II of Lydia (644–624 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Gyges.

nodes.name: King Sadyattes of Lydia (624–612 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Alyattes.

nodes.name: King Alyattes of Lydia (612–560 BCE; Coinage Pioneer)
nodes.notes: Minted earliest electrum coins; wed daughter Aryenis to Median Crown Prince Astyages.

nodes.name: King Croesus of Lydia (560–546 BCE; Conquered by Cyrus)
nodes.notes: Famed for wealth; fought Cyrus the Great at Thymbra & Sardis (546 BCE).

nodes.name: Queen Aryenis of Media (Daughter of Alyattes; Wife of Astyages, Herodotus I.74)
nodes.notes: Married Astyages of Media to seal the Battle of the Eclipse peace treaty (585 BCE).

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus I Nicator (312–281 BCE; Husband of Apama)
nodes.notes: General of Alexander; wed Sogdian princess Apama.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus I Soter (281–261 BCE)
nodes.notes: Co-regent in Babylon & victor over Galatians.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus II Theos (261–246 BCE; Husband of Laodice & Berenice)
nodes.notes: Married Ptolemaic princess Berenice (Daniel 11:6 'King of the North').

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus II Callinicus (246–225 BCE)
nodes.role: Son of Antiochus II & Laodice I
nodes.notes: Father of Seleucus III & Antiochus III.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus III the Great (223–187 BCE; Dan 11:11)
nodes.notes: Restored Seleucid authority east to Bactria/India; wed daughter Cleopatra I Syra to Ptolemy V.

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus IV Philopator (187–175 BCE; 2 Macc 3)
nodes.notes: Dispatched Heliodorus to Jerusalem Temple.

nodes.name: Emperor Demetrius I Soter (161–150 BCE; 1 Macc 7)
nodes.notes: Authorized High Priest Alcimus against Judas Maccabeus.

nodes.name: Queen Apama of Sogdia (Daughter of Spitamenes; Wife of Seleucus I)
nodes.role: Sogdian Queen of the Seleucid Empire
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sogdian leader Spitamenes; sole Alexander-era queen marriage never repudiated.

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra I Syra of Egypt (Daughter of Antiochus III; Wife of Ptolemy V)
nodes.role: Seleucid Princess Who Brought Name 'Cleopatra' to Egypt
nodes.notes: Introduced Seleucid marriage link and name Cleopatra into the Ptolemaic house.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus IV Epiphanes (175–164 BCE; Sparked Maccabean Revolt)
nodes.notes: Desecrated the Second Temple in 167 BCE, provoking Mattathias & Judas Maccabeus.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus V Eupator (Son of Antiochus IV, 164–161 BCE)
nodes.notes: Young son of Antiochus IV.

nodes.name: King Antigonus I Monophthalmus (d. 301 BCE at Ipsus)
nodes.notes: Unifier of Asia until Battle of Ipsus.

nodes.name: King Demetrius I Poliorcetes (337–283 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Antigonus II Gonatas.

nodes.name: King Antigonus II Gonatas of Macedon (277–239 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Demetrius Poliorcetes.

nodes.name: King Philip V of Macedon (221–179 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of final king Perseus.

nodes.name: King Perseus of Macedon (Last King of Macedon, 179–168 BCE; Pydna)
nodes.notes: Defeated by Aemilius Paullus at Pydna (168 BCE) and interned at Alba Fucens.

nodes.name: King Pyrrhus of Epirus (319–272 BCE; Aeacid Cousin of Alexander)
nodes.role: Molossian King Claiming Descent From Achilles
nodes.notes: Son of Aeacides; second cousin of Alexander the Great and renowned adversary of Rome ('Pyrrhic victory').

nodes.name: King Mithridates I Ktistes of Pontus (281–266 BCE)
nodes.notes: Claimed Achaemenid Persian noble lineage.

nodes.name: King Pharnaces I of Pontus (185–155 BCE)
nodes.notes: Captured Sinope.

nodes.name: King Mithridates VI Eupator ('The Great' / Poison King, 120–63 BCE)
nodes.notes: Fought three Mithridatic Wars against Sulla, Lucullus & Pompey; father of Cleopatra of Pontus & Pharnaces II.

nodes.name: King Pharnaces II of Pontus & Bosporus (Son of Mithridates VI; Battle of Zela 47 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mithridates VI defeated by Julius Caesar at Zela (47 BCE).

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra of Pontus (Daughter of Mithridates VI; Wife of Tigranes the Great)
nodes.era: fl. 94–66 BCE (Plutarch Lucullus; Betham Tab. LXXXIII)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Mithridates VI; married Tigranes II the Great of Armenia and bore Artavasdes II.

nodes.name: King Artaxias I of Armenia (189–160 BCE; Founder of Artaxata)
nodes.notes: Established Artaxiad Dynasty & capital Artaxata.

nodes.name: Emperor Tigranes II the Great of Armenia (95–55 BCE; King of Kings)
nodes.notes: Built empire from Caspian to Syria; wed Cleopatra of Pontus.

nodes.name: King Artavasdes II of Armenia (55–34 BCE; Son of Tigranes II)
nodes.notes: Scholarly son of Tigranes the Great & Cleopatra of Pontus.

nodes.name: King Diodotus I Soter of Bactria (250–239 BCE)
nodes.notes: Broke away from Antiochus II in Bactria/Sogdia.

nodes.name: King Euthydemus I of Bactria (230–200 BCE)
nodes.role: Defender of Bactra Against Antiochus III
nodes.notes: Father of Indo-Greek conqueror Demetrius I.

nodes.name: King Demetrius I of Bactria (c. 200–180 BCE; Conqueror of Gandhara)
nodes.notes: Extended Hellenistic rule into Northwest India.

nodes.name: King Menander I Soter / King Milinda (165–130 BCE; Milinda Panha)
nodes.notes: Central royal interlocutor of Buddhist classic Milinda Panha.

nodes.name: King Aegialeus of Sicyon (1st King in Eusebius Chronicle, p. 53)
nodes.era: Eusebius Chronicle p.53 (Synchronized With Belus & Ninus)
nodes.role: First Attested Greek City-King in Eusebius
nodes.notes: Son of Inachus in Apollodorus; placed by Eusebius at the dawn of Greek chronology as contemporary of Nimrod/Belus & Ninus.

nodes.name: King Abgar V Ukkama of Osroene / Edessa (4 BCE–7 CE, 13–50 CE)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Edessa — Eusebius HE I.13; Doctrine of Addai)
nodes.notes: Abgarid king of Edessa prominent in early Syriac Christian historiography.

nodes.name: King Latinus of Laurentum (Father of Lavinia, Dionysius I.57–64)
nodes.era: 12th c. BCE (Dionysius Ant. I.57–64; Livy I.1)
nodes.notes: Welcomed Aeneas and gave daughter Lavinia in marriage.

nodes.name: Queen Lavinia (Daughter of Latinus; Wife of Aeneas; Mother of Silvius)
nodes.role: Latin Princess & Mother of Alban Dynasty
nodes.notes: Eponym of Lavinium; mother of Silvius Posthumus by Aeneas.

nodes.name: King Ascanius / Iulus (Son of Aeneas & Creusa; Founder of Alba Longa, Dionysius I.65–70)
nodes.role: Founder of Alba Longa & Claimed Ancestor of Gens Julia
nodes.notes: Son of Aeneas & Trojan Creusa; built Alba Longa.

nodes.name: 1. King Silvius Posthumus (Son of Aeneas & Lavinia, 29 yrs)
nodes.notes: Half-brother of Ascanius; ancestor of all Alban Silvii.

nodes.name: 2. King Aeneas Silvius (31 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Silvius.

nodes.name: 3. King Latinus Silvius (51 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Aeneas Silvius.

nodes.name: 4. King Alba Silvius (39 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Latinus Silvius.

nodes.name: 5. King Atys / Capetus I Silvius (26 yrs, Livy I.3)
nodes.notes: Son of Alba.

nodes.name: 6. King Capys Silvius (28 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Atys.

nodes.name: 7. King Capetus / Calpetus Silvius (13 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Capys.

nodes.name: 8. King Tiberinus Silvius (Eponym of River Tiber, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Drowned in the Albula, thereafter named the Tiber River.

nodes.name: 9. King Agrippa Silvius (41 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Tiberinus.

nodes.name: 10. King Romulus / Alladius Silvius (19 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Agrippa.

nodes.name: 11. King Aventinus Silvius (37 yrs; Eponym of Aventine Hill)
nodes.notes: Buried on the Aventine Hill.

nodes.name: 12. King Procas Silvius (23 yrs; Father of Numitor & Amulius)
nodes.notes: Father of rightful heir Numitor and usurper Amulius.

nodes.name: 13. King Numitor Silvius of Alba Longa (Grandfather of Romulus & Remus)
nodes.notes: Restored to Alba Longa's throne by grandsons Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: Rhea Silvia / Ilia (Daughter of Numitor; Mother of Romulus & Remus)
nodes.notes: Mother of Rome's twin founders Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: King Amulius of Alba Longa (42-Year Usurper, Dionysius I.71, 76)
nodes.notes: Overthrew Numitor before being slain by Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: Remus (Twin Brother of Romulus, 753 BCE)
nodes.notes: Twin brother of Romulus born to Rhea Silvia.

nodes.name: 2. King Numa Pompilius (Sabine Lawgiver King, 715–673 BCE)
nodes.notes: Instituted Roman religious calendar, temples & priestly colleges.

nodes.name: 3. King Tullus Hostilius (673–642 BCE; Absorbed Alba Longa)
nodes.notes: Destroyed Alba Longa and incorporated its noble Alban clans into Rome.

nodes.name: 4. King Ancus Marcius (642–617 BCE; Grandson of Numa)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Numa Pompilius; built Sublician Bridge & Ostia port.

nodes.name: 5. King Lucius Tarquinius Priscus (+ Tanaquil, 616–579 BCE)
nodes.notes: Initiated Circus Maximus & Cloaca Maxima.

nodes.name: 6. King Servius Tullius (578–535 BCE; Servian Constitution & Walls)
nodes.notes: Reformed Roman centuriate classes; son-in-law of Tarquinius Priscus.

nodes.name: 7. King Lucius Tarquinius Superbus (535–509 BCE; Expelled at Republic's Founding)
nodes.notes: Expelled in 509 BCE by Lucius Junius Brutus, inaugurating the Roman Republic.

nodes.name: Gaius Julius Caesar (100–44 BCE; Dictator Perpetuo)
nodes.role: Dictator of Rome & Great-Uncle / Adoptive Father of Augustus
nodes.notes: Descendant of Gens Julia; crossed Rubicon 49 BCE, wed Cornelia/Calpurnia, fathered Julia & Ptolemy XV Caesarion, adopted Octavian.

nodes.name: Julia Minor (Sister of Julius Caesar; Grandmother of Augustus)
nodes.notes: Sister of Julius Caesar; wed Marcus Atius Balbus and bore Atia.

nodes.name: Atia Balba (Niece of Julius Caesar; Mother of Augustus & Octavia Minor)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Julia Minor & Balbus; wed Gaius Octavius and bore Octavia Minor & Augustus.

nodes.name: Octavia Minor (Sister of Augustus; Wife of Mark Antony; Progenitress of Caligula, Claudius & Nero!)
nodes.role: Key Matriarch Linking Julii, Antonii & Julio-Claudians
nodes.notes: Elder sister of Augustus; bore Antonia Minor by Mark Antony — uniting Julian & Antonian lines in Caligula, Claudius, and Nero!

nodes.name: Emperor Augustus / Gaius Octavius (27 BCE–14 CE; Luke 2:1)
nodes.notes: Adopted heir of Julius Caesar; ruled 27 BCE–14 CE during the birth of Jesus.

nodes.name: Empress Livia Drusilla / Julia Augusta (Wife of Augustus; Mother of Tiberius & Drusus)
nodes.role: First Empress of Rome & Mother of Tiberius
nodes.notes: Mother of Emperor Tiberius and General Drusus the Elder by Tiberius Claudius Nero; wed Augustus for 51 years.

nodes.name: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa (c. 63–12 BCE; Builder of Pantheon & Co-Ruler)
nodes.role: Son-in-Law of Augustus & Maternal Grandfather of Caligula
nodes.notes: Wed Augustus's daughter Julia the Elder, fathering Gaius, Lucius, Agrippina the Elder & Agrippa Postumus.

nodes.name: Julia the Elder (Sole Biological Child of Emperor Augustus)
nodes.notes: Mother of Agrippina the Elder by Marcus Agrippa.

nodes.name: General Nero Claudius Drusus (Son of Livia; Brother of Tiberius; Husband of Antonia)
nodes.role: Stepson of Augustus & Father of Germanicus & Claudius
nodes.notes: Brother of Emperor Tiberius; wed Antonia Minor and fathered Germanicus and Emperor Claudius.

nodes.name: Antonia Minor (Daughter of Mark Antony & Octavia; Mother of Germanicus & Claudius)
nodes.era: 36 BCE – 37 CE (Suetonius Claudius 11; Josephus Ant. XVIII.6)
nodes.role: Matriarch of Three Generations of Roman Emperors
nodes.notes: Befriended Berenice I & young Herod Agrippa I in Rome; bore Germanicus, Livilla & Emperor Claudius.

nodes.name: General Germanicus Julius Caesar (15 BCE–19 CE; Father of Caligula)
nodes.era: 15 BCE – 19 CE (Tacitus Annals I–II; Suetonius Caligula 1–7)
nodes.notes: Son of Drusus the Elder & Antonia Minor; wed Agrippina the Elder, bearing Caligula & Agrippina the Younger.

nodes.name: Agrippina the Elder (Daughter of Julia & Agrippa; Mother of Caligula & Agrippina II)
nodes.notes: Granddaughter of Augustus; mother of Emperor Caligula and Agrippina the Younger.

nodes.name: Empress Agrippina the Younger (Sister of Caligula; Wife of Claudius; Mother of Nero)
nodes.role: Daughter of Germanicus & Mother of Emperor Nero
nodes.notes: Great-granddaughter of Augustus; mother of Emperor Nero.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantius I Chlorus (Tetrarch, 293–306 CE; Father of Constantine I)
nodes.role: Western Augustus & Father of Constantine the Great
nodes.notes: Father of Constantine the Great by St. Helena.

nodes.name: Empress St. Helena Augusta (Mother of Constantine the Great, c. 246–330 CE)
nodes.era: c. 246–330 CE (Eusebius VC III; Chronicon Paschale)
nodes.notes: Mother of first Christian Emperor Constantine I.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantine II (Son of Constantine I, 337–340 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Gaul, Spain & Britain after 337 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantius II (Son of Constantine I, 337–361 CE)
nodes.role: Middle Son of Constantine & Eastern Emperor
nodes.notes: Ruled the Eastern Roman Empire 337–361 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Constans I (Son of Constantine I, 337–350 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Italy, Africa & Illyricum.

nodes.name: Emperor Arcadius (Elder Son of Theodosius I, 395–408 CE; Chronicon Paschale p. 80)
nodes.role: First Emperor of Permanently Divided Eastern Roman Empire
nodes.notes: Proclaimed Augustus by father Theodosius I at the Hebdomon in Constantinople (383 CE); father of Theodosius II.

nodes.name: Emperor Honorius (Younger Son of Theodosius I, 395–423 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Theodosius I & Aelia Flaccilla.

nodes.name: Empress Galla Placidia (Daughter of Theodosius I; Queen of Visigoths & Augusta, c. 390–450 CE)
nodes.role: Daughter of Theodosius I & Mother of Valentinian III
nodes.notes: Daughter of Theodosius I & Galla; wed Visigothic King Athaulf and later Emperor Constantius III.

nodes.name: Emperor Valentinian III (Son of Galla Placidia, 425–455 CE)
nodes.notes: Western Emperor during Attila's campaigns.

nodes.name: King Deioces of Media (Daiukku, r. c. 700–647 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of Median Kingdom at Ecbatana
nodes.notes: Son of Phraortes; first king of unified Media according to Herodotus.

nodes.name: King Phraortes of Media (Fravartish, Son of Deioces, r. c. 647–625 BCE)
nodes.notes: Subjugated Persians and fell against Assyria.

nodes.name: King Cyaxares of Media (Uvakhshatra, Son of Phraortes, r. 625–585 BCE)
nodes.notes: Allied with Nabopolassar of Babylon to overthrow Assyria; father of Astyages & Amytis.

nodes.name: King Astyages of Media (Ishtumegu, Son of Cyaxares, r. 585–550 BCE)
nodes.role: Last King of Media & Maternal Grandfather of Cyrus
nodes.notes: Father of Princess Mandane; defeated by his grandson Cyrus the Great in 550 BCE.

nodes.name: Achaemenes (Hakhamanish, Eponymous Founder of Achaemenids)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of both royal branches proclaimed in Darius I's Behistun Inscription.

nodes.name: King Teispes of Anshan (Chishpish, Son of Achaemenes)
nodes.notes: Father of Cyrus I (Senior line) and Ariaramnes (Junior line).

nodes.name: King Cyrus I of Anshan (Kurash I, Son of Teispes)
nodes.notes: Paid tribute to Ashurbanipal; father of Cambyses I.

nodes.name: King Cambyses I of Anshan (Kambujiya I, Father of Cyrus the Great)
nodes.notes: Married Median Princess Mandane (daughter of Astyages).

nodes.name: Shahanshah Cambyses II (Son of Cyrus the Great, r. 530–522 BCE; Conquered Egypt)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Cyrus the Great; defeated Psamtik III at Pelusium (525 BCE).

nodes.name: Prince Bardiya / Smerdis (Younger Son of Cyrus the Great, d. 522 BCE)
nodes.role: Younger Son of Cyrus the Great
nodes.notes: Brother of Cambyses II.

nodes.name: Queen Atossa (Daughter of Cyrus the Great; Wife of Darius I; Mother of Xerxes I)
nodes.role: Achaemenid Empress Uniting Senior & Junior Lines
nodes.notes: Daughter of Cyrus the Great; married Darius I and bore Xerxes I, uniting both Achaemenid branches.

nodes.name: Ariaramnes (Ariyaramna, Son of Teispes)
nodes.notes: Younger son of Teispes.

nodes.name: Arsames (Arshama, Son of Ariaramnes)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Darius I the Great.

nodes.name: Hystaspes / Vishtaspa (Satrap of Parthia; Father of Darius I)
nodes.role: Father of Darius I the Great
nodes.notes: Son of Arsames; father of Darius I.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes I Longimanus (Son of Xerxes I, r. 465–424 BCE; Ezra 7 & Nehemiah 2)
nodes.notes: Commissioned Ezra (458 BCE) and Nehemiah (445 BCE) to restore Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Darius II Ochus (Son of Artaxerxes I, r. 423–404 BCE)
nodes.notes: Married half-sister Parysatis; father of Artaxerxes II & Cyrus the Younger.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes II Mnemon (Son of Darius II, r. 404–358 BCE)
nodes.notes: Reigned 46 years; father of Artaxerxes III.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Artaxerxes III Ochus (Son of Artaxerxes II, r. 358–338 BCE)
nodes.notes: Ended the 30th native dynasty of Egypt.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Arses / Artaxerxes IV (Son of Artaxerxes III, r. 338–336 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Artaxerxes III.

nodes.name: Shahanshah Darius III Codomannus (Great-Grandson of Darius II, r. 336–330 BCE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Ostanes (brother of Artaxerxes II); defeated by Alexander the Great at Gaugamela (331 BCE); father of Stateira II.

nodes.name: Princess Stateira II (Daughter of Darius III; Married Alexander the Great at Susa, 324 BCE)
nodes.era: d. 323 BCE (Arrian Anabasis VII.4; Plutarch Alexander 70)
nodes.role: Achaemenid Princess Married to Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: United the Achaemenid Persian and Argead Macedonian royal houses at the Susa Weddings (324 BCE).

nodes.name: Prince Cyrus the Younger (Son of Darius II; Battle of Cunaxa 401 BCE)
nodes.notes: Younger son of Darius II & Parysatis who fell at Cunaxa.

nodes.name: Queen Homai Chehrzad (Daughter & Successor of Kay Bahman)
nodes.notes: Mother of Darab.

nodes.name: King Darab (Son of Kay Bahman & Homai; Father of Dara II & Iskandar in Shahnameh)
nodes.notes: In Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, fathered both Dara II and (via Nahid daughter of Failaqus/Philip) Iskandar.

nodes.name: King Dara II ibn Darab (Last Kayanian Shah)
nodes.role: Persian Epic Counterpart of Darius III
nodes.notes: Fought half-brother Iskandar (Alexander) in Shahnameh epic chronology.

nodes.name: King Arsaces I / Ashk ben Ashkan (Founder of Parthia, 247–217 BCE)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Ashkanian/Arsacid Dynasty traced by Al-Biruni to Kayanian Siyavush.

nodes.name: King Tiridates I / Arsaces II (Brother of Arsaces I, c. 217–211 BCE)
nodes.notes: Brother of Arsaces I.

nodes.name: King Mithridates I the Great of Parthia (171–132 BCE)
nodes.notes: Conquered Media and Mesopotamia from the Seleucids.

nodes.name: King Phraates II of Parthia (Son of Mithridates I, 132–127 BCE)
nodes.notes: Defeated Antiochus VII Sidetes.

nodes.name: King Mithridates II the Great of Parthia (124–91 BCE; 'King of Kings')
nodes.role: Parthian Hegemon From Euphrates to Bactria
nodes.notes: Established the Silk Road embassy with Han China & allied with Sulla.

nodes.name: King Orodes II of Parthia (57–37 BCE; Victor of Carrhae 53 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Pacorus I & Phraates IV.

nodes.name: King Phraates IV of Parthia (37–2 BCE; Returned Crassus's Eagles to Augustus)
nodes.notes: Made 20 BCE treaty with Emperor Augustus.

nodes.name: King Vologases I of Parthia (51–78 CE; Patron of Avesta Compilation)
nodes.role: Placed Brother Tiridates on Armenian Throne
nodes.notes: Preserved Zoroastrian Avestan texts and founded Vologesocerta.

nodes.name: King Artabanus IV / Ardawan (Last Parthian Shahanshah, d. 224 CE at Hormozdgan)
nodes.notes: Fell in battle against Ardashir I, ending the 470-year Arsacid Empire.

nodes.name: Aramaneak (Eldest Son of Hayk Nahapet)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Settled in Ayrarat plain.

nodes.name: Aramayis (Son of Aramaneak; Builder of Armavir)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Built capital Armavir on the Araxes.

nodes.name: Amasia (Son of Aramayis; Named Mt. Masis)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Gegham.

nodes.name: Gegham (Son of Amasia; Eponym of Lake Sevan / Gegharkunik)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Harma & Sisak (Syunik).

nodes.name: Harma (Son of Gegham)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Father of Aram.

nodes.name: Patriarch Aram (Son of Harma; Classical Eponym of Armenia)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Extended borders into Cappadocia and Assyria; father of Ara.

nodes.name: Ara the Handsome (Son of Aram; Coveted by Queen Semiramis)
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Fell defending Armenia against Semiramis (Shammuramat).

nodes.name: Ma'add ibn Adnan (Son of Adnan)
nodes.notes: Son of Adnan.

nodes.name: Nizar ibn Ma'add (Father of Mudar & Rabi'ah)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Nizarite Arab confederations.

nodes.name: Mudar ibn Nizar (Brother of Rabi'ah)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Mudar tribes.

nodes.name: Ilyas ibn Mudar
nodes.notes: Married Khindif.

nodes.name: Mudrikah ('Amr) ibn Ilyas
nodes.notes: Son of Ilyas.

nodes.name: Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah
nodes.notes: Father of Kinanah & Asad.

nodes.name: Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Quraysh and allied Hijazi clans.

nodes.name: Al-Nadr ibn Kinanah
nodes.notes: Considered founder of Quraysh in some traditions.

nodes.name: Malik ibn al-Nadr
nodes.notes: Father of Fihr.

nodes.name: Fihr ibn Malik (Quraysh — Eponym of Tribe of Quraysh)
nodes.notes: United the Hijazi clans around Mecca as Quraysh.

nodes.name: Ghalib ibn Fihr
nodes.notes: Son of Fihr.

nodes.name: Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib
nodes.notes: Father of Ka'b.

nodes.name: Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy
nodes.notes: Preached at Mecca; father of Murrah & Adi (Umar's line).

nodes.name: Murrah ibn Ka'b
nodes.notes: Father of Kilab & Taym (Abu Bakr's clan).

nodes.name: Kilab ibn Murrah
nodes.notes: Married Fatimah bint Sa'd; father of Qusayy.

nodes.name: Qusayy ibn Kilab (Zayd — Unifier & Custodian of Mecca, c. 400–480 CE)
nodes.notes: Reclaimed custody of the Ka'bah and established Dar al-Nadwah in Mecca.

nodes.name: 'Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy (Al-Mughirah — Father of Hashim & 'Abd Shams)
nodes.role: 18th Gen Common Ancestor of Prophet, Umayyads & Abbasids
nodes.notes: Fathered twin lines: Hashim (Prophet, Alids, Abbasids) and 'Abd Shams (Umayyads).

nodes.name: Hashim ibn 'Abd Manaf ('Amr al-'Ula — Eponym of Banu Hashim, d. c. 497 CE)
nodes.notes: Led the winter & summer trade caravans of Quraysh; married Salma bint 'Amr of Medina.

nodes.name: 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim (Shaybah al-Hamd, c. 497–578 CE — Rediscovered Zamzam)
nodes.notes: Custodian of Mecca during the Year of the Elephant (570 CE); father of 'Abdallah, Abu Talib, Hamza & al-'Abbas.

nodes.name: 'Abdallah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (545–570 CE; Father of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Wed Aminah bint Wahb and passed away before Muhammad's birth.

nodes.name: Prophet Muhammad ibn 'Abdallah (570–632 CE; Seal of the Prophets in Islam)
nodes.role: Prophet of Islam & Unifier of Arabia
nodes.notes: Son of 'Abdallah & Aminah bint Wahb; married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; father of Fatimah al-Zahra.

nodes.name: Fatimah al-Zahra bint Muhammad (c. 605–632 CE; Wife of Caliph Ali)
nodes.notes: Married cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib; mother of Imams Hasan and Husayn.

nodes.name: Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (625–670 CE; Eldest Grandson of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Father of Hasan al-Muthanna -> living Hashemites of Jordan & Alaouites of Morocco.

nodes.name: Aminah bint Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah (d. 577 CE; Mother of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Noblewoman of Banu Zuhrah (descended from Kilab ibn Murrah); mother of Prophet Muhammad.

nodes.name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (c. 555–619 CE; First Wife of Prophet Muhammad)
nodes.notes: Merchant of Quraysh (descended from Qusayy's brother 'Abd al-'Uzza); bore Fatimah al-Zahra.

nodes.name: Abu Talib ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ('Abd Manaf, c. 535–619 CE; Uncle & Protector of Muhammad)
nodes.role: Chief of Banu Hashim & Father of Ali
nodes.notes: Father of Ja'far al-Tayyar and Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib.

nodes.name: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (626–680 CE; Martyr of Karbala)
nodes.notes: Son of Ali & Fatimah; ancestor of Husaynid Sayyids and Nizari Ismaili Imams.

nodes.name: Imam Ali Zayn al-Abidin (659–713 CE; Son of Imam Husayn)
nodes.notes: Survived Karbala; father of Muhammad al-Baqir.

nodes.name: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (677–733 CE; Son of Zayn al-Abidin)
nodes.notes: Father of Ja'far al-Sadiq.

nodes.name: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (702–765 CE; Jurist & 6th Husaynid Imam)
nodes.role: Ancestor of Fatimids & Aga Khan V
nodes.notes: Teacher of Sunni & Shia jurists; father of Isma'il -> Fatimids -> Aga Khan V.

nodes.name: Al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (c. 566–653 CE; Eponym of the Abbasid Caliphate)
nodes.role: Paternal Uncle of Muhammad & Progenitor of Abbasids
nodes.notes: Father of scholar 'Abdallah ibn al-'Abbas.

nodes.name: 'Abdallah ibn al-'Abbas (619–687 CE; Foremost Qur'anic Exegete & Grandfather of Caliphs)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Abbasid caliphs al-Saffah and al-Mansur via Ali ibn 'Abdallah -> Muhammad.

nodes.name: Caliph Abu al-'Abbas al-Saffah (1st Abbasid Caliph, r. 750–754 CE)
nodes.notes: Brother of Caliph al-Mansur.

nodes.name: Caliph al-Mahdi (Son of al-Mansur; Father of Harun al-Rashid, r. 775–785 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliphs al-Hadi and Harun al-Rashid.

nodes.name: 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf (Progenitor of the Umayyad Caliphs)
nodes.role: Son of 'Abd Manaf & Twin Brother of Hashim
nodes.notes: Father of Umayyah.

nodes.name: Umayyah ibn 'Abd Shams (Eponym of Banu Umayyah)
nodes.notes: Father of Harb (Sufyanids) and Abu al-'As (Caliph Uthman & Marwanids).

nodes.name: Harb ibn Umayyah (Commander of Quraysh at Fijar)
nodes.notes: Father of Abu Sufyan.

nodes.name: Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb (c. 565–653 CE; Father of Mu'awiya I)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliph Mu'awiya I.

nodes.name: Caliph Yazid I ibn Mu'awiya (r. 680–683 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mu'awiya I.

nodes.name: Abu al-'As ibn Umayyah (Son of Umayyah; Ancestor of Uthman & Marwanids)
nodes.notes: Brother of Harb; ancestor of Caliph Uthman and the Marwanid Umayyad Caliphs of Damascus and Cordoba.

nodes.name: 'Affan ibn Abi al-'As (Father of Caliph Uthman)
nodes.notes: Father of 3rd Rashidun Caliph Uthman ibn 'Affan.

nodes.name: Al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As (Brother of 'Affan; Father of Marwan I)
nodes.notes: Uncle of Caliph Uthman.

nodes.name: Caliph Marwan I ibn al-Hakam (623–685 CE; Founder of Marwanid Umayyads)
nodes.notes: Father of Caliph 'Abd al-Malik.

nodes.name: Caliph al-Walid I (r. 705–715 CE; Builder of Damascus Mosque & Expansion to Spain/Sindh)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of 'Abd al-Malik; under his reign Muslim armies reached Iberia & the Indus.

nodes.name: Caliph Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik (r. 724–743 CE; Grandfather of 'Abd al-Rahman I)
nodes.notes: Son of 'Abd al-Malik; grandfather of Emir 'Abd al-Rahman I of Cordoba via Mu'awiya ibn Hisham.

nodes.name: King Ya'rub ibn Qahtan (1st Arabic-Speaking King of Yemen)
nodes.era: Proto-Arabian Era (Tabari; Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Yemeni & South Arabian Arabized tribes.

nodes.name: Yashjub ibn Ya'rub
nodes.notes: Son of Ya'rub.

nodes.name: Saba ibn Yashjub ('Abd Shams — Builder of Marib Dam)
nodes.role: Eponym of Sabaeans; Father of Himyar & Kahlan
nodes.notes: Fathered twin branches Himyar (Tubba kings) and Kahlan (Lakhmids, Ghassanids & Azd).

nodes.name: Himyar ibn Saba (Eponym of Himyarite Kingdom of Yemen)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Himyarite Tubba monarchs.

nodes.name: Tubba As'ad Abu Karib of Himyar (c. 390–440 CE; Embraced Judaism in Yathrib)
nodes.notes: Adopted Judaism in Yathrib and clothed the Ka'bah.

nodes.name: King Yusuf As'ar Dhu-Nuwas of Himyar (r. 517–525 CE; Clashed with King Kaleb of Aksum)
nodes.role: Last Independent Jewish Tubba of Himyar
nodes.notes: Defeated at the Red Sea by Aksumite King Kaleb (Elesbaan) in 525 CE.

nodes.name: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan (Restorer of Himyar against Aksum, c. 575 CE)
nodes.notes: Reclaimed Yemen from Aksumite rule.

nodes.name: Kahlan ibn Saba (Brother of Himyar; Ancestor of Lakhmids, Ghassanids & Ansar of Medina)
nodes.notes: Son of Saba; ancestral trunk of the Lakhmid kings of Al-Hirah and Ghassanid kings of Syria.

nodes.name: Jafnah ibn 'Amr (1st Ghassanid King of Syria, c. 220 CE)
nodes.notes: Founded the Arab Christian Jafnid/Ghassanid kingdom allied with Rome/Byzantium.

nodes.name: King al-Harith V ibn Jabalah of Ghassan (Arethas, r. 529–569 CE; Ally of Justinian I)
nodes.role: Patricius & Paramount Phylarch of the Arabs
nodes.notes: Elevated by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I to king over Syria's Arab foederati.

nodes.name: King Imru' al-Qays I ibn 'Amr of Al-Hirah (d. 328 CE; Namara Inscription)
nodes.notes: Attested in the 328 CE Namara inscription — oldest dated classical Arabic royal epitaph.

nodes.name: King al-Mundhir III ibn al-Nu'man of Al-Hirah (r. 505–554 CE)
nodes.notes: Fought Roman-allied Ghassanid King al-Harith V across Syria.

nodes.name: King al-Nu'man III ibn al-Mundhir of Al-Hirah (r. 582–602 CE)
nodes.role: Last Christian Lakhmid King of Al-Hirah
nodes.notes: Patron of Pre-Islamic Arabic poets; executed by Khosrow II Parviz, sparking the Battle of Dhu Qar.

nodes.name: King Septimius Odaenathus of Palmyra (Husband of Zenobia, d. 267 CE)
nodes.role: Corrector Totius Orientis & King of Kings of Palmyra
nodes.notes: Defeated Shapur I of Persia after Valerian's capture; husband of Zenobia.

nodes.name: Empress Zenobia / Bat-Zabbai of Palmyra (r. 267–272 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Syria, Egypt, and Anatolia; claimed descent from Cleopatra VII of Egypt and Dido of Carthage.

nodes.name: Emperor Vaballathus of Palmyra (Son of Odaenathus & Zenobia, r. 267–272 CE)
nodes.notes: Bore titles of Augustus until defeated by Roman Emperor Aurelian in 272 CE.

nodes.name: Berr / Mazigh (Patriarch of the Imazighen in Ibn Khaldun)
nodes.era: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berberes v4
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Bernes (Branes) and Madghis al-Abtar (Botr).

nodes.name: Bernes (Progenitor of Sanhaja, Masmuda & Kutama Berbers)
nodes.notes: Father of the great sedentary Amazigh confederations.

nodes.name: Sanhaja (Son of Bernes; Ancestor of Almoravids & Zirids)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the Sahara and Maghreb Sanhaja confederations.

nodes.name: Masmuda (Son of Bernes; Ancestor of Atlas Almohads)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the High Atlas Masmuda tribes.

nodes.name: Kutama (Son of Bernes; Supporters of Fatimid North Africa)
nodes.notes: Kabyle confederation key to North African state formation.

nodes.name: Madghis al-Abtar (Progenitor of Zenata, Luwata & Hawwara Berbers)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Zenata nomadic confederations.

nodes.name: Zana / Zenata (Descendant of Madghis al-Abtar; Ancestor of Marinids & Zayyanids)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of Queen al-Kahina's Jerawa Zenata tribe.

nodes.name: King Kusayla / Aksil of Altava (d. 688 CE; Awraba Berber Monarch)
nodes.notes: United Amazigh and Byzantine forces in Numidia.

nodes.name: Queen Dihya al-Kahina (d. 703 CE; Jerawa Zenata Queen of the Aures)
nodes.notes: Jerawa Zenata queen who led Amazigh resistance in the Aures Mountains.

nodes.name: Lord Rama / Sri Ramachandra (Gen 65, Son of Dasharatha; Hero of Ramayana)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of King Dasharatha & Kausalya; husband of Sita; father of Lava & Kusha.

nodes.name: Goddess Sita / Janaki (Daughter of Siradhvaja Janaka; Queen of Ayodhya)
nodes.role: Princess of Videha & Mother of Lava and Kusha
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Siradhvaja Janaka; mother of twins Lava and Kusha.

nodes.name: Prince Bharata (Son of Dasharatha & Kaikeyi; Regent of Ayodhya)
nodes.notes: Ruled Ayodhya from Nandigrama bearing Rama's sandals during the 14-year exile.

nodes.name: Prince Lakshmana (Son of Dasharatha & Sumitra; Companion of Rama)
nodes.notes: Accompanied Rama & Sita throughout the 14-year forest exile.

nodes.name: Prince Shatrughna (Son of Dasharatha & Sumitra; Founder of Mathura's Solar Line)
nodes.notes: Conquered Lavana and founded Mathura.

nodes.name: King Lava of Shravasti (Twin Son of Rama & Sita; Ancestor of Mewar Sisodias)
nodes.role: Twin Prince of North Kosala & Lahore
nodes.notes: Traditional Solar ancestor of North Kosala / Shravasti and Mewar Rajputs.

nodes.name: King Kusha of Kushavati (Twin Son of Rama & Sita; Ancestor of Brihadbala)
nodes.role: Twin Prince Continuing Ayodhya Main Line
nodes.notes: Father of Atithi, continuing the Ayodhya Solar Dynasty to Brihadbala.

nodes.name: Emperor Yudhishthira (Eldest Pandava; Dharmaraja of Indraprastha)
nodes.notes: Victor of Kurukshetra & Emperor of Hastinapura.

nodes.name: Prince Bhima / Bhimasena (2nd Pandava; Slayer of Jarasandha & Duryodhana)
nodes.notes: Father of Ghatotkacha.

nodes.name: Prince Arjuna (3rd Pandava; Recipient of the Bhagavad Gita; Ancestor of Parikshit)
nodes.notes: Wed Draupadi and Subhadra (sister of Krishna); father of Abhimanyu.

nodes.name: Prince Nakula (4th Pandava; Twin Son of Pandu & Madri)
nodes.notes: Master of horses and swords.

nodes.name: Prince Sahadeva (5th Pandava; Twin Son of Pandu & Madri)
nodes.notes: Scholar-warrior of the Pandavas.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Duryodhana (Eldest of 100 Kauravas; Son of Dhritarashtra & Gandhari)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Dhritarashtra & Gandhari.

nodes.name: Prince Abhimanyu (Son of Arjuna & Subhadra; Father of Parikshit)
nodes.notes: Fell at the Chakravyuha; married Uttara and fathered posthumous heir Parikshit.

nodes.name: Emperor Parikshit (Son of Abhimanyu & Uttara; Sole Surviving Kuru Heir)
nodes.notes: Saved in the womb by Krishna; father of Janamejaya.

nodes.name: Emperor Janamejaya (Son of Parikshit; Patron of Mahabharata Recitation)
nodes.notes: Heard the Mahabharata recited by Vaishampayana.

nodes.name: Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (Founder of Maurya Empire, r. 322–297 BCE)
nodes.role: Unifier of India & Ally/Father-in-Law of Seleucus I
nodes.notes: Overthrew the Nandas with Chanakya and forged a treaty with Seleucus I Nicator.

nodes.name: Emperor Bindusara Amitraghata (Son of Chandragupta Maurya, r. 297–273 BCE)
nodes.role: Father of Ashoka & Correspondent of Antiochus I
nodes.notes: Extended Mauryan rule south across the Deccan.

nodes.name: Emperor Ashoka the Great (r. 268–232 BCE; Pillar Edicts Naming Antiochus II & Ptolemy II)
nodes.notes: Sent Buddhist missions to Sri Lanka, Syria, Egypt, and Macedonia.

nodes.name: Arahant Mahinda & Therī Sanghamitta (Son & Daughter of Ashoka Who Brought Buddhism to Lanka)
nodes.notes: Brought the Bodhi Tree sapling to Anuradhapura under King Devanampiya Tissa.

nodes.name: Maharaja Sri Gupta (Founder of Gupta Line, c. 240–280 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Ghatotkacha Gupta.

nodes.name: Maharajadhiraja Chandragupta I (r. 319–335 CE; + Licchavi Princess Kumaradevi)
nodes.notes: Allied with the ancient Licchavis of Vaisali through Kumaradevi.

nodes.name: Emperor Samudragupta (Son of Chandragupta I, r. 335–375 CE; Allahabad Pillar)
nodes.notes: Extended Gupta suzerainty from Himalayas to South India.

nodes.name: Emperor Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (Son of Samudragupta, r. 375–415 CE)
nodes.notes: Overthrew the Western Kshatrapas and hosted Chinese pilgrim Faxian.

nodes.name: Emperor Kumaragupta I (Son of Chandragupta II, r. 415–455 CE; Founder of Nalanda Mahavihara)
nodes.notes: Founded the great monastic university of Nalanda.

nodes.name: Emperor Skandagupta (Son of Kumaragupta I, r. 455–467 CE; Repelled Huna Invasions)
nodes.notes: Defeated the Hephthalites (White Huns) in northern India.

nodes.name: King Vijaya of Tambapanni (1st King of Sri Lanka, c. 543 BCE; Mahavamsa VI–VII)
nodes.notes: Prince from Lala/Vanga who landed at Tambapanni (Lanka).

nodes.name: King Pandukabhaya of Anuradhapura (r. 437–367 BCE; Mahavamsa X)
nodes.notes: United Sri Lanka and laid out Anuradhapura.

nodes.name: King Devanampiya Tissa of Anuradhapura (r. 250–210 BCE; Ally of Emperor Ashoka)
nodes.role: First Buddhist Monarch of Sri Lanka
nodes.notes: Received Ashoka's son Mahinda and planted the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi.

nodes.name: King Dutugemunu / Dutthagamani Abhaya (r. 161–137 BCE; Built Ruwanwelisaya Stupa)
nodes.notes: United all Lanka from Ruhuna.

nodes.name: King Nyatri Tsenpo (1st Yarlung King of Tibet; Claimed Shakya/Licchavi Descent)
nodes.notes: First of the 7 Heavenly Throne Kings of Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Songtsen Gampo (33rd Yarlung King, 617–650 CE; Unifier of Tibetan Empire)
nodes.role: Unifier of Tibet & Sponsor of Tibetan Script
nodes.notes: Married Nepalese princess Bhrikuti and Tang Chinese princess Wencheng.

nodes.name: Emperor Trisong Detsen (r. 755–797 CE; Founded Samye Monastery with Padmasambhava)
nodes.notes: Brought Shantarakshita & Padmasambhava to Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Ralpacan (r. 815–838 CE; Grandson of Trisong Detsen)
nodes.notes: Expanded Buddhist translations and signed 821 CE treaty with Tang China.

nodes.name: Emperor Qin Shi Huang / Ying Zheng (1st Emperor of Unified China, r. 221–210 BCE)
nodes.role: First Emperor of Qin & Builder of Great Wall/Terracotta Army
nodes.notes: Unified Warring States China in 221 BCE.

nodes.name: Emperor Han Gaozu / Liu Bang (Founder of Han Dynasty, r. 202–195 BCE)
nodes.notes: Rose from peasant official to defeat Xiang Yu and establish Han.

nodes.name: Emperor Wen of Han / Liu Heng (Son of Gaozu, r. 180–157 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Emperor Jing.

nodes.name: Emperor Jing of Han / Liu Qi (Son of Emperor Wen, r. 157–141 BCE)
nodes.notes: Consolidated imperial centralization.

nodes.name: Emperor Wu of Han / Liu Che (Han Wudi, r. 141–87 BCE; Opened Silk Road)
nodes.role: Greatest Han Emperor (Zhang Qian & Sima Qian)
nodes.notes: Sent Zhang Qian to Bactria & Parthia, initiating the Silk Road.

nodes.name: Emperor Guangwu of Han / Liu Xiu (Restorer of Eastern Han, r. 25–57 CE)
nodes.role: 9th-Gen Descendant of Liu Bang & Eastern Han Founder
nodes.notes: Restored Han Dynasty at Luoyang.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Gaozu / Li Yuan (Founder of Tang Dynasty, r. 618–626 CE)
nodes.notes: Established Tang capital at Chang'an.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Taizong / Li Shimin (Son of Li Yuan, r. 626–649 CE; Tian Kehan)
nodes.notes: Sponsored Xuanzang's journey to India and Princess Wencheng's marriage to Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Gaozong / Li Zhi (Son of Taizong, r. 649–683 CE)
nodes.notes: Unified the Korean Peninsula campaign in alliance with Silla.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Xuanzong / Li Longji (Grandson of Gaozong & Wu Zetian, r. 712–756 CE)
nodes.role: Kaiyuan Golden Age Monarch (Li Bai & Du Fu)
nodes.notes: Presided over Tang cultural zenith.

nodes.name: Empress Wu Zetian (Sole Female Huangdi of China, r. 690–705 CE)
nodes.role: Only Sovereign Empress Regnant in Chinese History
nodes.notes: Consort of Gaozong; ruled in her own right as Zhou Dynasty Huangdi.

nodes.name: Emperor Song Taizu / Zhao Kuangyin (Founder of Song Dynasty, r. 960–976 CE)
nodes.notes: Ended Five Dynasties fragmentation and inaugurated the Northern Song.

nodes.name: Emperor Hongwu / Zhu Yuanzhang (Founder of Ming Dynasty, r. 1368–1398 CE)
nodes.notes: Drove out Yuan rule and established Nanjing.

nodes.name: Emperor Yongle / Zhu Di (Son of Hongwu, r. 1402–1424 CE; Forbidden City & Zheng He)
nodes.notes: Commissioned Admiral Zheng He's treasure voyages across Asia and East Africa.

nodes.name: Khan Nurhaci (Founder of Later Jin / Manchu Aisin Gioro Clan, r. 1616–1626)
nodes.notes: Created the Eight Banners; father of Hong Taiji.

nodes.name: Emperor Hong Taiji (Son of Nurhaci; Proclaimed Great Qing, r. 1626–1643)
nodes.notes: Father of Shunzhi.

nodes.name: Emperor Shunzhi / Fulin (1st Qing Emperor in Beijing, r. 1644–1661)
nodes.notes: Entered Beijing in 1644 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Kangxi / Xuanye (Son of Shunzhi, r. 1661–1722 — 61 yrs)
nodes.notes: Compiled the Kangxi Dictionary and consolidated Tibet & Taiwan.

nodes.name: Emperor Yongzheng / Yinzhen (4th Son of Kangxi, r. 1722–1735)
nodes.notes: Centralized Qing imperial administration.

nodes.name: Emperor Qianlong / Hongli (Son of Yongzheng, r. 1735–1796)
nodes.notes: Oversaw the Siku Quanshu encyclopedia and zenith of Qing prosperity.

nodes.name: King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo (r. 391–413 CE; Hulbert Vol. 1)
nodes.notes: Expanded Goguryeo across Manchuria and the Korean Peninsula.

nodes.name: Queen Seondeok of Silla (r. 632–647 CE; Cheomseongdae Observatory)
nodes.notes: Built Hwangnyongsa Nine-Story Pagoda and Cheomseongdae.

nodes.name: King Munmu of Unified Silla (r. 661–681 CE; Nephew-Line Unifier of Korea)
nodes.role: Unifier of the Three Kingdoms of Korea
nodes.notes: Son of Muyeol; unified Silla in 668–676 CE.

nodes.name: King Taejo Wang Geon (Founder of Goryeo Dynasty, r. 918–943 CE)
nodes.notes: United Later Three Kingdoms in 936 CE.

nodes.name: King Taejo Yi Seong-gye (Founder of Joseon Dynasty, r. 1392–1398 CE)
nodes.notes: Founded Hanyang (Seoul) as royal capital.

nodes.name: King Sejong the Great of Joseon (Son of Taejong, r. 1418–1450 CE; Creator of Hangul)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Taejo; promulgated Hunminjeongeum (Hangul) in 1446 CE.

nodes.name: Turk / Japhis-Oglany (Eldest Son of Japheth in Abulghazi)
nodes.notes: Invented felt tents and ruled the Issyk-Kul steppe.

nodes.name: Taunak Khan (Son of Turk)
nodes.notes: Succeeded his father Turk.

nodes.name: Ilchi Khan (Son of Taunak)
nodes.notes: Father of Dib Bakuy.

nodes.name: Dib Bakuy Khan (Son of Ilchi)
nodes.notes: Father of Kayuk.

nodes.name: Kayuk Khan (Son of Dib Bakuy)
nodes.notes: Father of Alanja.

nodes.name: Alanja Khan (Son of Kayuk; Father of Twins Tatar & Mogul)
nodes.notes: Divided his domains between twin sons Tatar and Mogul.

nodes.name: Mogul / Mung'l Khan (Twin Son of Alanja; Ancestor of Oghuz & Borjigin)
nodes.notes: Brother of Tatar Khan; father of Qara Khan.

nodes.name: Qara Khan (Son of Mogul; Father of Oghuz Khan)
nodes.notes: Father of the hero Oghuz.

nodes.name: Oghuz Khagan (Son of Qara Khan; Epic Founder of the 24 Oghuz Tribes)
nodes.role: Great Khagan of the Oghuz Turks
nodes.notes: United the steppe nations and fathered 6 illustrious sons (Üçok & Bozok).

nodes.name: Tatar Khan (Twin Son of Alanja Khan; Eponym of the Tatars)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of the 7-generation Tatar Khans.

nodes.name: Gün Khan ('Sun', Eldest Son of Oghuz; Ancestor of Kayi / Ottomans)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the Kayi tribe from whom Suleyman Shah, Ertugrul & Osman I sprang.

nodes.name: Ay Khan ('Moon', 2nd Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Bozok prince.

nodes.name: Yildiz Khan ('Star', 3rd Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Bozok prince.

nodes.name: Gök Khan ('Sky', 4th Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince.

nodes.name: Dag Khan ('Mountain', 5th Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince.

nodes.name: Deniz Khan ('Sea', 6th Son of Oghuz; Ancestor of Seljuks via Kınık)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince linked with the Kınık clan of the Seljuks.

nodes.name: Seljuk Beg ibn Duqaq (10th c. CE; Founder of Seljuk Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Son of Duqaq; converted to Islam near Jand; grandfather of Tughril & Chaghri Beg.

nodes.name: Mikail ibn Seljuk (Son of Seljuk; Father of Tughril & Chaghri Beg)
nodes.notes: Father of Tughril Beg & Chaghri Beg.

nodes.name: Sultan Tughril Beg (1st Great Seljuk Sultan, r. 1037–1063)
nodes.notes: Restored Abbasid protection in Baghdad and founded the Great Seljuk Empire.

nodes.name: Chaghri Beg (Brother of Tughril; Father of Alp Arslan, d. 1060)
nodes.notes: Father of Great Sultan Alp Arslan.

nodes.name: Sultan Alp Arslan (Son of Chaghri Beg; Victor of Manzikert 1071 CE)
nodes.notes: Opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement at Manzikert (1071).

nodes.name: Sultan Malik-Shah I (Son of Alp Arslan; Patron of Omar Khayyam & Nizam al-Mulk, r. 1072–1092)
nodes.notes: Zenith of Great Seljuk power from Syria to Transoxiana.

nodes.name: Süleyman Shah (Kayi Chieftain; Father of Ertuğrul Ghazi)
nodes.notes: Led Kayi clan westward into Anatolia.

nodes.name: Ertuğrul Ghazi (Son of Süleyman Shah; Father of Osman I, d. c. 1280)
nodes.role: Bey of Söğüt & Father of Osman I
nodes.notes: Lord of the Seljuk frontier margraviate at Söğüt; father of Sultan Osman I.

nodes.name: Fénius Farsaid (Scythian King Who Studied the 72 Languages at Babel)
nodes.era: Tower of Babel Era (Lebor Gabála; Keating)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Founded the school of languages and fathered Nel / Niul.

nodes.name: Prince Nel / Niul (Son of Fénius; Wed Egyptian Princess Scota)
nodes.role: Linguist Invited to Egypt by Pharaoh
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Married Scota, daughter of Pharaoh Cingris, and befriended Moses.

nodes.name: Goídel Glas / Gaedhal Glas (Son of Niul & Scota; Eponym of the Gaels)
nodes.role: Eponym of All Gaelic Peoples & Language
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Blessed by Moses after the serpent bite; ancestor of the Milesians.

nodes.name: King Breogán (Founder of Brigantia / A Coruña in Galicia, Spain)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Built the watchtower from whose summit his son Íth sighted Ireland.

nodes.name: Bile mac Breogán (Father of Míl Espáine)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Elder son of Breogán.

nodes.name: Míl Espáine / Milesius (Galamh, Father of the Milesian Conquerors of Ireland)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Éremón (Uí Néill, Connacht, Leinster, Dal Riada) and Éber Finn (Munster, O'Brien, MacCarthy).

nodes.name: High King Éremón mac Míl (1st Milesian High King; Ancestor of Uí Néill & Scots)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Co-king with brother Éber Finn; ancestor of Conn of the Hundred Battles.

nodes.name: High King Conn Cétchathach ('Of the Hundred Battles', 2nd c. CE trad.)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Cormac mac Airt and Niall of the Nine Hostages.

nodes.name: High King Cormac mac Airt of Tara (3rd c. CE trad.; Lawgiver Patron of Fionn)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Grandson of Conn; grandfather of Niall's ancestor Fiacha Sraibtine.

nodes.name: High King Niall Noígíallach ('Of the Nine Hostages', d. c. 405 CE)
nodes.role: Progenitor of All Northern & Southern Uí Néill Dynasties
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Father of Eógan (O'Neill), Conall Gulban (O'Donnell / St. Columba) & Lóegaire (met St. Patrick!).

nodes.name: Princess Scota (Daughter of Pharaoh Cingris; Wife of Niul & Mother of Goídel Glas)
nodes.notes: Egyptian princess married to Scythian scholar Niul; eponym of Scotland ('Scotia').

nodes.name: High King Éber Finn mac Míl (Brother of Éremón; Ancestor of Munster / Eoghanacht / Dál gCais)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Cormac Cas -> Brian Boru.

nodes.name: Prince Ír mac Míl (Ancestral Founder of Ulaid / Ulster & Dál nAraidi)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of Cú Chulainn's Ulaid lineages.

nodes.name: Amairgin Glúngel mac Míl (First Poet & Judge of Ireland)
nodes.notes: Sang the Song of Amairgin upon landing in Ireland.

nodes.name: Prince Eógan mac Néill (Founder of Cenél nEógain / O'Neill Kings of Ailech)
nodes.role: Son of Niall of the Nine Hostages
nodes.notes: Progenitor of O'Neill High Kings.

nodes.name: Prince Conall Gulban mac Néill (Ancestor of O'Donnell & St. Columba of Iona)
nodes.role: Son of Niall; Great-Grandfather of St. Columba
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Tyrconnell & St. Columba.

nodes.name: High King Brian Bóruma / Brian Boru (r. 1002–1014 CE; Victor of Clontarf)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Éber Finn & Cormac Cas (Dál gCais); defeated Vikings at Clontarf (1014 CE).

nodes.name: King Fergus Mór mac Eirc (Founder of Scottish Dál Riata, 498 CE)
nodes.notes: Crossed from Antrim into Argyll, founding the Scottish royal stem.

nodes.name: King Kenneth I MacAlpin (Cináed mac Ailpín, 843–858 CE; 1st King of Alba/Scotland)
sources: Chronicle of the Kings of Alba
nodes.notes: Descendant of Fergus Mór; united Dál Riata and Pictland.

nodes.name: King Malcolm III Canmore (+ St. Margaret of Scotland, r. 1058–1093 CE)
nodes.notes: Married St. Margaret of Wessex (linking Scotland & England's House of Wessex!).

nodes.name: King Robert I the Bruce of Scotland (r. 1306–1329 CE; Bannockburn 1314)
nodes.role: Descendant of Malcolm III & Liberator of Scotland
nodes.notes: Won Scottish independence at Bannockburn (1314 CE); grandfather of Robert II (House of Stewart).

nodes.name: Yngvi-Freyr (Progenitor of Uppsala Yngling Kings, Prose Edda / Ynglinga Saga)
nodes.notes: Son of Njörðr; founder of the Swedish/Norwegian Yngling royal stem.

nodes.name: King Harald I Fairhair of Norway (Haraldr Hárfagri, r. 872–930 CE)
nodes.notes: Descended from the Ynglings; unified Norway at Hafrsfjord.

nodes.name: King Skjöldr / Scyld Scefing (Eponym of Danish Skjöldung Kings, Beowulf & Edda)
nodes.notes: Son of Odin in Snorri's Edda; ancestor of Danish and Viking kings.

nodes.name: King Ragnar Lodbrok ('Hairy-Breeches', 9th c. CE Legendary Sea-King)
nodes.role: Famous Viking Father of Sons of Ragnar
nodes.notes: Fathered Björn Ironside, Ivar the Boneless & Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye.

nodes.name: King Björn Ironside (Son of Ragnar; Raided Mediterranean; Ancestor of Munsö Sweden)
nodes.notes: Led 859 CE Viking expedition to Spain and Italy.

nodes.name: King Ivar the Boneless (Son of Ragnar; Leader of Great Heathen Army 865 CE)
nodes.notes: Conquered York and Dublin.

nodes.name: King Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye (Son of Ragnar; Ancestor of Harthacnut & Canute)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Gorm the Old & King Canute the Great.

nodes.name: Duke Rollo / Hrólfr of Normandy (r. 911–927 CE; Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte)
nodes.notes: Norwegian noble of Jarl Rognvald's house (kin/contemporary of Harald Fairhair) who founded Normandy.

nodes.name: Duke William I Longsword of Normandy (Son of Rollo, r. 927–942 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Rollo & Poppa of Bayeux.

nodes.name: Duke Richard I the Fearless of Normandy (Son of William Longsword, r. 942–996)
nodes.notes: Father of Richard II and Emma of Normandy (Queen of Ethelred II & Canute!).

nodes.name: Duke Richard II the Good of Normandy (Son of Richard I, r. 996–1026 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Robert I the Magnificent.

nodes.name: Duke Robert I the Magnificent of Normandy (r. 1027–1035; Father of William the Conqueror)
nodes.notes: Son of Richard II; fathered William I of England with Herleva of Falaise.

nodes.name: King Harald III Hardrada of Norway (+ Elizabeth of Kiev, r. 1046–1066 CE)
nodes.notes: Married Elizabeth Yaroslavna of Kiev; fell at Stamford Bridge (1066 CE).

nodes.name: Brutus of Troy (Son of Silvius; Legendary Founder of Britain, Geoffrey of Monmouth)
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Aeneas; divided Britain among sons Locrinus, Camber & Albanactus.

nodes.name: King Locrinus of Loegria / England (Eldest Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Camber of Cambria / Wales (Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Albanactus of Alba / Scotland (Youngest Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Leir / Lear of Britain (Father of Goneril, Regan & Cordelia)
nodes.era: c. 8th c. BCE trad. (Geoffrey of Monmouth II.11)
nodes.notes: 8th-gen descendant of Locrinus.

nodes.name: King Beli Mawr ('Beli the Great', Progenitor of Welsh Royal Houses)
nodes.notes: Key ancestral node of British and Welsh dynastic pedigrees.

nodes.name: King Uther Pendragon (Son of Constantine; Father of King Arthur)
nodes.notes: Brother of Aurelius Ambrosius; father of King Arthur.

nodes.name: King Arthur of Britain (+ Queen Guinevere, Geoffrey of Monmouth IX–XI)
nodes.notes: Hero-king of post-Roman Britain.

nodes.name: King Hengist of Kent (Leader of Anglo-Saxon Arrival, c. 449 CE; Bede HE I.15)
nodes.notes: Jutish commander tracing pedigree to Woden.

nodes.name: King Cerdic of Wessex (r. 519–534 CE; Direct Male Ancestor of English Kings)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Egbert, Alfred the Great & the modern British monarchy.

nodes.name: Prince Rurik of Novgorod (r. 862–879 CE; Founder of Rurikid Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Varangian prince invited to rule Novgorod in 862 CE.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Igor' of Kiev (Son of Rurik, r. 912–945 CE)
nodes.role: Son of Rurik & Father of Svyatoslav
nodes.notes: Married St. Olga of Kiev.

nodes.name: Princess St. Olga of Kiev (Regent, 945–960 CE; First Christian Rurikid Sovereign)
nodes.notes: Baptized in Constantinople (957 CE); grandmother of St. Vladimir.

nodes.name: Queen Anne Yaroslavna of Kiev (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of King Henry I of France)
nodes.role: Queen of France Linking Kiev to Capetians
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yaroslav the Wise & Ingegerd of Sweden; ancestral mother of Capetian France & European royalty!

nodes.name: Queen Anastasia Yaroslavna of Hungary (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of Andrew I)
nodes.notes: Mother of King Solomon of Hungary.

nodes.name: Queen Elizabeth Yaroslavna of Norway (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of Harald Hardrada)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yaroslav the Wise who wed Harald Hardrada.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Vsevolod I of Kiev (Son of Yaroslav the Wise; + Byzantine Princess Anastasia Monomachina)
nodes.role: Son of Yaroslav & Father of Vladimir Monomakh
nodes.notes: Married Byzantine imperial princess of the Monomachos house.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Vladimir II Monomakh of Kiev (+ Gytha of Wessex, Dau. of King Harold II, r. 1113–1125)
nodes.notes: Married Princess Gytha of England (daughter of Harold Godwinson!), uniting Kievan Rus', Byzantium & Anglo-Saxon England!

nodes.name: Grand Prince Yuri Dolgoruky ('Long-Arm', Son of Vladimir Monomakh; Founder of Moscow 1147)
nodes.role: Founder of Moscow & Grandfather of Nevsky
nodes.notes: Mentioned in 1147 CE as founder of Moscow; grandfather of St. Alexander Nevsky.

nodes.name: King Eric VI the Victorious of Sweden (r. c. 970–995 CE)
nodes.notes: First historically verified king of unified Sweden; father of Olof Skötkonung.

nodes.name: King Olof Skötkonung of Sweden (r. 995–1022 CE; 1st Christian King)
nodes.notes: Father of Ingegerd of Sweden (+ Yaroslav the Wise) and Anund Jacob.

nodes.name: Princess Ingegerd Olofsdotter (St. Anna of Novgorod; Wife of Yaroslav the Wise)
nodes.role: Grand Princess of Kiev Linking Sweden to France, Hungary & England
nodes.notes: Married Yaroslav the Wise (1019 CE), mothering Anne of Kiev, Anastasia of Hungary, Elizabeth of Norway & Vsevolod I.

nodes.name: Birger Jarl of Bjälbo (Founder of Stockholm, r. 1248–1266 CE)
nodes.role: Bjälbo Regent & Father of Kings Valdemar & Magnus
nodes.notes: Married Ingeborg of Sweden (descendant of Munsö kings); consolidated medieval Sweden.

nodes.name: King Charles IX of Sweden (Son of Gustav I Vasa, r. 1604–1611)
nodes.notes: Father of Gustavus Adolphus.

nodes.name: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden (r. 1611–1632; Lion of the North)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Christina.

nodes.name: Queen Christina of Sweden (r. 1632–1654)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Gustavus Adolphus.

nodes.name: King Charles XII of Sweden (r. 1697–1718)
nodes.notes: Great Northern War commander.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden (b. 1946; Great-Grandson of Queen Victoria via Princess Margaret!)
nodes.notes: Descendant of both Gustav Vasa and Queen Victoria.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden (b. 1977; Future Queen)
nodes.role: Heir Apparent to the Swedish Throne
nodes.notes: Eldest child of King Carl XVI Gustaf.

nodes.name: King Gorm the Old of Denmark (r. c. 936–958 CE; Jelling Stones)
nodes.notes: Father of Harald Bluetooth.

nodes.name: King Harald I Bluetooth of Denmark & Norway (r. c. 958–986 CE; Christianizer)
nodes.notes: Father of Sweyn Forkbeard.

nodes.name: King Sweyn Forkbeard (+ Gunhild/Sigrid of Poland; King of Denmark & England, d. 1014)
nodes.role: Father of Cnut the Great & Estrid
nodes.notes: Fathered Cnut the Great.

nodes.name: King Valdemar I the Great of Denmark (r. 1157–1182; Grandson of Harald & Kiev!)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Estrid Svendsdatter & Yaroslav the Wise via Canute Lavard & Ingeborg of Kiev.

nodes.name: Queen Margaret I of Denmark, Norway & Sweden (Architect of Kalmar Union, 1397)
nodes.notes: Founder of the Kalmar Union.

nodes.name: King Christian IV of Denmark & Norway (r. 1588–1648; Oldenburg)
nodes.role: Brother of Queen Anne (+ James VI & I)
nodes.notes: Uncle of King Charles I of England.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Frederik X of Denmark (b. 1968; Glücksburg Heir of Christian IV & Victoria)
nodes.notes: Acceded in 2024.

nodes.name: Queen Emma of Normandy (Daughter of Richard I; Wife of Ethelred II & Cnut; Mother of Edward the Confessor & Harthacnut)
nodes.role: Twice Queen of England & Normandy Bridge
nodes.notes: Bridged Norman Dukes with Anglo-Saxon and Danish crowns.

nodes.name: Duke Mieszko I of Poland (r. c. 960–992 CE; Baptism of Poland 966)
nodes.notes: Father of Boleslaw I & Gunhild/Sigríðr.

nodes.name: King Boleslaw I the Brave of Poland (r. 992–1025; 1st Crowned King)
nodes.notes: Father of Mieszko II.

nodes.name: King Mieszko II Lambert of Poland (r. 1025–1034)
nodes.notes: Father of Casimir I.

nodes.name: Duke Casimir I the Restorer (+ Maria Dobroniega of Kiev, r. 1039–1058)
nodes.notes: Married Yaroslav the Wise's sister Maria Dobroniega of Kiev.

nodes.name: King Casimir III the Great of Poland (r. 1333–1370; Codifier & University Founder)
nodes.notes: Great lawgiver; sister Elizabeth married Charles I of Hungary -> Louis the Great.

nodes.name: Princess Gunhild / Świętosława of Poland (Daughter of Mieszko I; Mother of Cnut the Great)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Mieszko I who wed Eric the Victorious of Sweden and Sweyn Forkbeard of Denmark.

nodes.name: Princess Maria Dobroniega of Kiev (Daughter of St. Vladimir; Wife of Casimir I)
nodes.role: Sister of Yaroslav & Duchess of Poland
nodes.notes: Daughter of St. Vladimir the Great of Kiev; mother of Boleslaw II & Wladyslaw Herman.

nodes.name: King Mindaugas of Lithuania (r. c. 1236–1263)
nodes.notes: United Baltic Aukštaitija.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania (r. 1316–1341; Founder of Vilnius)
nodes.notes: Father of Algirdas and Kęstutis.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Algirdas (+ Uliana of Tver, r. 1345–1377)
nodes.notes: Wed Rurikid Princess Uliana of Tver.

nodes.name: King Wladyslaw II Jagiello (1386–1434; Victor of Grunwald 1410)
nodes.notes: Wed Queen Jadwiga of Poland, uniting Poland and Lithuania.

nodes.name: King Casimir IV Jagiellon (Son of Jagiello, r. 1447–1492)
nodes.notes: Father of Kings of Poland, Bohemia & Hungary.

nodes.name: King Sigismund I the Old (+ Bona Sforza, r. 1506–1548)
nodes.notes: Son of Casimir IV.

nodes.name: King John III Sobieski of Poland-Lithuania (r. 1674–1696; Relief of Vienna 1683)
nodes.notes: Maternal lineage connected back to Rurikid & Polish nobility.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Vytautas the Great of Lithuania (Son of Kęstutis; Cousin of Jagiello, 1392–1430)
nodes.notes: Daughter Sophia of Lithuania married Grand Prince Vasily I of Moscow.

nodes.name: Queen St. Jadwiga of Poland (Daughter of Louis I of Hungary; Rex Poloniae, 1384–1399)
nodes.notes: Married Grand Duke Jagiello (Wladyslaw II), uniting Poland & Lithuania.

nodes.name: Chieftain Álmos (Father of Árpád, c. 820–895 CE)
nodes.notes: Led Magyars westward.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Árpád of Hungary (r. c. 895–907 CE; Conquest of Carpathian Basin)
nodes.notes: Father of Zoltán.

nodes.name: King St. Stephen I of Hungary (r. 1000–1038 CE; 1st Christian King)
nodes.notes: Great-great-grandson of Árpád; wed Gisela of Bavaria.

nodes.name: King Andrew I of Hungary (+ Anastasia of Kiev, r. 1046–1060)
nodes.notes: Married Anastasia Yaroslavna of Kiev.

nodes.name: King Béla III of Hungary (+ Margaret of France, r. 1172–1196)
nodes.notes: Father of Andrew II.

nodes.name: King Andrew II of Hungary (r. 1205–1235; Golden Bull 1222)
nodes.role: Father of St. Elizabeth & Béla IV
nodes.notes: Issued the Golden Bull of 1222.

nodes.name: King Béla IV of Hungary (Rebuilder after Mongol Invasion, r. 1235–1270)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Charles I & Kunigunda of Bohemia.

nodes.name: King Louis I the Great of Hungary & Poland (Anjou-Capet, r. 1342–1382)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Jadwiga of Poland and Queen Mary of Hungary.

nodes.name: Princess St. Elizabeth of Hungary (Daughter of Andrew II, 1207–1231)
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Andrew II & Gertrude of Merania.

nodes.name: Regent John Hunyadi (Defender of Belgrade 1456, d. 1456)
nodes.notes: Father of King Matthias Corvinus.

nodes.name: King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary (r. 1458–1490; Bibliotheca Corviniana)
nodes.notes: Son of John Hunyadi; famed Renaissance patron.

nodes.name: Duke St. Wenceslas I of Bohemia (Přemyslid Martyr, r. 921–935 CE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of St. Ludmila & Bořivoj I.

nodes.name: King Ottokar II of Bohemia (r. 1253–1278; + Kunigunda of Kiev/Hungary)
nodes.role: Iron and Golden King of Bohemia
nodes.notes: Married Kunigunda (granddaughter of Béla IV & Rostislav of Kiev).

nodes.name: Emperor & King Charles IV of Bohemia (r. 1346–1378; Golden Bull & Charles Univ.)
nodes.notes: Son of Queen Elisabeth of Bohemia (Přemyslid); father of Sigismund & Anne of Bohemia.

nodes.name: Queen Anne of Bohemia (Daughter of Charles IV; Wife of King Richard II of England)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Emperor Charles IV who wed King Richard II.

nodes.name: Princess Bonne of Bohemia (Sister of Charles IV; Wife of King John II of France)
nodes.role: Ancestral Mother of Valois Kings of France
nodes.notes: Mother of Charles V the Wise of France.

nodes.name: Emperor Sigismund of Luxembourg (Son of Charles IV; King of Hungary & Bohemia)
nodes.notes: Daughter Elizabeth of Luxembourg wed Habsburg Albert II.

nodes.name: Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine (Duchess of Aquitaine; Queen of France & England, 1122–1204)
nodes.role: Mother of Richard I, King John & Eleanor of Castile
nodes.notes: Mother of Europe's greatest medieval royal network.

nodes.name: Queen Blanche of Castile (Granddaughter of Eleanor; Mother of King St. Louis IX of France)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Alfonso VIII & Eleanor of England; mother of St. Louis IX.

nodes.name: Queen Juana of Castile & Aragon ('Juana la Loca', Daughter of Ferdinand & Isabella, 1479–1555)
nodes.notes: Married Philip the Handsome; mother of Emperor Charles V & Ferdinand I.

nodes.name: Archduke Philip the Handsome of Burgundy (Son of Emperor Maximilian I; Father of Charles V)
nodes.role: Habsburg Prince & King Consort of Castile
nodes.notes: Son of Maximilian I & Mary of Burgundy.

nodes.name: Queen Catherine of Aragon (Daughter of Ferdinand & Isabella; Mother of Mary I of England)
nodes.role: Spanish Princess & 1st Queen of Henry VIII
nodes.notes: Mother of Queen Mary I.

nodes.name: Emperor Ferdinand I (Son of Philip & Juana; King of Bohemia & Hungary, 1556–1564)
nodes.notes: Brother of Charles V.

nodes.name: Emperor Joseph II (Eldest Son of Maria Theresa, r. 1765–1790)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Empress Maria Theresa.

nodes.name: Emperor Leopold II (Son of Maria Theresa; Father of Emperor Francis II, r. 1790–1792)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Habsburg Emperor Franz Joseph.

nodes.name: Queen Marie Antoinette of France (Daughter of Maria Theresa; Wife of Louis XVI, d. 1793)
nodes.role: Archduchess of Austria & Queen of France
nodes.notes: Daughter of Empress Maria Theresa.

nodes.name: Napoleon II Bonaparte ('L'Aiglon', King of Rome; Son of Napoleon I & Marie Louise, 1811–1832)
nodes.notes: United Bonaparte and Habsburg bloodlines.

nodes.name: Cosimo de' Medici ('Pater Patriae' of Florence, 1389–1464)
nodes.notes: Patron of Renaissance humanism.

nodes.name: Lorenzo de' Medici ('Il Magnifico', 1449–1492; Patron of Leonardo & Michelangelo)
nodes.role: Grandson of Cosimo; Father of Pope Leo X
nodes.notes: Great Renaissance statesman.

nodes.name: Queen Catherine de' Medici (Great-Granddaughter of Lorenzo; Queen of France by Henry II)
nodes.role: Mother of Francis II, Charles IX & Henry III
nodes.notes: Dominant Renaissance queen mother of Valois France.

nodes.name: Queen Marie de' Medici (Granddaughter of Emperor Ferdinand I; Wife of King Henry IV of France)
nodes.role: Mother of Louis XIII & Queen Henrietta Maria
nodes.notes: Mother of Louis XIII and grandmother of Charles II & James II of England.

nodes.name: German Emperor Kaiser Wilhelm I of Prussia (1797–1888)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Frederick William & Hohenzollern electors.

nodes.name: Empress Victoria / Princess Royal (Eldest Daughter of Queen Victoria; Mother of Kaiser Wilhelm II)
nodes.notes: Married Frederick III of Prussia.

nodes.name: German Emperor Frederick III (Son of Wilhelm I; Husband of Victoria, r. 1888)
nodes.role: German Emperor & Father of Wilhelm II
nodes.notes: Father of Kaiser Wilhelm II.

nodes.name: German Emperor Kaiser Wilhelm II (Son of Frederick III & Victoria, r. 1888–1918)
nodes.role: Last German Emperor & Grandson of Queen Victoria
nodes.notes: First cousin of King George V and Tsaritsa Alexandra.

nodes.name: Electress Sophia of Hanover (Granddaughter of King James I; Act of Settlement 1701)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Elizabeth Stuart & Frederick V; mother of King George I.

nodes.name: King Edward VII (Son of Queen Victoria & Prince Albert, r. 1901–1910)
nodes.notes: Married Alexandra of Denmark.

nodes.name: King George V (Son of Edward VII; Renamed House of Windsor 1917, r. 1910–1936)
nodes.notes: Father of Edward VIII & George VI.

nodes.name: King George VI (Son of George V, r. 1936–1952)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Elizabeth II.

nodes.name: Queen Elizabeth II (r. 1952–2022; Longest-Reigning British Monarch)
nodes.role: Queen of the United Kingdom & Commonwealth
nodes.notes: Daughter of George VI; wed Prince Philip of Greece & Denmark.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Charles III of the United Kingdom (b. 1948, r. 2022–present)
nodes.role: Reigning Sovereign of the United Kingdom
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Queen Elizabeth II & Prince Philip.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): William, Prince of Wales (b. 1982; Son of King Charles III & Diana)
nodes.role: Heir Apparent to the British Crown
nodes.notes: Father of Prince George, Princess Charlotte & Prince Louis.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Prince George of Wales (b. 2013; Future Windsor Heir)
nodes.notes: 2nd in line to the British throne.

nodes.name: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg & Gotha (1819–1861; Consort of Queen Victoria)
nodes.role: Father of Nine Royal Children Across Europe
nodes.notes: First cousin and husband of Queen Victoria.

nodes.name: Emperor Paul I of Russia (Son of Peter III & Catherine II, r. 1796–1801)
nodes.notes: Father of Emperors Alexander I & Nicholas I.

nodes.name: Emperor Alexander I of Russia (r. 1801–1825; Defeated Napoleon 1812)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Paul I.

nodes.name: Emperor Alexander II the Liberator (Son of Nicholas I, r. 1855–1881)
nodes.notes: Father of Alexander III; grandfather of Nicholas II.

nodes.name: Emperor Tsar Nicholas II (Son of Alexander III, r. 1894–1917)
nodes.notes: Married Alix of Hesse (Empress Alexandra, granddaughter of Queen Victoria).

nodes.name: Grand Duchess Anastasia Nikolaevna (Daughter of Nicholas II & Alexandra, 1901–1918)
nodes.role: Youngest Daughter of Tsar Nicholas II
